# Phase E2: the N8 pack and one Edio - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for
> tracking.

**Goal:** Everything RetroPlug knows about the Everdrive N8 Pro becomes one workspace package, `packages/n8`, that a
product lists and nothing else names, with the Edio protocol written once, in C++ that builds for the RP2350 as it
builds for the desktop, and wrapped for TypeScript over an RPC facet; the Pico box then runs on that same code and
still does everything it did. The contract between the N8's node and the link that drives its cart becomes a portable
C device ABI in `node-sdk`; the pack starts its desktop service through a provider each product's generated code
calls; the TypeScript clients, the C++ Edio and the Pico's `edio.c` give way to the one Edio; and the box's whole image
links under E1's link trap on the heap, on exceptions and on RTTI, in CI. Every desktop suite is bit-identical, the
two goldens that change on purpose are `[packages]` (`rp.n8.nes` registering from its pack) and the Edio golden (13
cases recorded from the old clients), and nothing is re-recorded.

**Architecture:** Per [modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md), whose section 13 ("As
built") records the build and which Task 5 lands with its status line, sections 1 to 11 corrected in place. Task 1
draws the device ABI (`rp_device.h`, `rp_jobs.h`, `rp_stage.h`, a fixed registry in the engine, the cart and surface
interfaces beside their nodes); Task 2 moves the N8 code into `packages/n8` by `git mv`, splits its portable target
(`retroplug-n8`, `device: true`) from its desktop one (`retroplug-n8-desktop`, the provider and the facet's link
half), and has every product start the pack's provider through a generated header in place of naming an N8 class;
Task 3 writes the one Edio (`Transport`, `Edio`, `Menu`, `Ops`) in the portable target, puts `N8Link`, `N8Host` and
the facet's sessions on it, and swaps the TypeScript clients for `@retroplug/n8`'s wrapper of the facet; Task 4 makes
the Pico box C++ on the pack (`UsbCdcTransport`, a static SOF timer, the trap over the whole image) with
`pnpm device:box` in CI; Task 5 lands the docs.

**Tech stack:** C++20 (desktop GCC 13.3; the devcontainer's `arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1 with newlib and its
libstdc++), C for the device ABI's headers (compiled as C by a test), CMake's `string(JSON)` manifests and a script-mode
reader, rpcpp's QuickJS codec for the facet, the Pico SDK 2.1.1 with TinyUSB 0.18.0 and Pico-PIO-USB at `5a37a66`,
Catch2, the TypeScript mock tier and `test-native`, pnpm workspaces for the new member. No submodule moves. **No
implementer touches the hardware**: the Pico gate and the desktop N8 leg are the controller's, in Task 6.

**Spec:** [modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md). The main design's Phase E outline is
[modular-graph-design.md](modular-graph-design.md) section 8; E1's design, whose package boundary the pack follows, is
[modular-graph-phase-e1-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e1-design.md), and E1's plan, the previous one executed this
way, is [modular-graph-phase-e1-plan.md](modular-graph-phase-e1-plan.md).

**Provenance:** every code block below was built and run before this plan was written, on the scratch branch
`proto/e2-n8` in this worktree, on top of the design commit f9ce365d7: five commits, one per task (Task 6 is the
acceptance run and commits nothing), with GCC 13.3 on linux-x64 (a Ryzen 9 9950X, 32 threads). A block that creates a
file is that file as the prototype commit left it; one that changes it is the prototype's diff for it, so `git apply`
it from the step's text (or apply it hunk by hunk with the Edit tool); a move is a `git mv`, followed by the
prototype's diff of the moved file on its new path when the commit also changes it; a deletion is a `git rm`. Each
code task's verification is the stage's final run of `/tmp/e2pro/tip-verify.sh` after its review's fix pass
(`/tmp/e2pro/s1f-*.log`, `s2f-*.log`, `s3f-*.log`, and `s4g-*.log` for Task 4's second fix pass, whose tree is
`3e839bc00`'s); Task 5 changes docs and four comments in code. Every expected pass, test count and figure is quoted from
the stage reports in /tmp/e2pro, from those logs, from the design's record or from the hardware gate's logs, which is
what the generator checks; a failing step's expected failure is what the missing code produces, as each step says.
When this plan was generated it was replayed in a scratch clone of f9ce365d7, every block written, moved or applied in
order, and each task committed with the command given: each commit's tree came out exactly as the prototype's, and
each commit message as its. The prototype commits, by task:

- Task 1 `3babae072`: the device ABI, links by name and capability jobs as portable C.
- Task 2 `3eb5a7928`: the N8 pack, its provider and the facet's link half.
- Task 3 `5fda0b8b8`: the one Edio, its menu and operations, the facet's sessions and the TS swap.
- Task 4 `3e839bc00`: the box on the N8 pack's Edio, a static SOF timer and the link trap on the whole image.
- Task 5 `236a1d16f`: the docs. Task 6 is the acceptance run and commits nothing.

**Where this plan departs from the design as committed (f9ce365d7).** The design was written before the prototype;
this plan follows what was built, and Task 5 lands the design with section 13's record and sections 1 to 11 corrected
in place. In short:

- **The user's decisions** (`.superpowers/e-pico/decisions.md`, the E2 entries): the pack holds the N8's native code
  whole, its portable target (the Edio, the menu's commands, the operations, `rp.n8.nes`) and its desktop target
  (the serial transport, the link thread, `N8Host`, the cart link, the facet), started through a provider so that no
  product names an N8 class, with the device ABI in `node-sdk` as portable C; C++ owns the protocol and the
  multi-step operations (a ROM boot, a file read or written whole, a listing), shared by the box, `N8Host`'s jobs
  and the CLI's facet, and TypeScript keeps the decoders and the presentation; the box's whole image links under the
  87-symbol trap, with `skip_alarm_pool` and a static SOF timer of its own; `pico/n8-host` stays in place, becomes
  C++ and loses `edio.c`, the box's policy staying in the firmware and `midi.c` staying C. During the build the user
  decided that a moved file's link in a plan doc (`docs/launchpad-plan.md:297`) gets a path-only fix, the record's
  prose never edited, and that every box test boots BlipToaster, never `n8-midi.nes`.
- **The device ABI's shape.** `node-sdk` gains three portable C headers, not two: `rp_device.h`
  (`rp.host.devices/2`, a link acquired by device name and interface id, with a `ctx` and a `release`), `rp_jobs.h`
  and `rp_stage.h` (`rp.stage/1`, moved out of `HostServices.hpp`, the one interface a device node presents rather
  than takes); `DeviceJobSlot` becomes the desktop-only `graph/desktop/DeviceJobSlot.hpp`. The engine's registry is
  a fixed table of 8 entries (a name up to 31 characters, an interface id up to 63), installed through
  `Engine::installDevice` / `clearDevice` and, for a C++ link, `installLink` / `clearLink` (`[[nodiscard]]`; a
  product logs a refusal); `setDeviceLinks`, `HostDevices` and `DeviceLinks.hpp` go. A link pointer identifies one
  installation. The cart's interface is `rp::n8::CartLink` (`n8`, `rp.n8.cart-link/1`) with a fixed 64-word
  `CartNotes` in place of `std::bitset`, and `rp.n8.nes` is renamed from `N8Nodes` to `N8Node`; both stubs, `NoCart`
  and the Launchpad's `NoSurface`, count in 32-bit atomics, which the Cortex-M33 has lock-free.
- **The opaque `rp_job`, and four report entries.** `struct rp_job` is incomplete in every host: the engine's record
  is `rp::host::Job` behind `handle()` and `record()` (an earlier build defined `struct rp_job` as the record
  itself), so a pack's tests keep a record of their own (`packages/n8/native/test/FakeJobs.hpp`). The report
  interface `rp.host.jobs/1` has four entries and no `ctx`: `progress`, `succeed` (copied), `fail` and `abandon`,
  the last for a node leaving the plan, whose completion keeps its "left the plan" words. A node reaches it through
  `get_interface` at bind, and a host that offers none sees the node refuse its jobs. Commit 1's one behaviour
  change is the refusal of a device job whose strings hold a NUL (a C string would carry it cut short); a refusal
  comes back cut at 255 bytes and a `fail()` reason at 1024, never inside a UTF-8 sequence.
- **Providers are an object per instance.** The design's global `rp_start_providers(host)` would have kept provider
  state in statics, and a DAW holds several instances, each with its own engine. The generated header
  (`build/packages/products/<product>/rp_product_providers.hpp`, header-only and inline, never committed) gives
  `rp::Providers rp_start_providers(const rp_device_host*)`, `rp_restore_providers(rp::Providers&)`,
  `rp_stop_providers(rp::Providers&)` and `rp_register_package_rpc<Server>(Server&, const rp::Providers&)`;
  `rp_provider` leads with `abi_version`, a provider is a function returning `const rp_provider*`, and no call of
  the table throws. A product that never includes the header links nothing of the providers, so listing a pack (its
  node types) and starting its provider are separate: the render host, the UI harness, the Node addon and most test
  binaries list `n8` and start nothing. The CLI starts and mounts the providers but never restores them (n8.cfg is
  the UI's persisted link, and restoring it would claim the port the CLI's own sessions open). The test host starts
  the real provider over `FakeN8` (prototype question 1). `RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES` is `core dsp graph-runtime n8
  native`, so `rp.n8.nes` registers after `rp.host.audio-out` in every `[packages]` row, each product's type ids
  unchanged.
- **The facet's link half lands with the pack (Task 2)**, the session half with the Edio (Task 3). `N8Rpc.hpp`
  (header-only in Task 2; `N8Rpc.cpp` in Task 3, with only `registerRpc` a template) replaces `N8Hooks.cpp` and the
  four `__rp_*N8` hooks, and `@retroplug/n8`'s `createN8Client(call)` is the TS side. Its byte strings are
  `rfl::Bytestring`, which the QuickJS codec carries and the JSON one cannot, so the facet's tests mount it on a
  QuickJS server (`QjsRpc.hpp`).
- **`threads` belongs to the link, and `rp.n8.nes` is `device: true`.** The first build had the node declare
  `threads`, which kept a Pico target from planning it and `device: true` from holding. The thread is the desktop
  link's, so the node declares none and relies only on `CartLink::push()` never blocking, never allocating and
  taking no lock; the planner now plans `rp.n8.nes` for a Pico target. `retroplug-n8-device` compiles in the default
  build, and `rp-device-check` links the pack from Task 2 on (`RP_DEVICE_CHECK_PACKAGES` is `core dsp n8`), its host
  offering `rp.host.devices/2` with an acquire that always answers null, so the node runs on its stub. The Launchpad
  nodes still declare `threads` for their link: the exception, until their pack.
- **`chrImage.ts` and `risaSyncTranslator.ts` stay in `packages/retroplug`**: each imports `retroplug` modules (the
  NES tile codec, risa's sync protocol), a cycle if the pack held them. They move within `retroplug`
  (`src/risa/rom/chrImage.ts`, `src/risaSyncTranslator.ts`, their tests to `test/risa/`). The pack's TS tests are
  swept from `packages/*/ts/test` and type-checked by `retroplug`'s tsconfig.
- **The one Edio, as built.** Every call answers a `Status` struct (`Ok`, `Timeout`, `LinkDown`, `BadReply`,
  `Device`, `NotFound`, `Cancelled`, `TooLarge`, with a `Where` and a `Step`), worded by `describe()` as the TS
  client threw it; transports never throw; one timeout table with no sticky timeouts; one write per frame. A short
  write now fails the command, where both old clients ignored the count (the root of the 2026-10-22 mid-command
  bug); the desktop's wire is otherwise the old clients' byte for byte, in fewer `write` calls. The golden's 15
  cases carried no listing, file read, menu command or boot, so 13 more were recorded from the old TS clients at the
  pack commit and appended (28 cases); every one matched the new Edio on the first run. `bootRom`'s battery path is
  a never-inlined helper sized for any FatFs name (789 bytes, used only when a battery is written).
- **The box keeps `bootRom`, with `BootOptions`.** The first box kept the upload outside `bootRom`, which sent one
  extra `*t` before each `*n` and broke the wire's equality with `edio.c`; `BootOptions` (no handshake of
  `bootRom`'s own, and a hook before each step that may use the Edio) lets the box keep `bootRom` and the old wire.
  `Where::MapIndex` lets the box tell a missing map index from a failed install, as `edio.c` could.
- **The alarm-pool wrap.** `skip_alarm_pool` alone left the heap in the image: `pio_usb_host_init` still contains
  the call `alarm_pool_create(2, 1)` behind its `if`, so the firmware links with `--wrap=alarm_pool_create_on_timer`
  and defines the wrapper as a `panic()` that never runs. A remount rebinds the transport only at the main loop's
  top level, and `BOOT_GONE()` checks the link, so a remount inside the probe abandons the boot at once.
- **The 4 KB stack.** The hand sum for the box's deepest chain is a pessimistic 2.3 KB against the SDK's nominal 2
  KB (the old firmware's about 2.0 KB), so `n8_host` sets `PICO_STACK_SIZE=0x1000` (all of SCRATCH_Y) and keeps core
  1's reservation at 2 KB (`PICO_CORE1_STACK_SIZE=0x800`); the linker checks only the reservation.
- **The hardware gate passed on the prototype's image** (sha256 `10a6b09edb99...`, BlipToaster), run by the
  controller: the boot through the menu in 12.2 s from the saved choice, `stress.sh` with no loss and isolated
  latency 587 us average and 1110 us worst (the baseline's 625 / 1089), the A4 and C5 audio control identical to the
  baseline's, `faults.sh --rounds 8` 8 of 8 (the baseline's 7 of 8), and the upload path (two ROMs staged, a SysEx
  `7D 50` pick, about 4.9 s per 294928-byte upload). The final fix pass's image is byte-identical to the gate's, so
  the gate holds for Task 4's tree. **An image carries the day it was built**: the Pico SDK's standard binary info
  stamps it with `__DATE__` (nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, so Task 4 and Task 6 hash each
  image with that one string normalised to the gate's `Nov 4 2026`, after checking exactly one is present; Task 6
  runs the gate again on the executed tree.
- **Smaller departures.** `N8ReliableLink.hpp` moves into the pack (the emulated NES FIFO role includes it from
  there) and `util/FixedQueue.hpp` into `node-sdk`, so the pack depends on `node-sdk` alone;
  `cmake/test-binary.cmake` moves to the root so a pack defines its own test binaries; the manifest reader runs in
  script mode (`cmake/check-manifest.cmake`), and the configure holds four refused manifests to their reasons;
  `cmake/reflectcpp-pin.cmake`, `cmake/device-image.cmake` and `cmake/check-trap.cmake` hold what the two device
  projects share. `tip-verify.sh`'s sanitizer legs had used the tag `[n8]`, which matches nothing, so from Task 2
  the legs name `[n8-node]`, `[n8-adapters]` and `[providers]` and `retroplug-n8-test` has legs of its own. `pnpm
  install --offline` without `--frozen-lockfile` silently pruned 464 lines of `pnpm-lock.yaml` (every other
  platform's esbuild and typescript optional packages), so Task 2 applies the lockfile's two entries as a patch and
  checks them with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`. `writeBattery` is linked into the box and never
  called there.
- **The counts, start to end:** `retroplug-n8-test` from the baseline's 57 cases (529 assertions) to 89 (1220),
  `retroplug-serial-test` 1 / 7 throughout, `retroplug-engine-graph-test` from 313 cases to 330,
  `retroplug-device-mode-test` from 10 cases to 11, `pnpm test` from 1814 cases over 174 files to 1781 over 174
  (Task 2 adds `link-client`; Task 3 adds `session-client` and deletes `edio.test.ts` and `menu-load.test.ts`),
  `test:native` from 167 files to 168 (`n8-session`), and `device:check`'s image from 65156 / 1844 / 412742 (flash /
  data / bss) to 82012 / 2000 / 416402.
- **Owed, not runnable here.** Windows has not built E2 (the pack's targets are ours, so they build under `/W4 /WX`;
  the risks include `DeviceAbi.c` compiled as C by MSVC with `rp_job_error`'s `static __inline`, the
  `__declspec(noinline)` on `writeBattery`, the facet's `rfl::Bytestring` under the QuickJS codec, and shadowing
  MSVC refuses), so a `build.bat` and `test.bat` run is owed. macOS (AppleClang with libc++) and CI's arm64 Linux
  job have not built it either, and the linux job's two new steps (the TinyUSB init with the Pico-PIO-USB fetch, and
  `pnpm device:box`) have run only as the local `env -i` dry run. `build.yml` runs on `workflow_dispatch`, on pull
  requests and on pushes to `main` only, so a push of `feature/modularize` runs nothing: these runs are owed to a
  dispatched run or a PR, which the user (or their Windows agent) starts. Task 6 states them.
- **What no log backs.** No E2 stage ran the Reaper suite, `pnpm validate`, the desktop N8 leg or ASan over
  `retroplug-device-mode-test`, and Task 6's hardware legs run on the executed tree for the first time (the gate's
  figures are the prototype image's, which Task 4's image must equal byte for byte but for its build date; Task 6
  predicts the tip's image equal too, since Task 5 changed one comment line the image compiles). Every gate leg's
  commands are the controller's record (`/tmp/e2pro/gate-commands.txt`), the CH345's port looked up by name in place
  of that boot's `hw:4,0,0`. The red runs (Task 1's missing header, Task 2's golden) and the alarm-pool mutation's
  failure are predicted from the code at each step, with the stage's own wording where a stage ran the same check;
  Task 2's refused manifests are held to the reasons `tests.cmake` itself requires. A few counts are a report's, not
  a log's (`[n8-node]`, `[providers]`, the `[capability]` slices, `pnpm test n8`'s seven files), and a few lines ask
  for the count because none was recorded (the case count of Task 1's slice, Task 6's CI-view parity alone and
  fixture-free `test:ui`, the fresh tree's runs). Task 4's all-options firmware build follows the knobs the stage's
  own scratch build recorded in its cache, at the stage commit before the fix passes. The `env -i` dry run of
  `device:check` and `device:box` was logged at that same commit, whose sizes it reports; the fix passes' plain runs
  give the sizes this plan quotes. No parity baseline, kit golden, render baseline, descriptor golden or
  `buildGraph` golden is re-recorded by any task; the two goldens that change (`[packages]` in Task 2, the Edio
  golden's 13 recorded cases in Task 3) are quoted as diffs.


**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**
- This plan lives at `docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-plan.md` and is committed before Task 1 (a docs commit of its own):
  the header's links are relative to that location; every command and path in the steps is relative to the worktree
  root.
- Commit after each task (the commands are given; Task 6 commits nothing unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit
  of its own). No `Co-Authored-By` or "generated with" trailer. Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context lines of older code and of the specs, which carry
  many): leave those be.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the session
  itself.
- Don't `rm -rf build` to fix CMake; investigate. Never use bare `git stash`, and never switch branches with uncommitted
  work in the tree. Never touch a submodule. `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure (the two tracked
  patches): expected, leave it. `build-device/` and, from Task 4, `build-box/` are scratch build dirs the device
  scripts own and `.gitignore` lists; removing them is fine. `pico/n8-host/build/` is the rig's build dir (ignored by
  `pico/.gitignore`); only Task 4's image step and Task 6 build there.
- The derived files are never committed: the embedded bundle C arrays (`build/native/*bundle_data.c`), the products'
  generated registration sources and, from Task 2, their providers headers (`build/packages/products/`, a
  `<product>/rp_product_providers.hpp` per desktop product, and `build/packages/test/without/` for the test of a
  product that lists none), the device-mode test's `device-entries.cpp` and the device check's `DeviceCheckCases.hpp`
  (`build/device-check/`, or the device build dir's `cases/`).
- **Parity holds the engine's output to the bit, and no task re-records anything.** Never set `RP_PARITY_UPDATE`,
  `RP_KIT_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_RENDER_GOLDEN_UPDATE` or `RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE`: a golden that moves means the step is wrong.
  **Two goldens change on purpose, each as a quoted diff**: Task 2's `[packages]` golden, where `rp.n8.nes` moves under
  the n8 package with every product's type ids unchanged, and Task 3's Edio golden, which moves into the pack and gains
  13 cases the prototype recorded from the old TS clients (the step gives the recording as provenance; nothing here
  re-runs it). **The skip baseline is regenerated once**, in Task 3 (`--update-skip-baseline`, which no other step
  passes), and its diff must be empty.
- **Run no `pnpm install` but Task 2 Step 5's frozen one** (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`). A
  non-frozen install re-resolves the lockfile: offline it silently prunes 464 lines of `pnpm-lock.yaml` (every other
  platform's optional packages). Task 2 applies the lockfile's two new entries as the quoted diff and checks them with
  that frozen install.
- **A move is a `git mv`, never a copy and a delete**, so history follows the file: the step prints the commands, and
  where the commit also changes a moved file its diff follows the move, on the new path. Between a task's moves and
  the step that points its CMake at the new places the tree does not configure; the steps say when to build.
- Every whole-file block below (a `Create`) is followed by the `sed -n` range that extracts it from this plan and by the
  blob hash the file must have: write or extract the file, then `git hash-object <path>` must print the hash the step
  quotes, which is the prototype commit's blob. A retyped slip fails there rather than in a test that never reads the
  line. One new file is executable (`tools/build-box.sh`, Task 4): its step sets the bit.
- Every `check:docs` count below is 81: the stages' logs record 80, and this plan is the 81st tracked Markdown file
  `check-doc-links` walks. `docs/*-plan.md` are records: never edit one but for the path-only link fix Task 2 makes
  (the user's decision).
- The fixture groups need `RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources` on the same command line; without it their
  cases skip. A shell `export` does not survive between commands. `pnpm test:native` takes ONE filter per run (an
  exact slug like `render-baseline`, or a dash-form prefix; `risa-render` runs its three files). The CI views pass
  `RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/nonexistent-rp-resources RISA_SRC=/nonexistent-rp-risa`, because without them the runners
  fall back to `../resources`, which exists beside this worktree and holds some fixtures.
- The Catch2 binaries, `retroplug-render-host-test` and `rp-device-check-cases` are `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL`: `cmake --build
  build` does not relink them, so a library edit needs the target built by name before a run (`pnpm test:plugin`,
  `test:n8` and `test:native` build theirs first). A new or removed source needs `cmake -S . -B build` first. The
  `-device` object libraries, `retroplug-n8-device` among them from Task 2, are in the default build.
- The build trees were last built at the prototype's tip, so each task's first build in a tree re-runs CMake there and
  recompiles what changed; that is expected.
- The sanitizer trees are their own: `build-tsan/` and `build-asan/`. Configure one only if its `CMakeCache.txt` is
  missing (`cmake -S . -B build-tsan -DRETROPLUG_SANITIZE=thread`, or `build-asan` with `=address`); from Task 2, where
  a pack adds its own test binaries, re-run `cmake -S . -B build-tsan` and `cmake -S . -B build-asan` (the cache is
  kept) before the first build there, as the stage did. Build the binary in that tree before running it there; a stale
  prototype binary proves nothing.
- Case counts are exact. A `test cases: N | P passed | S skipped` line, an `All tests passed (A assertions in N test
  cases)` line and a per-file count must match the quoted N/P/S (Catch2 pads the `test cases:` line's columns with
  spaces, which the quotes below collapse to one). Assertion totals are exact for `retroplug-graph-test`,
  `retroplug-audio-test`, `retroplug-device-mode-test`, the launchpad, n8 and serial binaries and the small six.
  **A run that includes `[engine-jobs]`, and so any whole engine-graph run and the sanitizer legs, reports an
  assertion total that moves from run to run** (one render-progress case polls a running render): for those the case
  count must match and the total is the prototype's, quoted for scale. The `[capability]` slices quoted below
  (`[devices],[capability],[n8-adapters]` in Task 1, the five-tag slice in Task 3) hold steady, as the reports found
  running them twice, so their totals are exact.
- The prototype branch `proto/e2-n8` is this plan's provenance, and no step reads it: every byte check is a blob
  hash quoted in the step.
- The device steps need `arm-none-eabi-g++` (13.2.1 here). `pnpm device:check` uses `PICO_SDK_PATH` when it is set
  (this devcontainer sets `/opt/pico-sdk`, an SDK with no submodules, which is all the check needs);
  `pnpm device:box` (Task 4 on) needs the SDK's TinyUSB, so it uses `PICO_SDK_PATH` only when that carries it and
  `/workspaces/pico-sdk` (2.1.1, TinyUSB 0.18.0) otherwise, saying so, and Pico-PIO-USB from `PICO_PIO_USB_PATH` or
  `/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB` (`5a37a66`, never edited). The CI dry runs clone both from GitHub.
- **No implementer touches the hardware.** Never open `/dev/ttyACM*` or `/dev/ttyDbgProbe`, never run
  `pico/n8-host/loop.sh`, `stress.sh` or `faults.sh`, never flash anything, and never touch the NES, the N8, the Pico,
  the Debug Probe, the L6, the video capture card or the power plug: the user's own sessions may be using them. The

### Task 1: the device ABI, links by name and capability jobs as portable C

Design sections 5 and 10's first commit. The N8's node and the link that drives its cart are about to move into a pack
of their own, so the contract between them can no longer be the engine's. `node-sdk` gains three portable C headers
(`rp_device.h`, `rp_jobs.h`, `rp_stage.h`) and the desktop-only `DeviceJobSlot.hpp`; the engine's `DeviceRegistry`
becomes a fixed table of named links behind `Engine::installDevice` and `installLink`, and answers `rp.host.jobs/1`;
the cart's and the surface's interfaces (`rp::n8::CartLink`, `rp::launchpad::SurfaceLink`) sit beside their nodes in
`packages/native/src/n8/` and `src/launchpad/`, where Task 2 moves the first into the pack; and `rp.n8.nes` moves to
`n8/N8Node.cpp`, including only `node-sdk` and its own headers. No behaviour changes but one: the engine refuses a
device job whose strings hold a NUL, which a C request would carry cut short.

The C ABI's test comes first, and fails to build because the headers it compiles as C do not exist yet. The headers,
the interfaces and the node's move follow, then the engine and the links, the products and the retyped tests; the tree
builds again only once all of them are in, so build nothing in Steps 2 to 6.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test of the C ABI**

`DeviceAbi.h` declares, once for C and C++, the layout record and the three functions `DeviceAbi.c` defines: the
headers compiled as C, C's `offsetof` of each struct compared with C++'s, and a C node that binds its link through the
registry and finishes a job through the reports. `DeviceAbi.test.cpp` holds four cases (`[devices]` and
`[capability]`): the layout, the C node's binding and job, `rp.host.jobs/1`'s progress, succeed and fail, and a report
after an abandon reaching nothing. `tests.cmake` adds both sources to the engine-graph binary (the C file builds in
the root project's default C).

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/DeviceAbi.h`:

````cpp
/* What DeviceAbi.c, compiled as C, offers DeviceAbi.test.cpp: one declaration of each, read by both languages, so the
 * layout the two compare cannot drift between them. */
#ifndef RP_TEST_DEVICE_ABI_H
#define RP_TEST_DEVICE_ABI_H

#include <stddef.h>

#include "graph/rp_device.h"
#include "graph/rp_jobs.h"
#include "graph/rp_stage.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Where C puts each field the headers' structs carry, for the C++ side to compare with its own offsetof. */
typedef struct rp_test_c_layout {
    size_t request_size, request_offset, request_length, request_bytes, request_byte_count;
    size_t devices_size, devices_release;
    size_t device_jobs_size, device_jobs_submit;
    size_t host_jobs_size, host_jobs_fail, host_jobs_abandon;
    size_t stage_size, stage_stage;
} rp_test_c_layout;

void rp_test_c_layout_of(rp_test_c_layout* out);
/* A C device node's whole use of the two interfaces: bind the link "n8" names, then finish a job through the host's
 * reports - two progress reports and its three result bytes - and give the link back. Answers what the acquire did. */
void* rp_test_c_bind_and_finish(const rp_host_devices* devices, const rp_host_jobs* reports, rp_job* job);
/* The submit a C node presents: it refuses with its reason in the caller's buffer, cut to fit. */
rp_device_jobs rp_test_c_device_jobs(void);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* RP_TEST_DEVICE_ABI_H */
````

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/DeviceAbi.c`:

````cpp
/* The device ABI compiled as C (graph/rp_device.h, graph/rp_jobs.h, graph/rp_stage.h): what a C node binds a link and
 * finishes a job through, so a header that slips C++ in (a default argument, a reference, a namespace) fails this
 * translation unit rather than a pack's. DeviceAbi.test.cpp calls these and compares what C laid out with C++'s. */

#include "DeviceAbi.h"

#include <stdint.h>

void rp_test_c_layout_of(rp_test_c_layout* out) {
    out->request_size = sizeof(rp_job_request);
    out->request_offset = offsetof(rp_job_request, offset);
    out->request_length = offsetof(rp_job_request, length);
    out->request_bytes = offsetof(rp_job_request, bytes);
    out->request_byte_count = offsetof(rp_job_request, size);
    out->devices_size = sizeof(rp_host_devices);
    out->devices_release = offsetof(rp_host_devices, release);
    out->device_jobs_size = sizeof(rp_device_jobs);
    out->device_jobs_submit = offsetof(rp_device_jobs, submit);
    out->host_jobs_size = sizeof(rp_host_jobs);
    out->host_jobs_fail = offsetof(rp_host_jobs, fail);
    out->host_jobs_abandon = offsetof(rp_host_jobs, abandon);
    out->stage_size = sizeof(rp_host_stage);
    out->stage_stage = offsetof(rp_host_stage, stage);
}

void* rp_test_c_bind_and_finish(const rp_host_devices* devices, const rp_host_jobs* reports, rp_job* job) {
    static const uint8_t kResult[3] = {0xC0, 0xDE, 0x01};
    void* link = devices->acquire(devices->ctx, "n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1");
    reports->progress(job, 1, 3);
    reports->progress(job, 3, 3);
    reports->succeed(job, kResult, sizeof kResult);
    devices->release(devices->ctx, link);
    return link;
}

static bool refuseEveryJob(void* ctx, const rp_job_request* request, rp_job* job, char* error, size_t error_cap) {
    (void)ctx;
    (void)job;
    rp_job_error(error, error_cap, request->op[0] != '\0' ? "a C node has no operation of that name" : "no operation");
    return false;
}

rp_device_jobs rp_test_c_device_jobs(void) {
    rp_device_jobs jobs = {NULL, &refuseEveryJob};
    return jobs;
}
````

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/DeviceAbi.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// The device ABI's C headers (graph/rp_device.h, rp_jobs.h and rp_stage.h, docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md
// section 5): compiled as C by DeviceAbi.c and laid out there as C++ lays them out, a C node's binding and job driven
// through an engine's registry and report interface, and rp.host.jobs/1 itself (the reports a device finishes the
// engine's record through, and DeviceJobSlot's rule that a report after an abandon reaches nothing).
//
// Run via `pnpm test:plugin engine-graph`.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "DeviceAbi.h"
#include "graph/desktop/DeviceJobSlot.hpp"
#include "graph/rp_device.h"
#include "graph/rp_jobs.h"
#include "host/devices/DeviceRegistry.hpp"
#include "host/engine/CapabilityJobs.hpp"

namespace {

using rp::host::Job;
using Bytes = std::vector<std::uint8_t>;

int acquired = 0, released = 0;
void countAcquire(void*) { ++acquired; }
void countRelease(void*) { ++released; }

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("the device ABI compiles as C, and C lays it out as C++ does", "[devices]") {
    rp_test_c_layout c{};
    rp_test_c_layout_of(&c);
    CHECK(c.request_size == sizeof(rp_job_request));
    CHECK(c.request_offset == offsetof(rp_job_request, offset));
    CHECK(c.request_length == offsetof(rp_job_request, length));
    CHECK(c.request_bytes == offsetof(rp_job_request, bytes));
    CHECK(c.request_byte_count == offsetof(rp_job_request, size));
    CHECK(c.devices_size == sizeof(rp_host_devices));
    CHECK(c.devices_release == offsetof(rp_host_devices, release));
    CHECK(c.device_jobs_size == sizeof(rp_device_jobs));
    CHECK(c.device_jobs_submit == offsetof(rp_device_jobs, submit));
    CHECK(c.host_jobs_size == sizeof(rp_host_jobs));
    CHECK(c.host_jobs_fail == offsetof(rp_host_jobs, fail));
    CHECK(c.host_jobs_abandon == offsetof(rp_host_jobs, abandon));
    CHECK(c.stage_size == sizeof(rp_host_stage));
    CHECK(c.stage_stage == offsetof(rp_host_stage, stage));
}

TEST_CASE("a C node binds its link and finishes a job through the engine's registry and reports", "[devices]") {
    acquired = released = 0;
    rp::host::DeviceRegistry registry;
    int                      link = 0;  // the link's identity is all the C side reads of it
    REQUIRE(registry.install("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1", &link, &countAcquire, &countRelease));

    Job job;
    CHECK(rp_test_c_bind_and_finish(registry.api(), rp::host::jobReports(), rp::host::handle(&job)) == &link);
    CHECK(acquired == 1);
    CHECK(released == 1);
    // The record behind the rp_job the C side named, finished as the engine's own: progress overwritten to the last,
    // the result copied, the terminal state last.
    CHECK(job.state.load() == Job::Done);
    CHECK(job.progress.load() == 3);
    CHECK(job.total.load() == 3);
    CHECK(job.result == Bytes{0xC0, 0xDE, 0x01});

    // A C node's refusal comes back in the caller's buffer, NUL-terminated and cut to fit.
    const rp_device_jobs jobs = rp_test_c_device_jobs();
    const rp::host::JobRequest r{"cart", RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE, "dump", "", 0, 0, {}, ""};
    const rp_job_request       request = rp::host::requestView(r);
    char                       error[256] = {};
    Job                        refused;
    CHECK_FALSE(jobs.submit(jobs.ctx, &request, rp::host::handle(&refused), error, sizeof error));
    CHECK(std::string(error) == "a C node has no operation of that name");
    CHECK(refused.state.load() == Job::Queued);  // a refusal leaves the record untouched
    char small[6] = {'x', 'x', 'x', 'x', 'x', 'x'};
    CHECK_FALSE(jobs.submit(jobs.ctx, &request, rp::host::handle(&refused), small, sizeof small));
    CHECK(std::string(small) == "a C n");
    rp_job_error(small, 0, "nothing fits");  // no room: nothing is written
    CHECK(std::string(small) == "a C n");
    rp_job_error(small, sizeof small, nullptr);  // no text: an empty reason
    CHECK(small[0] == '\0');
}

TEST_CASE("rp.host.jobs/1: progress overwrites, succeed copies the result, fail keeps the reason", "[capability]") {
    const rp_host_jobs* reports = rp::host::jobReports();

    Job running;
    reports->progress(rp::host::handle(&running), 10, 100);
    reports->progress(rp::host::handle(&running), 40, 100);
    CHECK(running.progress.load() == 40);  // the latest, not a sum
    CHECK(running.total.load() == 100);
    CHECK_FALSE(running.finished());

    Job done;
    {
        Bytes result{1, 2, 3, 4};
        reports->succeed(rp::host::handle(&done), result.data(), result.size());
        result.assign(4, 0xFF);  // the caller's bytes are its own again the moment the report returns
    }
    CHECK(done.state.load() == Job::Done);
    CHECK(done.result == Bytes{1, 2, 3, 4});
    Job empty;
    reports->succeed(rp::host::handle(&empty), nullptr, 0);
    CHECK(empty.state.load() == Job::Done);
    CHECK(empty.result.empty());

    Job failed;
    {
        std::string reason = "the cart said no";
        reports->fail(rp::host::handle(&failed), reason.c_str());
        reason.assign("overwritten");
    }
    CHECK(failed.state.load() == Job::Failed);
    CHECK(failed.failure.load() == Job::Device);
    CHECK(failed.error == "the cart said no");

    Job abandoned;
    reports->abandon(rp::host::handle(&abandoned));
    CHECK(abandoned.state.load() == Job::Failed);
    CHECK(abandoned.failure.load() == Job::Removed);  // the failure the engine gives a job whose node is gone
    CHECK(abandoned.error.empty());
}

TEST_CASE("a device's report after its node abandoned the job reaches nothing", "[capability]") {
    rp::DeviceJobSlot slot;
    int               owner = 0, other = 0;
    Job               job;
    REQUIRE(slot.claim(rp::host::jobReports(), rp::host::handle(&job), &owner));
    Job second;
    CHECK_FALSE(slot.claim(rp::host::jobReports(), rp::host::handle(&second), &owner));  // one job at a time
    slot.progress(5, 10);
    CHECK(job.progress.load() == 5);

    // Another node leaving the plan touches nothing of this job's.
    slot.abandon(&other);
    CHECK_FALSE(job.finished());
    CHECK_FALSE(slot.abandoned());

    // Its own node leaving fails it at once, and the slot stays busy while the device is still at work.
    slot.abandon(&owner);
    CHECK(job.state.load() == Job::Failed);
    CHECK(job.failure.load() == Job::Removed);
    CHECK(slot.abandoned());
    CHECK(slot.busy());

    // What the device reports from here on reaches no record: the engine may already have freed it.
    slot.progress(9, 10);
    slot.succeed(Bytes{7, 7});
    CHECK(job.progress.load() == 5);
    CHECK(job.result.empty());
    CHECK(job.failure.load() == Job::Removed);
    // The device's finish frees the slot for the next job.
    CHECK_FALSE(slot.busy());
    Job next;
    REQUIRE(slot.claim(rp::host::jobReports(), rp::host::handle(&next), &owner));
    slot.fail("the next one's own reason");
    CHECK(next.error == "the next one's own reason");
    CHECK(next.failure.load() == Job::Device);

    // A claim given back before the job started leaves its record untouched.
    Job unstarted;
    REQUIRE(slot.claim(rp::host::jobReports(), rp::host::handle(&unstarted), &owner));
    slot.unclaim();
    CHECK(unstarted.state.load() == Job::Queued);
    CHECK_FALSE(slot.busy());
}
````

Create `packages/node-sdk/native/src/graph/rp_device.h`:

````cpp
/* rp_device.h - the device links a node binds by name (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 5).
 *
 * A host owns the hardware - the serial port, the MIDI ports, reconnecting, the farewell a device needs - and installs
 * a link for each device under a name and the id of the interface the link implements. A node that drives the device
 * asks for both and is handed the link, or null when the host has none: the interface between the node and its link is
 * the device's own contract (a pack's header, rp::n8::CartLink for the N8's cart), and the host knows nothing of it but
 * its id. Plain C so a C node can bind one; the link it is handed is whatever that interface says it is.
 *
 * Threads: acquire and release are [control]. A node acquires in its activate and releases in its destroy, and both
 * run on the control thread (a plan's reclaim included). A reactivate runs deactivate and activate again on one
 * instance (a sample-rate change, a block growth), so a node that already holds a link keeps it and does not acquire a
 * second: the host forwards each acquire a node makes to the link's own hook, and the balance is the node's to keep.
 * The link outlives every plan whose nodes hold it (a host tears its plans down before it takes its links back), so a
 * node may use it in its destroy, not only give it back.
 *
 * A link pointer identifies one installation: release is handed the pointer alone, so a host installs each link under
 * one name and one interface id, and refuses the same pointer a second time. A device that offers two interfaces (or
 * two versions of one) installs a distinct object for each, never one context struct under two ids. */
#ifndef RP_DEVICE_H
#define RP_DEVICE_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* The host's device links, through rp_host.get_interface (a node takes the interface in bind_host). /2: links by name
 * and interface id, handed out as the interface's own pointer; /1 handed out C++ classes of the engine's, one accessor
 * per device. */
#define RP_HOST_DEVICES_INTERFACE "rp.host.devices/2"
typedef struct rp_host_devices {
    void* ctx;
    /* [control] The link the host installed under `name` with the interface `interface_id`, or null: a name the host
     * has no device for, or a device whose link implements another interface (another version of it included). A
     * node that is answered null runs on a disconnected stub of its own, so a document plans and runs the same in
     * every host. The host forwards the acquire to the link's own hook (a cart link counts the nodes holding it). */
    void* (*acquire)(void* ctx, const char* name, const char* interface_id);
    /* [control] A node is done with a link it acquired here. The link is told only while it is still the one the host
     * installed: a host takes its links back before the objects they wrap go, and a plan freed after that hands its
     * links back to a host that no longer names them, so a release never reaches a freed link. Null is ignored. */
    void (*release)(void* ctx, void* link);
} rp_host_devices;

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* RP_DEVICE_H */
````

Create `packages/node-sdk/native/src/graph/rp_jobs.h`:

````cpp
/* rp_jobs.h - capability jobs a device's node runs (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 5, the job model of
 * docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 6).
 *
 * The control plane asks a node of the running graph to do something to the system behind it - a read, a write, a
 * dump - and the answer comes later. A host keeps a record per job; a device's node is handed the request and the
 * record's opaque handle, takes the job or refuses it at once, and a job it takes is finished through the host's report
 * interface below, from whichever thread runs it (a device's own, for an N8 cart's seconds of USB transfers). Plain C
 * so a C node can present one; the record's internals are the host's alone.
 *
 * Two rules a device's jobs keep, beside whatever bound the host puts on its records:
 *
 *   - One job at a time per device. A device's node refuses a second at submission ("busy: ..."), and one while the
 *     device is not attached ("not connected"), synchronously, before the host keeps a record. A node leaving the plan
 *     abandons its job (rp_host_jobs.abandon), which fails it at once; the device reports into it no more.
 *   - Progress overwrites. A device reports its latest progress into the record, and the host hands a listener the
 *     value it finds when it next looks: a job that reports in a tight loop accumulates nothing. */
#ifndef RP_JOBS_H
#define RP_JOBS_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* The three capabilities a job may name, as the descriptors spell them: a node presents an rp_device_jobs under each it
 * answers, through its get_interface. */
#define RP_SYSTEM_MEMORY_INTERFACE "rp.system.memory/1"
#define RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE "rp.system.sram/1"
#define RP_SYSTEM_ROM_INTERFACE "rp.system.rom/1"

/* What the control plane asks for, valid for the length of the submit call only: a device that needs any of it later
 * (the bytes it uploads, the file name it reaches) copies it. Every string is non-null and NUL-terminated, empty when
 * the request does not carry it; the arguments an operation does not read are ignored. A host refuses a request whose
 * source strings hold a NUL byte rather than build one of these from it: a C string ends there, so the device would
 * read a battery name "a\0b" as "a" and reach another game's file. */
typedef struct rp_job_request {
    const char*    node_id;     /* a node of the host's last published plan */
    const char*    capability;  /* one of the ids above */
    const char*    op;          /* memory: regions, read, write; sram: dump, restore; rom: header, title, upload */
    const char*    region;      /* memory: the region's name */
    const char*    name;        /* rom upload: the file name the image is stored under on the device; sram on a cart:
                                   the ROM file name whose battery file the job reaches */
    uint32_t       offset;      /* memory: where a read or write starts in the region */
    uint32_t       length;      /* memory read, rom header: how many bytes (0: to the end) */
    const uint8_t* bytes;       /* memory write, sram restore, rom upload */
    size_t         size;
} rp_job_request;

/* The host's record of one job, opaque to a node: what a submit is handed and every report names. */
typedef struct rp_job rp_job;

/* What a device's node presents under each capability id it answers. [control] `submit` takes the job into `job` or
 * refuses it, false with a NUL-terminated reason in `error` (at most error_cap bytes, the NUL included): "busy", "not
 * connected", an operation it does not have, arguments it will not take. A refusal leaves the record untouched. A job
 * taken is the device's to finish, through the host's rp_host_jobs: on its own thread, or at once, before submit
 * returns (a read the device's host answers from what it keeps). */
typedef struct rp_device_jobs {
    void* ctx;
    bool (*submit)(void* ctx, const rp_job_request* request, rp_job* job, char* error, size_t error_cap);
} rp_device_jobs;

/* The host's report interface, through rp_host.get_interface: how a device finishes the jobs it takes. A node takes it
 * in bind_host, as it takes rp.host.devices, and hands it with each job to whatever runs the job (its device link); a
 * host that offers none takes no device jobs, and its device nodes refuse every one. There is no ctx: the record is
 * the whole of what a report reaches, so one interface serves every record a host makes.
 *
 * [any thread], one job by one thread at a time: whoever finishes the job reports into it, and nothing touches a
 * record after its terminal report (succeed, fail or abandon), which the host may free from then on. progress may come
 * any number of times before that. */
#define RP_HOST_JOBS_INTERFACE "rp.host.jobs/1"
typedef struct rp_host_jobs {
    /* The progress so far, `done` of `total` (bytes, for a transfer). Overwrites. */
    void (*progress)(rp_job* job, uint32_t done, uint32_t total);
    /* Finish the job with its result: the host copies `size` bytes from `data` (null when size is 0). */
    void (*succeed)(rp_job* job, const uint8_t* data, size_t size);
    /* Finish the job with the reason it failed, which the host copies. */
    void (*fail)(rp_job* job, const char* reason);
    /* [control] The node that submitted the job is leaving the plan: the job fails as its node's removal, the same
     * failure the host gives a job whose node is gone, and the device reports into it no more. */
    void (*abandon)(rp_job* job);
} rp_host_jobs;

/* Write `text` into a submit's error buffer: as much as fits, always NUL-terminated, nothing when there is no room. A
 * cut never ends inside a UTF-8 sequence (the reason crosses the RPC as a string), so it backs up to the start of the
 * code point it would have split. __inline for MSVC's C, whose default dialect has no `inline`. */
#if defined(_MSC_VER) && !defined(__cplusplus)
#define RP_JOBS_INLINE static __inline
#else
#define RP_JOBS_INLINE static inline
#endif
RP_JOBS_INLINE void rp_job_error(char* error, size_t error_cap, const char* text) {
    if (error == NULL || error_cap == 0) return;
    size_t n = 0;
    if (text != NULL)
        while (n + 1 < error_cap && text[n] != '\0') {
            error[n] = text[n];
            ++n;
        }
    if (text != NULL && text[n] != '\0')
        while (n > 0 && ((unsigned char)text[n] & 0xC0u) == 0x80u) --n;
    error[n] = '\0';
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* RP_JOBS_H */
````

````cpp
/* rp_stage.h - a message a host hands a node outside its inputs (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 4).
 *
 * The one interface of the device ABI that a node presents rather than takes: the host asks for it through the node's
 * get_interface. The UI stages a settings message at one node by the document id it gives it, so it reaches the cart
 * whose menu it is whatever the project's musical routing does with channels. The host asks the node the running plan
 * places under that id, so it learns no node's type: a system node hands the message to its core's ingress, a device
 * node to its device. In the SDK rather than an engine header because a device's node presents it and includes nothing
 * of the engine's.
 *
 * [audio] - the call happens on the thread that drains the host's command ring, before the block that follows it, so a
 * staged message lands at frame 0 of the next block. */
#ifndef RP_STAGE_H
#define RP_STAGE_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#define RP_STAGE_INTERFACE "rp.stage/1"
typedef struct rp_host_stage {
    void* ctx;
    /* Hand `size` staged bytes to the node, at frame 0 of the next block, the rate being the block's transport rate a
     * device needs to time a release. False when the node stages nothing (no core yet, or a message its door cannot
     * take), which is what the caller reads as "this node took none". */
    bool (*stage)(void* ctx, const uint8_t* data, size_t size, double sample_rate);
} rp_host_stage;

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* RP_STAGE_H */
````

Create `packages/node-sdk/native/src/graph/desktop/DeviceJobSlot.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The one job a device runs at a time (graph/rp_jobs.h), between the control thread that hands it a record and the
// device's own thread that reports into it. Desktop only: it holds a std::mutex, and a device image has neither the
// threads it serialises nor the lock, so this is the desktop half of the SDK (graph/desktop/), and no device build may
// include it.

#ifdef RP_DEVICE
#error "graph/desktop/DeviceJobSlot.hpp is desktop-only (a std::mutex between a device's thread and the control thread)"
#endif

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "graph/rp_jobs.h"

namespace rp {

// The record is the host's, freed once terminal, and the node that submitted the job can leave the plan while the
// device is still busy (a node removed, a plan torn down), so every touch the device makes goes through here, under a
// lock the control thread shares: once `abandon` has failed the record, the device's later reports reach nothing, and
// the record may be freed without waiting for the device to finish. The lock is held for a report, never across device
// I/O, and never by the block thread. Every report goes through the host's rp.host.jobs/1, which the node submitting
// the job hands over with it.
class DeviceJobSlot {
public:
    // [control] Take the slot for `job`, submitted by the node `owner`, reporting through `reports`; false while
    // another job holds it.
    bool claim(const rp_host_jobs* reports, rp_job* job, const void* owner) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        if (busy_) return false;
        busy_ = true;
        reports_ = reports;
        job_ = job;
        owner_ = owner;
        abandoned_.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        return true;
    }
    // [control] Give back a claim whose job never started (the device would not take it after all), the record
    // untouched.
    void unclaim() {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        clear();
    }
    // [device] The progress so far: overwrites, as graph/rp_jobs.h says.
    void progress(std::uint32_t done, std::uint32_t total) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        if (!job_) return;
        reports_->progress(job_, done, total);
    }
    // [device] Finish the job with its result (the host copies it), or with the reason it failed, and free the slot for
    // the next. The terminal report is the record's last touch.
    void succeed(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& bytes) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        if (job_) reports_->succeed(job_, bytes.data(), bytes.size());
        clear();
    }
    void fail(const std::string& error) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        if (job_) reports_->fail(job_, error.c_str());
        clear();
    }
    // [control] The node `owner` is leaving the plan: a job it holds the slot for fails now (its node's removal), and
    // the device reports into its record no more. The slot stays busy until the device finishes (succeed or fail),
    // since the device is still busy; abandoned() tells it to stop at the next point that leaves the device coherent.
    void abandon(const void* owner) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        if (!busy_ || owner_ != owner) return;
        abandoned_.store(true, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        if (!job_) return;
        reports_->abandon(job_);
        job_ = nullptr;
    }
    // [any] Whether a job holds the slot (taken, not yet finished), and whether its node abandoned it.
    bool busy() const {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        return busy_;
    }
    bool abandoned() const { return abandoned_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }

private:
    void clear() {
        busy_ = false;
        reports_ = nullptr;
        job_ = nullptr;
        owner_ = nullptr;
    }

    mutable std::mutex  mutex_;
    bool                busy_ = false;
    const rp_host_jobs* reports_ = nullptr;
    rp_job*             job_ = nullptr;  // null once finished or abandoned: the device touches it no more
    const void*         owner_ = nullptr;
    std::atomic<bool>   abandoned_{false};
};

}  // namespace rp
````

`n8/CartLink.hpp` is `rp::n8::CartLink` (`kDeviceName` `"n8"`, `rp.n8.cart-link/1`): no string, vector or bitset

Create `packages/native/src/n8/CartLink.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The cart's device link (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 5): the interface between rp.n8.nes and
// whoever drives a real cart, which a host installs under the device name "n8" with the interface id
// "rp.n8.cart-link/1" (rp.host.devices/2, graph/rp_device.h). The engine knows nothing of it but that id: the node and
// the link that drives the cart are the pack's own, and this is their contract. The host owns the device - the serial
// port, reconnecting, the pause a job's transfer needs - and a link is the whole of what a node may do with it: the
// streaming ring, the connected state, the expansion-audio register and the capability jobs it runs on its own thread.
//
// Portable, so the node builds for the device as it does for the desktop: no std::string, std::vector or std::bitset,
// no RTTI, and a protected non-virtual destructor (a link is never deleted through this interface, and a virtual one
// makes the deleting destructor reach operator delete).
//
// The link outlives every plan whose nodes hold it: a host tears its plans down while its links are alive, and a
// reactivate keeps the link across it. So a node may use it in destroy, not only give it back: a job it cancels, the
// notes a cart still holds that it hands over, a connected() or dropped() it reads.

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "graph/rp_jobs.h"

namespace rp::n8 {

// What the node asks for, and what a host installs its cart link as.
inline constexpr const char* kDeviceName        = "n8";
inline constexpr const char* kCartLinkInterface = "rp.n8.cart-link/1";

// The notes a cart holds, one bit a note: channel * 128 + note, 16 channels of 128 (what rp.n8.nes keeps its books in,
// and what it hands its link when it leaves the plan holding some). A fixed array of words, so it is the same type on
// the device, where std::bitset's out-of-range checks would throw.
class CartNotes {
public:
    static constexpr std::size_t kNotes = 16 * 128;

    static constexpr std::size_t size() { return kNotes; }
    // The note `i` (below size(); one past it is ignored or answers false).
    void set(std::size_t i) {
        if (i < kNotes) words_[i / 32] |= bit(i);
    }
    void reset(std::size_t i) {
        if (i < kNotes) words_[i / 32] &= ~bit(i);
    }
    bool test(std::size_t i) const { return i < kNotes && (words_[i / 32] & bit(i)) != 0; }
    bool any() const {
        for (std::uint32_t w : words_)
            if (w != 0) return true;
        return false;
    }
    bool none() const { return !any(); }
    bool operator==(const CartNotes&) const = default;

private:
    static constexpr std::uint32_t bit(std::size_t i) { return std::uint32_t{1} << (i % 32); }

    std::uint32_t words_[kNotes / 32] = {};
};

// A cart in a real console (rp.n8.nes): the same inputs an emulated NES takes, pushed at the cart's FIFO.
class CartLink {
public:
    // [audio] Hand one message to the device at its intra-block `frame`, a sample offset `sampleRate` turns into the
    // moment the link releases it at. Lock-free, never allocates, never blocks; `flush` is the bytes port's barrier
    // flag, which the cart needs no separate byte for. False when any of the bytes were lost (the device is detached, a
    // job holds it, or its ring was full), which is the answer a node keeps its own books on; dropped() is the same
    // losses as a count.
    virtual bool push(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, bool flush,
                      double sampleRate) = 0;
    // [any] Whether the device is attached. Plain state, read afresh: a link may come up or go away between two reads.
    virtual bool connected() const = 0;
    // [any] The pushes that lost their bytes: the device was detached, a job held it, or its ring was full. An adapter
    // counts its own, so a caller reads the pushes it made that went nowhere even while another path pushes at the same
    // device.
    virtual std::uint64_t dropped() const = 0;
    // [audio, any thread] The cart's expansion-audio master-volume register: 0..255, or -1 to leave the register to
    // the cart (N8Host::EXP_VOL_AUTO: unity for a mapper that carries the sound chip, otherwise whatever the device's
    // own menu set). The link keeps the value and a live one reaches the device through its own serial thread at that
    // thread's next turn, so a node's param may call this from the block (no lock, no allocation, no std::function on
    // the caller's side), and every connect re-applies the value.
    virtual void setExpansionVolume(int value) = 0;
    // [control] Run a capability job on the device (graph/rp_jobs.h, docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 6):
    // the node that presents rp.system.sram/1 or rp.system.rom/1 hands each job it is asked for here, with the host's
    // report interface and itself as `owner`. True when the device took it into `job` (it finishes it through
    // `reports`, on its own thread or at once); false with the reason in `error` (graph/rp_jobs.h's rp_job_error),
    // leaving `job` untouched: one job at a time per device ("busy: ..."), and none while the device is not attached
    // ("not connected"), which is all a link with no device ever answers. While a job runs the link reads disconnected
    // and drops (and counts) what is pushed, and the job completes once streaming has resumed.
    virtual bool submitJob(const rp_job_request& request, rp_job* job, const rp_host_jobs* reports, const void* owner,
                           char* error, std::size_t errorCap) {
        (void)request;
        (void)job;
        (void)reports;
        (void)owner;
        rp_job_error(error, errorCap, "not connected");
        return false;
    }
    // [control] The node `owner` is leaving the plan: a job it submitted that is still running fails now (its node's
    // removal) and the device reports into its record no more, stopping at the next point that leaves the device
    // coherent. Nothing when it holds no job.
    virtual void abandonJobs(const void* owner) { (void)owner; }
    // [control] The node is leaving the plan while the cart holds `notes` (it pushed their note-ons and no note-offs):
    // the device sends each a note-off from its own thread, after every byte pushed before this call, so no console is
    // left holding a tone no node will ever release. The node's destroy calls it, on the control thread after the plan
    // swap, where it may not push itself: the audio thread (and the node taking over) may still be pushing. A link with
    // no device, or one not streaming, drops them; nothing a node does depends on whether they went.
    virtual void releaseNotes(const CartNotes& notes) { (void)notes; }

    // There is deliberately no error string here: why a cart would not open is the host UI's (it reads N8Host's
    // lastError through Settings > N8), not something a document's node can act on. Nor an acquire or a release: a
    // host installs the link with hooks of its own for those (rp.host.devices/2), which the cart adapter uses to count
    // the nodes holding it and put the expansion volume back to AUTO on the last release.

protected:
    ~CartLink() = default;
};

// What rp.n8.nes runs on when the host answers its acquire with null (a host that owns no cart, as the CLI, the Node
// addon, the render host and the UI harness are): never connected, taking every push nowhere and counting it (a node
// keeps its own books on push()'s answer), an expansion volume it has nowhere to send, and every job refused "not
// connected" (CartLink's own answer). The node's own member, so a document plans and runs the same in every host.
class NoCart final : public CartLink {
public:
    bool push(std::uint32_t, const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t size, bool, double) override {
        if (size != 0) dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        return size == 0;
    }
    bool          connected() const override { return false; }
    std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return dropped_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }
    void          setExpansionVolume(int) override {}

private:
    // 32 bits, where the interface answers 64: a 64-bit atomic is a library call on the RP2350's Cortex-M33 (no
    // doubleword exclusives), and nothing reads a stub's count but the node that owns it, which keeps its own books.
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> dropped_{0};
};

}  // namespace rp::n8
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The control surface's device link (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 5): the interface between the
// rp.launchpad.surface-in / -out nodes and whoever drives the Launchpad, which a host installs under the device name
// "launchpad" with the interface id "rp.launchpad.surface-link/1" (rp.host.devices/2, graph/rp_device.h). Beside the
// surface's nodes in packages/native until the Launchpad has a pack of its own; the engine knows nothing of it but that
// id. The host owns the device - the MIDI ports, pairing them, the farewell the device needs before a host lets it go -
// and a link is the whole of what a node may do with it: the device's own MIDI in both directions, kept out of the
// musical stream, and its connected state.
//
// As rp::n8::CartLink: no RTTI, a protected non-virtual destructor, and a link that outlives every plan whose nodes
// hold it, so a node may use it in its destroy.

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

namespace rp::launchpad {

// What the nodes ask for, and what a host installs its surface link as.
inline constexpr const char* kDeviceName           = "launchpad";
inline constexpr const char* kSurfaceLinkInterface = "rp.launchpad.surface-link/1";

// The widest message one link carries in either direction: a bulk LED SysEx at its worst (the Pro MK3's 106 RGB colour
// specifications at five bytes each, plus the 8-byte frame, is 538). The device's own replies are far shorter; one
// bound serves both ways, and a message past it is dropped and counted, never truncated into something the other end
// would misread.
inline constexpr std::size_t kMaxDeviceMessage = 560;

// One message in storage the caller owns: a drain copies into the node's own array, so nothing the block thread drops
// is freed there. Also the slot a device link's own receive ring holds (LaunchpadLink's). There is no arrival frame:
// the device's traffic is not timed against the block, so a surface node places what it drains at frame 0.
struct DeviceMessage {
    std::uint16_t size                     = 0;
    std::uint8_t  data[kMaxDeviceMessage] = {};
};

// A control surface (rp.launchpad.surface-in / -out).
class SurfaceLink {
public:
    // [audio] Copy the messages the device sent since the last drain into `out` and answer how many: min(available,
    // capacity), and fewer only when nothing is left, so a caller draining in batches can stop on a short answer.
    // It allocates and frees nothing: both ends keep every message in a fixed slot of their own, and one the caller
    // has no room for stays queued rather than being dropped or freed here.
    virtual std::size_t drainInput(DeviceMessage* out, std::size_t capacity) = 0;
    // [audio] Queue one message for the device (an LED frame, a mode change). Lock-free, never blocks; drops (and
    // counts in dropped()) when nothing is connected, the message is wider than kMaxDeviceMessage, or the ring is full.
    virtual void pushOutput(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) = 0;
    // [any] Whether the device is attached.
    virtual bool connected() const = 0;
    // [any] The pushes that lost their bytes: the device was detached, or its send ring was full. As CartLink's, the
    // count is the link's own, so it covers what any path pushing at the same device lost. A real surface link answers
    // the pushes it lost while attached and the paint sent while nothing was connected (LaunchpadLink's
    // messagesDropped and messagesDetached), so a node reads one number for what the device never got; a message the
    // device sent that its receive ring had no room for is counted apart (messagesInboundDropped), and this does not
    // answer it.
    virtual std::uint64_t dropped() const = 0;

protected:
    ~SurfaceLink() = default;
};

// What the surface nodes run on when the host answers their acquire with null (every host but the standalone): nothing
// queued, nothing received, and every push counted as dropped (a node reads that count as its device's drop). Each
// node's own member, so a document plans and runs the same in every host.
class NoSurface final : public SurfaceLink {
public:
    std::size_t   drainInput(DeviceMessage*, std::size_t) override { return 0; }
    void          pushOutput(const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t size) override {
        if (size != 0) dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    bool          connected() const override { return false; }
    std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return dropped_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }

private:
    // 32 bits, as NoCart's: a 64-bit atomic is a library call on the RP2350's Cortex-M33, and nothing reads a stub's
    // count but the node that owns it. Not for the device yet, but a Launchpad pack inherits this stub.
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> dropped_{0};
};

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

- [ ] **Step 4: The engine's registry and its job reports**

`DeviceRegistry` is a fixed table of 8 `{name[32], interfaceId[64], link, acquire, release}` entries, copied in; it
refuses a null link, an empty or overlong name or id, a duplicate and a full table, clears by link, and
identity-checks a release, so one after a clear reaches nothing; `rp::host::linkHooks<Interface, Link>()` answers the
hooks for a C++ link. `Engine::setDeviceLinks` goes for `installDevice` / `clearDevice` and `installLink` /
`clearLink` (`[[nodiscard]]`). `CapabilityJobs.hpp` keeps the record as `rp::host::Job` behind `handle()` and
`record()`, builds the C request (`requestView`) and answers `jobReports()`; `submitDeviceJob` refuses a NUL-holding
field and cuts a refusal at 255 bytes, never inside a UTF-8 sequence. `HostServices.hpp` includes the two node-sdk
headers in place of the structs it held.

- [ ] **Step 5: The links and the products on the new interfaces**

`N8CartLink`, `LaunchpadSurfaceLink` and `HarnessSurfaceLink` implement the new interfaces; `N8CartLink` keeps
`acquire()` and `release()` as plain members, which `installLink` finds, and converts `CartNotes` to `N8Link`'s own
bitset. `N8Host::submitCartJob` takes the C request, views its bytes and copies them once, into the step that keeps
them, and answers through `rp_host_jobs`. The Launchpad nodes include no engine header. The SDL standalone, the plugin
and the test host install their links with `installLink` and say on stderr when one is refused; the CLI and the Node
addon installed nothing and still install nothing.

- [ ] **Step 6: The retyped tests and their helper**

`TestDevices.hpp` installs fakes through the registry (`installCart`, `installSurface`, `installOn`, each a
`REQUIRE`), with `kCartPushBytes` (560) as a fake's slot size. The device, capability, n8-node, n8-adapter, launchpad
and n8 cases move to the new interfaces; `Devices.test.cpp` gains the registry's table, a clear and a release after
it, a full table and the other refusals; `N8Node.test.cpp` gains the expansion range held to `rp.mesen.nes`'s
(`STATIC_REQUIRE`), the engine's NUL refusal, a host with no job reports, and a refusal cut to its buffer.
`N8CartJobs.test.cpp`'s plain-name loop drops its `"a\0b"` entry, whose check moved to the engine (2 assertions fewer
there).

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/TestDevices.hpp`:

````cpp

// surface link under "launchpad" as an rp::launchpad::SurfaceLink, with the fake's own acquire() and release() as the
// hooks when it counts them (rp::host::linkHooks). On an Engine (Engine::installLink) or on a rig's own registry, each
// install required to succeed; and taking them back (Engine::clearLink).

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "host/devices/DeviceRegistry.hpp"
#include "host/engine/Engine.hpp"

#include "n8/CartLink.hpp"

namespace rp::host::test {

// The widest push a test's fake cart records, in a slot of its own: a cart message has no bound of the link's, and the
// widest a case pushes is a SysEx far below this.
inline constexpr std::size_t kCartPushBytes = 560;

template <class Link>
void installCart(Engine& e, Link& link) {
    REQUIRE(e.installLink<rp::n8::CartLink>(rp::n8::kDeviceName, rp::n8::kCartLinkInterface, link));
}
template <class Link>
void installSurface(Engine& e, Link& link) {
    REQUIRE(e.installLink<rp::launchpad::SurfaceLink>(rp::launchpad::kDeviceName,
                                                      rp::launchpad::kSurfaceLinkInterface, link));
}
template <class Link>
void clearCart(Engine& e, Link& link) {
    e.clearLink<rp::n8::CartLink>(link);
}
template <class Link>
void clearSurface(Engine& e, Link& link) {
    e.clearLink<rp::launchpad::SurfaceLink>(link);
}

// The same on a registry a rig keeps itself (NodeRig, ProtocolNodes.test.cpp's), with the hooks Engine::installLink
// would give.
template <class Interface, class Link>
void installOn(DeviceRegistry& registry, const char* name, const char* interfaceId, Link& link) {
    const LinkHooks hooks = linkHooks<Interface, Link>();
    REQUIRE(registry.install(name, interfaceId, static_cast<Interface*>(&link), hooks.acquire, hooks.release));
}

}  // namespace rp::host::test
````
