````diff
+namespace {
+
+// A link of no interface at all, for the registry's own cases: it counts what the registry forwards to it.
+struct CountedLink {
+    int acquires = 0;
+    int releases = 0;
+};
+void countAcquire(void* link) { ++static_cast<CountedLink*>(link)->acquires; }
+void countRelease(void* link) { ++static_cast<CountedLink*>(link)->releases; }
+
+}  // namespace
+
+TEST_CASE("the registry hands a link out by its name and interface id, and tells its hooks", "[devices]") {
+    DeviceRegistry registry;
+    CountedLink    cart, surface;
+    REQUIRE(registry.install("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1", &cart, &countAcquire, &countRelease));
+    REQUIRE(registry.install("launchpad", "rp.launchpad.surface-link/1", &surface));  // no hooks: nothing forwarded
+    CHECK(registry.size() == 2);
+
+    // Through the C struct a node reads, as an Engine hands it out.
+    const rp_host_devices* api = registry.api();
+    CHECK(api->acquire(api->ctx, "n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1") == &cart);
+    CHECK(cart.acquires == 1);
+    CHECK(api->acquire(api->ctx, "launchpad", "rp.launchpad.surface-link/1") == &surface);
+    CHECK(surface.acquires == 0);
+
+    // The name alone is not enough, nor the id alone: either wrong answers null, and no hook hears of it.
+    CHECK(api->acquire(api->ctx, "n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/2") == nullptr);
+    CHECK(api->acquire(api->ctx, "n8", "rp.launchpad.surface-link/1") == nullptr);
+    CHECK(api->acquire(api->ctx, "nes", "rp.n8.cart-link/1") == nullptr);
+    CHECK(api->acquire(api->ctx, nullptr, "rp.n8.cart-link/1") == nullptr);
+    CHECK(api->acquire(api->ctx, "n8", nullptr) == nullptr);
+    CHECK(cart.acquires == 1);
+
+    // Each acquire is forwarded, a second node's included, and each release reaches the link it names.
+    CHECK(api->acquire(api->ctx, "n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1") == &cart);
+    CHECK(cart.acquires == 2);
+    api->release(api->ctx, &cart);
+    api->release(api->ctx, &cart);
+    CHECK(cart.releases == 2);
+    api->release(api->ctx, &surface);  // installed with no hook: nothing to tell
+    api->release(api->ctx, nullptr);   // a node that was answered null hands back nothing
+    CHECK(surface.releases == 0);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a link cleared from the registry is handed out no more, and a release after the clear reaches nothing",
+          "[devices]") {
+    DeviceRegistry registry;
+    CountedLink    cart, other;
+    REQUIRE(registry.install("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1", &cart, &countAcquire, &countRelease));
+    REQUIRE(registry.acquire("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1") == &cart);
+
+    // A link the registry does not hold clears nothing; the installed one goes.
+    registry.clear(&other);
+    registry.clear(nullptr);
+    CHECK(registry.size() == 1);
+    registry.clear(&cart);
+    CHECK(registry.size() == 0);
+
+    // The node that still holds it hands it back to a registry that no longer names it: the link hears nothing, so a
+    // host may free it once cleared.
+    registry.release(&cart);
+    CHECK(cart.releases == 0);
+    CHECK(registry.acquire("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1") == nullptr);
+    CHECK(cart.acquires == 1);
+
+    // The name is free again: another link may take it, and only that one is reached from then on.
+    REQUIRE(registry.install("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1", &other, &countAcquire, &countRelease));
+    CHECK(registry.acquire("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1") == &other);
+    registry.release(&cart);
+    registry.release(&other);
+    CHECK(cart.releases == 0);
+    CHECK(other.releases == 1);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("the registry refuses a full table, a link or a name installed twice, and a name it has no room for",
+          "[devices]") {
+    DeviceRegistry registry;
+    std::array<CountedLink, DeviceRegistry::kMaxLinks + 1> links{};
+    std::array<std::string, DeviceRegistry::kMaxLinks + 1> names;
+    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < DeviceRegistry::kMaxLinks; ++i) {
+        names[i] = "device-" + std::to_string(i);
+        REQUIRE(registry.install(names[i].c_str(), "rp.test.link/1", &links[i]));
+    }
+    CHECK(registry.size() == DeviceRegistry::kMaxLinks);
+    // Full: the next is refused, and every installed one still answers.
+    names.back() = "device-last";
+    CHECK_FALSE(registry.install(names.back().c_str(), "rp.test.link/1", &links.back()));
+    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < DeviceRegistry::kMaxLinks; ++i)
+        CHECK(registry.acquire(names[i].c_str(), "rp.test.link/1") == &links[i]);
+    CHECK(registry.acquire("device-last", "rp.test.link/1") == nullptr);
+    // A clear makes room for exactly one more.
+    registry.clear(&links[3]);
+    CHECK(registry.install("device-last", "rp.test.link/1", &links.back()));
+    CHECK(registry.acquire("device-last", "rp.test.link/1") == &links.back());
+    CHECK(registry.size() == DeviceRegistry::kMaxLinks);
+
+    DeviceRegistry fresh;
+    CountedLink    a, b;
+    REQUIRE(fresh.install("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1", &a));
+    // The same name and id twice, or the same link under another name: a host clears before it installs again.
+    CHECK_FALSE(fresh.install("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1", &b));
+    CHECK_FALSE(fresh.install("n8-b", "rp.n8.cart-link/1", &a));
+    // The same name under another interface id is another entry, for another link object: a link pointer identifies one
+    // installation (release is handed the pointer alone), so a device that offers two interfaces installs two objects.
+    CHECK(fresh.install("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/2", &b));
+    CHECK(fresh.acquire("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/1") == &a);
+    CHECK(fresh.acquire("n8", "rp.n8.cart-link/2") == &b);
+    // No link, no name, and a name or id past what an entry keeps.
+    CountedLink c;
+    CHECK_FALSE(fresh.install("other", "rp.test.link/1", nullptr));
+    CHECK_FALSE(fresh.install("", "rp.test.link/1", &c));
+    CHECK_FALSE(fresh.install(nullptr, "rp.test.link/1", &c));
+    CHECK_FALSE(fresh.install("other", "", &c));
+    const std::string longName(DeviceRegistry::kMaxName + 1, 'x');
+    const std::string longId(DeviceRegistry::kMaxInterfaceId + 1, 'x');
+    CHECK_FALSE(fresh.install(longName.c_str(), "rp.test.link/1", &c));
+    CHECK_FALSE(fresh.install("other", longId.c_str(), &c));
+    // At the bound exactly, both fit.
+    const std::string maxName(DeviceRegistry::kMaxName, 'x');
+    const std::string maxId(DeviceRegistry::kMaxInterfaceId, 'x');
+    CHECK(fresh.install(maxName.c_str(), maxId.c_str(), &c));
+    CHECK(fresh.acquire(maxName.c_str(), maxId.c_str()) == &c);
+}

+TEST_CASE("rp.n8.nes refuses every job in a host that offers no job reports, before its link is asked",
+          "[engine-graph][n8-node]") {
+    FakeCart cart;
+    NodeRig  rig(kRate);
+    rig.offerJobReports = false;
+    rig.installCart(cart);
+    REQUIRE(rig.set(fanOut(rig)).ok);
+    block(rig);
+
+    rp_node* node = rig.host->node("cart");
+    REQUIRE(node != nullptr);
+    const auto* jobs = static_cast<const rp_device_jobs*>(node->vt->get_interface(node, RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE));
+    REQUIRE(jobs != nullptr);
+    const JobRequest     r       = request(RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE, "dump");
+    const rp_job_request request = rp::host::requestView(r);
+    Job                  job;
+    char                 error[256] = {};
+    CHECK_FALSE(jobs->submit(jobs->ctx, &request, rp::host::handle(&job), error, sizeof error));
+    CHECK(std::string(error) == "this host takes no device jobs");
+    CHECK(job.state.load() == Job::Queued);  // the record untouched

+TEST_CASE("a device's refusal comes back through Engine::submitJob cut to its buffer, never inside a UTF-8 sequence",
+          "[engine-graph][n8-node]") {
+    FakeCart               cart;
+    Engine                 e(kRate);
+    rp::host::test::Roms   roms;
+    std::vector<DocSystem> systems{{1, rp::host::test::kNesType}};
+    withRoms(e, systems, roms);
+    rp::host::test::installCart(e, cart);
+    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(cartDocument(systems)).ok);
+    block(e);
+    static_assert(Engine::kDeviceJobErrorBytes == 256);
+
+    // Past the buffer: the reason arrives cut to its 255 bytes, the NUL the 256th.
+    cart.refusal = std::string(300, 'z');
+    const auto plain = e.submitJob(request(RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE, "dump"));
+    CHECK(plain.id == 0);
+    CHECK(plain.error == std::string(255, 'z'));
+
+    // A two-byte code point across the cut (its lead byte the 255th): the cut backs up to before it, so what crosses
+    // the RPC is still a string.
+    cart.refusal = std::string(254, 'x') + "\xC3\xA9" + "tail";
+    const auto split = e.submitJob(request(RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE, "dump"));
+    CHECK(split.id == 0);
+    CHECK(split.error == std::string(254, 'x'));
+    // One that fits whole is kept whole.
+    cart.refusal = std::string(253, 'x') + "\xC3\xA9";
+    CHECK(e.submitJob(request(RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE, "dump")).error == cart.refusal);
+}
````

````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(node-sdk): the device ABI, links by name and capability jobs as portable C

The N8's node and the link that drives its cart are about to move into a pack of their own, so the contract between
them can no longer be the engine's. node-sdk gains three portable C headers: graph/rp_device.h, rp.host.devices/2 (a
link acquired by device name and interface id, null when the host has none); graph/rp_jobs.h (the three capability
ids, rp_job_request of C strings and a byte span, the opaque rp_job, a device node's rp_device_jobs, and the engine's
report interface rp.host.jobs/1: progress, succeed copying, fail, and abandon for the node's removal); and
graph/rp_stage.h, rp.stage/1, which a device node presents. A node reaches the reports through get_interface at bind,
as it reaches the devices, and hands them with each job to its link. DeviceJobSlot becomes the desktop-only
graph/desktop/DeviceJobSlot.hpp, which refuses a device build, and reports through that interface.

The engine's DeviceRegistry is a fixed table of eight {name, interface id, link, acquire, release} entries, installed
and cleared through Engine::installDevice / clearDevice (installLink / clearLink for a C++ link, both nodiscard, and a
product says when one is refused); setDeviceLinks goes. rp_job stays incomplete: the engine's record is rp::host::Job
behind two casts (handle, record), so any host, a test's fake one included, keeps a record of its own. submitJob
refuses a request whose strings hold a NUL, which a C request would carry cut short, and a refusal's reason comes
back cut at 255 bytes, never inside a UTF-8 sequence.

The cart's interface is rp::n8::CartLink (n8/CartLink.hpp, "n8", rp.n8.cart-link/1), portable (a fixed CartNotes in
place of std::bitset, the job hook over the C request and an error buffer, a protected non-virtual destructor), with
NoCart the node's own stub; the surface's is rp::launchpad::SurfaceLink (launchpad/SurfaceLink.hpp) with NoSurface,
both stubs counting in 32 bits, which the RP2350 has lock-free. rp.n8.nes moves to n8/N8Node.cpp, includes only
node-sdk and n8 headers, and keeps the expansion-volume range as its own constants, which a test holds to
rp.mesen.nes's. N8Host views a job's bytes and copies them once, into the step that keeps them.

Tests: every device, capability, n8-node, n8-adapter, launchpad and n8 case retyped; new cases for the registry's
table, the headers compiled as C (DeviceAbi.c, one declaration shared with C++ in DeviceAbi.h) and laid out as C++
lays them out, a C node's binding and job, rp.host.jobs/1 with a report after an abandon reaching nothing, rp.n8.nes
in a host with no job reports, and a refusal's cut through Engine::submitJob. No behaviour change otherwise.
EOF
````

### Task 2: the N8 pack, its provider and the facet's link half

Design sections 3, 6 and 7 and section 10's second commit. Everything RetroPlug knows about the Everdrive N8 Pro on the
native side moves into one workspace package, `packages/n8` (`@retroplug/n8`), by `git mv`, as the template a
flash-cart pack follows. Its manifest has two native entries: the portable `retroplug-n8` (`rp_n8_package`,
`device: true`: `rp.n8.nes`, `CartLink.hpp` and the node's stub, on `node-sdk` alone) and the desktop
`retroplug-n8-desktop` (the C++ Edio, `N8Link`, `N8Host`, `N8Menu`, `N8CartLink` and `WjwwoodSerialPort`, moved as they
are, plus the provider and the facet's link half). A product starts the pack's device service through a provider its
generated header calls, so the SDL standalone, the plugin and the CLI name no N8 class; `N8Hooks` and the four
`__rp_*N8` hooks go for the facet. `rp.n8.nes` declares no `threads` (the thread is the link's), so its entry is
`device: true` and `rp-device-check` links it. `RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES` lists `n8` after the carved packages, so the
`[packages]` golden moves `rp.n8.nes` after `rp.host.audio-out` in every row, each product's type ids unchanged.

The golden comes first: its diff is the order the new package list registers in, and the Task 1 binary, which still
registers `rp.n8.nes` from `packages/native`, fails it. The moves follow, then the moved files' changes, the provider
mechanism, the pack's own files, the engine and the products, the device check, the tests and the UI; the tree
configures again only once the CMake of Steps 4 to 7 is in, so build nothing between Step 2 and Step 10.

25 files move. `packages/native/src/n8/` (Task 1's `CartLink.hpp` and `N8Node`) becomes the pack's portable
`packages/n8/native/src/n8/`; `packages/native/src/host/n8/`'s Edio, link, host, menu, cart link and serial port
become its desktop `n8/desktop/`; `transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp`, which `N8Link` and the emulated NES FIFO role both
speak, moves with them, keeping its include path; the eight files of `packages/native/test/n8/` become the pack's
`native/test/`; `util/FixedQueue.hpp`, which the reliable link needs, joins `node-sdk`, so the pack depends on

own test binaries. `packages/native/src/host/n8/SerialRpcService.*` stays: it is the CLI's raw serial facet, not the

- [ ] **Step 3: The moved files' changes**

Mostly include paths (`host/n8/...` is `n8/desktop/...`) and comments that named a hook or a path that moved.
`N8Node.cpp` drops `threads` and its `<iterator>` include (which made libstdc++ pull `<string>`, `<stdexcept>` and
`<exception>` into a device build; only `std::size` was used, which `<string_view>` declares), and `CartLink.hpp` says
why the node needs only a push that never blocks. The pack's tests run their jobs into a fake job host of their own
(Step 8's `FakeJobs.hpp`) in place of the engine's `CapabilityJobs.hpp`. `test-binary.cmake` resolves a caller's
sources against the calling directory.

````diff
diff --git a/cmake/test-binary.cmake b/cmake/test-binary.cmake

+# There are fourteen of them (eleven run by `pnpm test:plugin`, two by `pnpm test:n8` and the
 # hardware-only `retroplug-n8-hwtest`), and each was spelled out in full: the same
 # EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL, the same C++20 pair, the same output directory, the same Catch2 link.
 # Nine tenths of each block was boilerplate, which buried the one or two lines that were
@@ -21,8 +21,10 @@

 # retroplug-n8-hwtest is the one, a manual harness driven against real hardware.
 #
-# Sources are interpreted relative to packages/native/ (CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR at the point
-# this is included), matching how they were written before.
+# Shared by packages/native (cmake/tests.cmake) and the packs (packages/n8/native), so the root
+# CMakeLists includes it before the first retroplug_package(). Relative sources resolve against the

+# each caller writes its paths from its own tree.

     cmake_parse_arguments(T "NO_CATCH2" "NAME" "SOURCES;LIBS;INCLUDES;DEFS;PACKAGES" ${ARGN})
````

- [ ] **Step 4: Providers in `node-sdk`, and the manifest's provider and rpc fields**

`graph/rp_provider.h` (desktop-only C, an `#error` under `RP_DEVICE`) is `rp_device_host` and `rp_provider`, the
latter leading with `abi_version` (`RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION` 1), with `rp_provider_fn`, a function returning `const
rp_provider*`, and the rule that no call of the table throws. `graph/desktop/Providers.hpp` is `rp::Providers`, the
providers one product instance started: created in table order and restored in order, stopped in reverse (idempotent,
and in its destructor), move-only, refusing and logging an ABI mismatch, and destroying what it had started when a
create or its own `push_back` throws. `cmake/packages.cmake`'s manifest reader becomes its own function
(`_retroplug_read_manifest`), so `cmake/check-manifest.cmake` can run it in script mode; `_retroplug_read_provider`
reads `provider` and `rpc`, refuses either on a `device: true` entry and an `rpc` with no provider, requires `device`
on an entry with a provider, and `retroplug_product()` writes each desktop product's
`build/packages/products/<product>/rp_product_providers.hpp` (a device product gets none). The four scratch manifests
are what the configure must refuse (Step 11 shows each).

Create `packages/node-sdk/native/src/graph/rp_provider.h`:

````cpp
/* rp_provider.h - how a product starts a pack's device service without naming it (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md
 * section 6).
 *
 * A pack that owns hardware on the desktop (the N8's serial link, its persisted state, the cart link its node binds)
 * names a provider in its manifest: an entry of its desktop target with a `provider` (the C function returning this
 * table) and, when it has a facet, an `rpc` (the header and the function that mount it). cmake/packages.cmake generates
 * each product's rp_start_providers, rp_restore_providers, rp_stop_providers and rp_register_package_rpc from its
 * packages' manifests, so a product starts, restores, stops and mounts every provider it carries in one place and names
 * no class of any of them.
 *
 * Desktop only: a provider owns threads, ports and files, and a device image has none of those to give it (the Pico's
 * box drives its hardware itself until E3 makes it a graph host). Plain C, as the rest of the device ABI is, so a
 * provider in another language, or a downloaded pack's, can be one.
 *
 * Threads: every call here is [control]. A provider's device threads are its own; what it hands the engine goes
 * through rp_device_host's install and clear, whose rules are rp_device.h's. */
#ifndef RP_PROVIDER_H
#define RP_PROVIDER_H

#ifdef RP_DEVICE
#error "graph/rp_provider.h is desktop-only: a device image runs no provider"
#endif

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#define RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION 1u

/* What the product hands a provider to create it with: the engine's device registry and where persisted state lives.
 * The host and its strings outlive the provider (a product stops its providers before it destroys the engine). */
typedef struct rp_device_host {
    uint32_t    abi_version; /* RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION */
    void*       ctx;
    const char* config_dir;  /* where a provider keeps its persisted state (the N8's n8.cfg) */
    /* Install `link` under `name` with the interface `interface_id` (rp_device.h): a node asking for both is handed
     * `link`, and its acquire and release reach the hooks (null for none). False when the registry refuses it (a full
     * table, the name and id or the link taken, a name or id too long): the node then runs on its own stub. */
    bool (*install)(void* ctx, const char* name, const char* interface_id, void* link, void (*acquire)(void* link),
                    void (*release)(void* link));
    /* Take `link` back: a node's later release of it reaches nothing. The provider clears what it installed before it
     * frees the link. */
    void (*clear)(void* ctx, void* link);
} rp_device_host;

typedef struct rp_provider {
    /* RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION, first so that it reads the same in every layout: a host refuses a provider built
     * against another one (rp::Providers says so on stderr and carries on without it), as a provider refuses a host
     * whose rp_device_host is of another version. */
    uint32_t    abi_version;
    const char* id; /* the provider's name in a log line ("n8") */
    /* [control] After the engine, before the control plane can publish a graph. Returns the provider's state, or null
     * when it could not start (the product carries on without it, and its facet is not mounted). No call of this
     * table throws: a C++ provider catches what its own code throws and answers null, or logs and carries on. */
    void* (*create)(const rp_device_host* host);
    /* [control] Bring the persisted state back (reconnect a link left enabled), where the product restores its own. */
    void (*restore)(void* self);
    /* What the pack's rpc registration mounts (the `register` its manifest names is handed it), or null for none. */
    void* (*rpc_service)(void* self);
    /* [control] After the product's plans are reclaimed: clear what it installed and free everything. The plans come
     * first because a node holds the link it acquired and may use it in its destroy (rp_device.h): clearing the link
     * makes a later lookup answer null, but frees nothing a node already holds. */
    void (*destroy)(void* self);
} rp_provider;

/* A manifest's `provider` names a function of this type, as an `entry` names one returning an rp_package. */
typedef const rp_provider* (*rp_provider_fn)(void);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* RP_PROVIDER_H */
````

Create `packages/node-sdk/native/src/graph/desktop/Providers.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The providers one product instance started (graph/rp_provider.h), in the order its packages list them. The generated
// rp_start_providers (build/packages/products/<product>/rp_product_providers.hpp, cmake/packages.cmake) makes one from
// the product's table; the product keeps it beside its engine, restores it where it restores its own state, and stops
// it after its plans are reclaimed. One per instance, not one per process: a DAW holds several plugin instances, each
// with its own engine, and each starts its own providers into its own engine's registry.

#ifdef RP_DEVICE
#error "graph/desktop/Providers.hpp is desktop-only: a device image runs no provider"
#endif

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdio>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "graph/rp_provider.h"

namespace rp {

class Providers {
public:
    Providers() = default;
    // Creates each provider of `table` in order. One built against another ABI version is refused, and one whose create
    // answers null is left out, both said on stderr: the product carries on without it, its links never installed and
    // its facet never mounted (service() answers null). A throw, which the table's calls are not to make, stops what
    // was started before it goes on: the providers created so far are destroyed, the one whose record could not be
    // kept included, so none is left running with its links installed in an engine no Providers stops.
    Providers(const rp_provider_fn* table, std::size_t count, const rp_device_host* host) {
        try {
            started_.reserve(count);
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) start(i, table[i](), host);
        } catch (...) {
            stop();
            throw;
        }
    }
    Providers(const Providers&) = delete;
    Providers& operator=(const Providers&) = delete;
    Providers(Providers&& other) noexcept : started_(std::exchange(other.started_, {})) {}
    Providers& operator=(Providers&& other) noexcept {
        if (this != &other) {
            stop();
            started_ = std::exchange(other.started_, {});
        }
        return *this;
    }
    ~Providers() { stop(); }

    // Each started provider's persisted state back, in order.
    void restore() {
        for (const Started& s : started_)
            if (s.self && s.provider->restore) s.provider->restore(s.self);
    }
    // Destroys each started provider in the reverse of the order they were created, so one created later (which may
    // build on an earlier one's links) goes first. Idempotent: the destructor stops what was not stopped.
    void stop() {
        while (!started_.empty()) {
            const Started s = started_.back();
            started_.pop_back();
            if (s.self) s.provider->destroy(s.self);
        }
    }
    // What the `index`th provider of the table hands its pack's rpc registration, or null (it did not start, it has no
    // facet, or the providers were stopped).
    void* service(std::size_t index) const {
        if (index >= started_.size()) return nullptr;
        const Started& s = started_[index];
        return s.self && s.provider->rpc_service ? s.provider->rpc_service(s.self) : nullptr;
    }
    std::size_t size() const { return started_.size(); }

private:
    // The `index`th provider of the table. Of a refused one only the version is read: what follows it is laid out as
    // that provider's ABI says, so even its id is named by its place in the table.
    void start(std::size_t index, const rp_provider* provider, const rp_device_host* host) {
        void* self = nullptr;
        if (provider && provider->abi_version != RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION) {
            std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] provider %zu is of provider ABI %u, and this host of %u: not started\n",
                         index, static_cast<unsigned>(provider->abi_version), RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION);
            provider = nullptr;
        } else {
            self = provider ? provider->create(host) : nullptr;
            if (!self)
                std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the %s provider did not start\n", provider ? provider->id : "?");
        }
        try {
            started_.push_back({provider, self});
        } catch (...) {
            if (self) provider->destroy(self);
            throw;
        }
    }

    struct Started {
        const rp_provider* provider = nullptr;
        void*              self = nullptr;
    };
    std::vector<Started> started_;
};

}  // namespace rp
````

````cmake
# cmake -DRP_MANIFEST=<package.json> -P cmake/check-manifest.cmake: reads one manifest as retroplug_package() reads a
# package's (cmake/packages.cmake's _retroplug_read_manifest), in script mode, and fails as the configure would. The
# configure runs it over the scratch manifests a configure must refuse (packages/native/test/packages/refused, held by
# packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake), so a rule that stopped firing fails the configure rather than going unnoticed.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.19)
if(NOT RP_MANIFEST)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "check-manifest.cmake: pass -DRP_MANIFEST=<package.json>")
endif()
include("${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/packages.cmake")
_retroplug_read_manifest(scratch "${RP_MANIFEST}")
message(STATUS "check-manifest.cmake: ${RP_MANIFEST} reads")
````

````diff
+# retroplug_providers_header(<file> <label> <package>...): generates <file>, the providers of the packages listed
+# (graph/rp_provider.h) as rp_start_providers(host), rp_restore_providers(providers), rp_stop_providers(providers) and
+# rp_register_package_rpc<Server>(server, providers), in the order the packages and their manifests list them
+# (stopped in the reverse). retroplug_product() writes one per desktop product, rp_product_providers.hpp in an include
+# directory of its own; a test writes one for a list of its choosing. Header-only and inline on purpose: a binary that
+# never includes it (the render host, a test that starts no provider) names no provider, and a static library's members
+# are linked only where something names them, so it carries none of the providers' code, threads or ports. Whether a
+# product starts its providers is therefore its sources' word (whether they include the header), not CMake's. The
+# providers' state is an rp::Providers the product holds per instance (a DAW holds several), not a static here.
+function(retroplug_providers_header file label)
+    set(_providers "")
+    foreach(_p IN LISTS ARGN)
+        get_property(_pp GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_${_p}_PROVIDERS)
+        list(APPEND _providers ${_pp})

+    set(_registers "")

+        get_property(_r GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PROVIDER_${_v}_REGISTER)
+        string(APPEND _decls "extern \"C\" const rp_provider* ${_v}(void);\n")
+        string(APPEND _table "        &${_v},\n")
+        if(_r)
+            string(APPEND _includes "#include \"${_h}\"\n")
+            string(APPEND _registers "    ${_r}(server, providers.service(${_i}));\n")
+        endif()
+        math(EXPR _i "${_i} + 1")
+    endforeach()
+    list(LENGTH _providers _n)

+        set(_start "    (void)host;\n    return {};\n")
+        set(_registers "    (void)server;\n    (void)providers;\n")
+    else()
+        set(_start "    static const rp_provider_fn kProviders[] = {\n${_table}    };\n")
+        string(APPEND _start "    return rp::Providers(kProviders, ${_n}, host);\n")
+    endif()
+    if(NOT _registers)
+        set(_registers "    (void)server;\n    (void)providers;\n")
+    endif()

+//

+// product starts them after its engine and before its control plane can publish a graph, restores them where it
+// restores its own state, mounts their facets where it mounts its own, and stops them after it has reclaimed its plans.
+//

+// include directory of that product's targets alone, so each binary reads the header made for its own packages.
+#pragma once
+
+#include \"graph/desktop/Providers.hpp\"
+${_includes}
+${_decls}

+${_start}}
+
+// [control] Each provider's persisted state back (a link left enabled reconnects), in order.
+inline void rp_restore_providers(rp::Providers& providers) { providers.restore(); }
+
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The pack's manifest, its CMake, its provider and the facet's link half**

`packages/n8/package.json` names the two entries; `packages/n8/native/CMakeLists.txt` defines `retroplug-n8` (public
`node-sdk` alone), `retroplug-n8-desktop` (public `retroplug-n8` and `node-sdk`, private `serial` and `Threads`; no
packages/native target, no QuickJS, no rpcpp) and the pack's three test binaries under their old names, and returns
before its desktop half in a device build. `N8Provider` owns the serial port factory and lister, the `N8Host`
(n8.cfg's format and path unchanged) and the `N8CartLink`, installed as `n8` / `rp.n8.cart-link/1`;
`createProvider(host, factory, lister)` is the seam a test drives. `N8Rpc.hpp` is the facet's link half
(`n8LinkConfig`, `n8SetPort`, `n8Connect`, `n8SetLookahead`), header-only, so the product's server instantiates it and
the pack keeps rpcpp out. `ts/index.ts` is `createN8Client(call)`, the link half's TypeScript side.
`packages/retroplug` depends on `@retroplug/n8` as `workspace:*`, and the lockfile gains the member and the link: its
diff is applied as it stands, never regenerated (a plain `pnpm install --offline` prunes 464 lines here), and checked
by a frozen install.

````cmake
# The Everdrive N8 Pro pack (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 3): rp.n8.nes, the cart as a node, and the
# link interface it drives the cart through (n8/CartLink.hpp), with the desktop's half beside it: the Edio protocol, the
# serial thread that streams to the cart, the host that owns the link and runs the cart's jobs, and the serial port
# (n8/desktop/). BlipToaster's reliable link (transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp) is the pack's as well: N8Link speaks it to
# the cart, and the emulated NES FIFO role in packages/native speaks it from the cart's side. Added by
# retroplug_package(n8) (cmake/packages.cmake). Like any pack, it depends on node-sdk alone; nothing here links a
# packages/native target.

# --- retroplug-n8: the rp_n8_package entry, rp.n8.nes (src/n8/N8Node.cpp). The node reaches the cart only through the
# rp::n8::CartLink a host binds by name (rp.host.devices/2), so it holds no serial port, no thread and no protocol. A
# `device` entry: the desktop build compiles it as a device does too (retroplug-n8-device), and the device check
# (packages/graph-runtime/device-check) links it into the RP2350 image under the link trap.
retroplug_package_library(retroplug-n8
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/n8/N8Node.cpp)
target_include_directories(retroplug-n8 PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)
target_link_libraries(retroplug-n8 PUBLIC retroplug-node-sdk)

# The device build (RP_DEVICE_BUILD, cmake/packages.cmake) stops here: the desktop's half below is a serial port and a
# thread, which a device has neither of, and its manifest entry is not `device`.
if(RP_DEVICE_BUILD)
    return()
endif()

# Threads: N8Link's serial thread. Found here as well as in packages/native, as an imported target is visible only in
# the directory that finds it and below.
find_package(Threads REQUIRED)

# --- retroplug-n8-desktop: the cart's desktop link (src/n8/desktop/): Edio, the krikzz protocol over an ISerialPort;
# N8Link, the serial thread streaming MIDI to the cart's FIFO; N8Host, which owns that link, its config and n8.cfg, and
# runs the cart's capability jobs one at a time (graph/desktop/DeviceJobSlot.hpp); N8Menu, the on-device menu's
# commands a ROM job drives; WjwwoodSerialPort, the ISerialPort over deps/serial. N8CartLink.hpp, the rp::n8::CartLink
# over an N8Host that a host hands rp.n8.nes, is a header. No entry of its own: its manifest entry names the provider
# (rp_n8_provider, N8Provider.cpp: the N8Host, the cart link installed as `n8`, the facet's service) and the facet
# (N8Rpc.hpp, header-only, so the pack itself needs neither rpcpp nor QuickJS: a product's server instantiates it). A
# product starts the provider through its generated rp_start_providers (cmake/packages.cmake) and names nothing here;
# one that never does (the render host, most tests) pulls none of this library's objects in.
retroplug_package_library(retroplug-n8-desktop
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/n8/desktop/Edio.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/n8/desktop/N8Link.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/n8/desktop/N8Host.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/n8/desktop/N8Menu.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/n8/desktop/N8Provider.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/n8/desktop/WjwwoodSerialPort.cpp)
target_link_libraries(retroplug-n8-desktop
    PUBLIC  retroplug-n8           # n8/CartLink.hpp, which N8CartLink.hpp implements, and the include root
            retroplug-node-sdk     # graph/desktop/DeviceJobSlot.hpp, transport/SpscRing.hpp (N8Link's rings), jobs
    PRIVATE serial                 # wjwwood/serial, behind WjwwoodSerialPort.cpp alone (cmake/serial.cmake)
            Threads::Threads)      # N8Link's serial thread

# --- the pack's test binaries (cmake/test-binary.cmake), built by name; sources resolve against this directory.

# Guards the Everdrive N8 Pro protocol framing (Edio): that fifoWR emits the exact krikzz CMD_MEM_WR byte stream to
# ADDR_FIFO and the connect handshake accepts / rejects the 0xA5 status word; plus the N8Link forward path (the SDL
# standalone's realtime serial thread) and the cart's capability jobs (SRAM dump and restore, the ROM upload and its
# boot), which pause and resume streaming around the transfer; and the provider and the facet over them. Drives those
# against a capturing FakeSerialPort - no serial port is opened, no `rtmidi`, no hardware - and runs the jobs into a
# record of its own (test/FakeJobs.hpp), so like the pack's libraries it reaches nothing of packages/native. The CLI's
# risa-sync translation lives in TS (packages/retroplug src/n8, `pnpm test n8`); the C++ Edio/N8Link/N8Menu twin backs
# the realtime + job paths. Run by `pnpm test:n8`.
retroplug_add_test_binary(
    NAME     retroplug-n8-test
    SOURCES  test/Edio.test.cpp
             test/N8Host.test.cpp
             test/N8CartLink.test.cpp      # the cart device link over N8Link + N8Host
             test/N8CartJobs.test.cpp      # the cart's capability jobs, run with streaming paused
             test/N8Provider.test.cpp      # the provider and the facet's link methods, over a JSON server
    LIBS     retroplug-n8-desktop                      # Edio, N8Link, N8Host, N8Menu, the provider; the job ABI
             reflectcpp::reflectcpp                    # rfl::json - parse the shared Edio golden (twins edio.test.ts)
             rpcpp                                     # the server the facet is mounted on (JSON codec)
    # The shared Edio framing golden both this and edio.test.ts assert against (single source, no drift).
    DEFS     EDIO_GOLDEN_PATH="${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/retroplug/test/n8/edio-golden.json")

# WjwwoodSerialPort against a pseudo-terminal: that a read's timeout does not leak into the next write (the bug
# that left a real N8 mid-command behind N8Link's 0 ms back-channel polls). The one N8 test that opens a real serial
# port, so it is its own binary - retroplug-n8-test stays on fakes. Run by `pnpm test:n8`.
retroplug_add_test_binary(
    NAME     retroplug-serial-test
    SOURCES  test/WjwwoodSerialPort.test.cpp
    LIBS     retroplug-n8-desktop)                     # WjwwoodSerialPort, over deps/serial

# A manual hardware harness (NOT CI) that drives the real N8 card's jobs through the same native
# N8Host the cart's node hands them to, over a real /dev/ttyACM0 (the real WjwwoodSerialPort +
# `serial`). Brings its own main(), hence NO_CATCH2.
# Build by name: cmake --build build --target retroplug-n8-hwtest.
retroplug_add_test_binary(
    NAME     retroplug-n8-hwtest
    NO_CATCH2
    SOURCES  test/n8-sd-hwtest.cpp                     # its jobs run into test/FakeJobs.hpp's record
    LIBS     retroplug-n8-desktop)
# `timing` times against an ALSA capture of the console's audio, so it exists only where ALSA does. Linking
# ALSA::ALSA unconditionally failed the GENERATE step on macOS/Windows - EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL does not spare a target
# from resolving its link libraries.
find_package(ALSA)
if(ALSA_FOUND)
    target_sources(retroplug-n8-hwtest PRIVATE test/n8-timing.cpp)
    target_link_libraries(retroplug-n8-hwtest PRIVATE ALSA::ALSA)
    target_compile_definitions(retroplug-n8-hwtest PRIVATE RP_N8_TIMING=1)
endif()
````

````cpp
#include "n8/desktop/N8Provider.hpp"

#include <cstdio>
#include <exception>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "n8/CartLink.hpp"
#include "n8/desktop/N8CartLink.hpp"
#include "n8/desktop/N8Rpc.hpp"
#include "n8/desktop/WjwwoodSerialPort.hpp"

namespace rp::n8 {
namespace {

// Everything the provider owns, in the order it is built and the reverse of the order it goes: the host and the
// config dir it was handed (copied, so the provider never reads the product's strings after create), the N8Host, the
// cart link over it and the facet over it. The cart link is cleared from the registry before any of them is freed, so
// a lookup after the stop finds nothing: an acquire answers null, and the node that asks runs on its stub. That does
// not make it safe to stop the provider under a plan, as a node holds the link it acquired and may use it in its
// destroy (n8/CartLink.hpp): a product reclaims its plans before it stops its providers (graph/rp_provider.h).
struct Provider {
    Provider(const rp_device_host& given, retroplug::N8Link::PortFactory factory, retroplug::N8Host::PortLister lister)
        : host(given),
          configDir(given.config_dir ? given.config_dir : ""),
          n8(std::move(factory), std::move(lister), configDir),
          cart(n8),
          rpc(n8) {
        host.config_dir = configDir.c_str();
        // A refusal (a full table, the name taken) leaves rp.n8.nes on its stub, so it is said, not swallowed.
        installed = host.install && host.install(host.ctx, kDeviceName, kCartLinkInterface,
                                                 static_cast<CartLink*>(&cart), &acquireCart, &releaseCart);
        if (!installed) std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the N8 cart link was not installed\n");
    }
    ~Provider() {
        if (installed && host.clear) host.clear(host.ctx, static_cast<CartLink*>(&cart));
    }
    Provider(const Provider&) = delete;
    Provider& operator=(const Provider&) = delete;

    // The registry's hooks: a node's acquire and release reach the cart link, which counts the nodes holding it.
    static retroplug::N8CartLink& cartOf(void* link) {
        return static_cast<retroplug::N8CartLink&>(*static_cast<CartLink*>(link));
    }
    static void acquireCart(void* link) { cartOf(link).acquire(); }
    static void releaseCart(void* link) { cartOf(link).release(); }

    rp_device_host         host;
    std::string            configDir;
    retroplug::N8Host      n8;
    retroplug::N8CartLink  cart;
    N8Rpc                  rpc;
    bool                   installed = false;
};

Provider& providerOf(void* self) { return *static_cast<Provider*>(self); }

// The table's entries throw nothing (graph/rp_provider.h): a create that throws (an allocation, n8.cfg's directory)
// answers null and says why, and a restore that throws says why and leaves the link down.
void* createWithSerial(const rp_device_host* host) noexcept {
    try {
        return createProvider(
            host, [](const std::string& port) -> std::unique_ptr<retroplug::ISerialPort> {
                return std::make_unique<retroplug::WjwwoodSerialPort>(port);
            },
            [] {
                std::vector<retroplug::N8PortDto> ports;
                for (const auto& p : retroplug::listSerialPorts()) ports.push_back({p.port, p.isN8});
                return ports;
            });
    } catch (...) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the N8 provider did not start\n");
        return nullptr;
    }
}

// Load n8.cfg and reconnect the link if it was left enabled.
void restore(void* self) noexcept {
    try {
        retroplug::N8Host& n8 = providerOf(self).n8;
        n8.restore();
        if (const auto c = n8.getConfig(); c.enabled)
            std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] N8 restore: port '%s'%s\n", c.selectedPort.c_str(),
                         c.connected ? "" : " - not connected");
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] N8 restore failed: %s\n", e.what());
    } catch (...) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] N8 restore failed\n");
    }
}

void* rpcService(void* self) noexcept { return &providerOf(self).rpc; }

void destroy(void* self) noexcept { delete static_cast<Provider*>(self); }

}  // namespace

void* createProvider(const rp_device_host* host, retroplug::N8Link::PortFactory factory,
                     retroplug::N8Host::PortLister lister) {
    if (!host || host->abi_version != RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION) return nullptr;
    try {
        return new Provider(*host, std::move(factory), std::move(lister));
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the N8 provider did not start: %s\n", e.what());
    } catch (...) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the N8 provider did not start\n");
    }
    return nullptr;
}

retroplug::N8Host& providerHost(void* self) { return providerOf(self).n8; }

}  // namespace rp::n8

extern "C" const rp_provider* rp_n8_provider(void) {
    static const rp_provider kProvider{RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION, "n8", &rp::n8::createWithSerial, &rp::n8::restore,
                                       &rp::n8::rpcService, &rp::n8::destroy};
    return &kProvider;
}
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The N8 facet (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 6): what a product that starts the pack's provider mounts
// on its RPC server, through the rp_register_package_rpc cmake/packages.cmake generates for it from the pack's manifest
// (its `rpc` field names this header and registerRpc). Its streaming-link half is what the UI's Settings > N8 drives
// (packages/n8/ts's createN8Client, ui/screens/menu/n8Devices.ts): the ports, the chosen port, the link's state and
// lookahead, read and set on the provider's N8Host. A product that does not mount it has no N8 submenu, since the UI
// takes "the facet answers" for "this host has the N8 seam" (hasN8). Calls are synchronous and run on the thread
// the server answers on, the control thread, as every facet's do; N8Host serialises them with its link thread.
//
// The link half is the UI's alone. Each of its setters persists n8.cfg, which the standalone, the plugin and the CLI
// share (one config dir), so the CLI mounts it, as every product registers its packs one way, and its sessions never
// call it: a CLI script reaches the cart through the facet's session half (n8Open on a port, and the operations on the
// handle it answers), which persists nothing.

#include <cstdint>
#include <string>

#include "n8/desktop/N8Host.hpp"

namespace rp::n8 {

class N8Rpc {
public:
    explicit N8Rpc(retroplug::N8Host& host) : host_(host) {}

    // The serial ports (each flagged when it is an N8 by its USB VID:PID), the chosen port ("" for auto-detect),
    // whether the link is up, the user's streaming toggle, the lookahead, the bytes forwarded since connect and the
    // last error.
    retroplug::N8ConfigDto n8LinkConfig() { return host_.getConfig(); }
    // Choose the serial port by name; a live link reconnects on it. Persisted to n8.cfg. Always true.
    bool n8SetPort(std::string port) {
        host_.setPort(port);
        return true;
    }
    // Open (true) or close (false) the streaming link. Persisted to n8.cfg. Always true: whether the link came up is
    // n8LinkConfig's `connected` and `error`.
    bool n8Connect(bool enabled) {
        host_.connect(enabled);
        return true;
    }
    // The timed-release lookahead the link thread applies, in ms. Persisted to n8.cfg. Always true.
    bool n8SetLookahead(std::int32_t ms) {
        host_.setLookahead(ms);
        return true;
    }

private:
    retroplug::N8Host& host_;
};

// Mount the facet on `server` (any rpcpp TypedRpcServer: the products' over the QuickJS codec, the tests' over JSON).
// `service` is the N8 provider's (rp_provider.rpc_service), an N8Rpc; null (the provider did not start) mounts nothing,
// so the UI reads the host as having no N8 seam.
template <class Server>
void registerRpc(Server& server, void* service) {
    if (!service) return;
    N8Rpc& rpc = *static_cast<N8Rpc*>(service);
    server.template addMethod<&N8Rpc::n8LinkConfig>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&N8Rpc::n8SetPort>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&N8Rpc::n8Connect>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&N8Rpc::n8SetLookahead>(rpc);
}

}  // namespace rp::n8
````

````ts
// @retroplug/n8's TypeScript half (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 7): the client of the pack's RPC facet
// (packages/n8/native/src/n8/desktop/N8Rpc.hpp). It takes the app's RPC call rather than importing the app's backend,
// so the pack depends on nothing of packages/retroplug.
//
// This is the facet's streaming-link half, which the UI's Settings > N8 drives (ui/screens/menu/n8Devices.ts): the
// serial ports, the chosen one, the link's state and its lookahead, read and set on the host's N8 provider. The state
// lives in the native host (the serial link, n8.cfg), so every read is fresh.

/** The app's synchronous RPC call (packages/retroplug/src/rpcClient.ts's Call): it answers the method's result, and
 *  throws when the method fails or the host has no such method. */
export type N8Call = (method: string, ...params: unknown[]) => unknown;

export interface N8Port {
  port: string; // OS serial port name (/dev/ttyACM0, COM3, ...)
  isN8: boolean; // detected Everdrive N8 Pro (USB VID:PID 38df:0017)
}

export interface N8LinkConfig {
  ports: N8Port[]; // available serial ports
  selectedPort: string; // "" = none chosen (connect auto-picks the attached N8)
  connected: boolean; // the serial link is open + handshaken
  enabled: boolean; // the user's "stream to the N8" toggle
  lookaheadMs: number; // timed-release latency the serial thread applies
  bytes: number; // bytes forwarded since connect (status)
  error: string; // last error, or "" (status)
}

/** The facet's link methods. Each applies at once in the host, which persists it to n8.cfg. */
export interface N8LinkClient {
  linkConfig(): N8LinkConfig;
  setPort(port: string): void;
  connect(enabled: boolean): void;
  setLookahead(ms: number): void;
}

export interface N8Client {
  link: N8LinkClient;
}

// The reply read tolerantly, field by field, as the UI read the hook object it replaces: a host one version apart must
// not take the submenu down.
function readConfig(raw: unknown): N8LinkConfig {
  const c = (raw ?? {}) as Partial<Record<keyof N8LinkConfig, unknown>>;
  const ports = Array.isArray(c.ports)
    ? c.ports.map((p: { port?: unknown; isN8?: unknown } | null) => ({
        port: typeof p?.port === "string" ? p.port : "",
        isN8: !!p?.isN8,
      }))
    : [];
  return {
    ports,
    selectedPort: typeof c.selectedPort === "string" ? c.selectedPort : "",
    connected: !!c.connected,
    enabled: !!c.enabled,
    lookaheadMs: typeof c.lookaheadMs === "number" ? c.lookaheadMs : 0,
    bytes: typeof c.bytes === "number" ? c.bytes : typeof c.bytes === "bigint" ? Number(c.bytes) : 0,
    error: typeof c.error === "string" ? c.error : "",
  };
}

/** A client of the N8 facet over `call`. Creating one calls nothing; a host that did not mount the facet makes each
 *  method throw (the call's own error). */
export function createN8Client(call: N8Call): N8Client {
  return {
    link: {
      linkConfig: () => readConfig(call("n8LinkConfig")),
      setPort: (port) => void call("n8SetPort", port),
      connect: (enabled) => void call("n8Connect", enabled),
      setLookahead: (ms) => void call("n8SetLookahead", Math.trunc(ms)),
    },
  };
}
````

- [ ] **Step 6: The engine's side of a provider, and the products naming no N8 class**

`host/devices/ProviderHost.hpp` builds the `rp_device_host` whose `install` and `clear` forward to
`Engine::installDevice` and `clearDevice` (`noexcept`), with the product's config dir. The root lists `n8` in
`RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES` after `graph-runtime` and includes `cmake/test-binary.cmake` before the packages.
`sdl/main.cpp`, `PluginDSP.cpp` and `cli/main.cpp` hold an `rp::Providers` and a `ProviderHost`, call
`rp_start_providers` before the first graph and `rp_register_package_rpc` beside their own facets, and stop the
providers after `clearGraph()`; the standalone and the plugin restore them where they restored the `N8Host`, the CLI
never does. The six N8 sources leave the SDL and plugin targets; `retroplug-core` takes the pack's include roots for
the reliable link; `serial` now reaches the CLI however `RETROPLUG_N8_BRIDGE` is set. `packages/native/package.json`
drops `rp_n8_package`, and `N8Hooks.{hpp,cpp}` go. The engine's `deviceReason()` ends a device's refusal buffer at its
last byte and drops a trailing incomplete UTF-8 sequence, so a device that fills it without `rp_job_error` still gives
a bounded, whole reason.

Create `packages/native/src/host/devices/ProviderHost.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The rp_device_host a product hands its providers (graph/rp_provider.h, docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section
// 6): install and clear forward to the engine's device registry (Engine::installDevice and clearDevice, whose rules are
// DeviceRegistry's), and the config dir is the product's. A product declares it after its engine and before the
// rp::Providers it starts with it, so it outlives every provider.

#include <string>
#include <utility>

#include "graph/rp_provider.h"
#include "host/engine/Engine.hpp"

namespace rp::host {

class ProviderHost {
public:
    ProviderHost(Engine& engine, std::string configDir) : configDir_(std::move(configDir)) {
        host_ = {RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION, &engine, configDir_.c_str(), &install, &clear};
    }
    ProviderHost(const ProviderHost&) = delete;
    ProviderHost& operator=(const ProviderHost&) = delete;

    const rp_device_host* get() const { return &host_; }

private:
    static bool install(void* ctx, const char* name, const char* interfaceId, void* link, void (*acquire)(void*),
                        void (*release)(void*)) {
        return static_cast<Engine*>(ctx)->installDevice(name, interfaceId, link, acquire, release);
    }
    static void clear(void* ctx, void* link) { static_cast<Engine*>(ctx)->clearDevice(link); }

    std::string    configDir_;
    rp_device_host host_{};
};

}  // namespace rp::host
````

````diff
+    // The providers of the packages this product lists (the N8 pack's), started after the engine and before a session

+    // way, and the N8 sessions a CLI script opens arrive in the same facet. Never restored: a provider's persisted

+// A device's refusal, read from the buffer the engine handed it (rp_device_jobs::submit). The ABI asks for a reason of
+// at most `size` bytes with its NUL, which rp_job_error writes cut at a code point, but a device is not bound to that
+// helper: one that copies with memcpy or strncpy may leave no NUL, or split a code point at the end. So the buffer is
+// terminated at its last byte whatever the device wrote, and a UTF-8 sequence its end leaves incomplete is dropped
+// whole: the reason is always bounded and never carries half a character into a JS string.
+std::string deviceReason(char* error, std::size_t size) {
+    if (size == 0) return {};
+    error[size - 1] = '\0';
+    std::size_t n = std::strlen(error);
+    // Back over the continuation bytes at the end (three at most, a 4-byte sequence's), to the byte that leads them.
+    std::size_t lead = n;
+    while (lead > 0 && n - lead < 3 && (static_cast<unsigned char>(error[lead - 1]) & 0xC0u) == 0x80u) --lead;
+    if (lead > 0) {
+        const unsigned char b = static_cast<unsigned char>(error[lead - 1]);
+        const std::size_t   want = (b & 0xE0u) == 0xC0u ? 2 : (b & 0xF0u) == 0xE0u ? 3 : (b & 0xF8u) == 0xF0u ? 4 : 1;
+        if (want > 1 && n - (lead - 1) < want) n = lead - 1;
+    }
+    return std::string(error, n);
+}
````

- [ ] **Step 7: The device check links the pack**

`RP_DEVICE_CHECK_PACKAGES` is `core dsp n8`, and the device project finds the pack through `retroplug_package(n8)`.
The check's host now offers `rp.host.devices/2` with an acquire that always answers null: without it `rp.n8.nes`'s
activate refuses, and with it the node runs on its `NoCart`, as in a host that owns no device.
`tools/build-device-check.sh`'s size table gains the row `n8: the rp.n8 nodes`.

- [ ] **Step 8: The tests: the fake job host, the provider and the products' providers**

`FakeJobs.hpp` is the pack's own job record (`rp::n8::test::Job`, its `JobRequest`, `requestView`, `handle`, `record`
and an `rp_host_jobs` over it), so `retroplug-n8-test` and `-hwtest` read nothing of packages/native and a record
other than the engine's is proved to work. `N8Provider.test.cpp` holds `[n8-rpc]` (the four link methods over FakeN8,
persistence to n8.cfg, a null service mounting nothing) and `[n8-provider]` (the install, the hooks reaching
`N8CartLink`'s holder count, restore from an n8.cfg left enabled, a destroy clearing exactly its link, the clear
reading through the link before it is freed). `Providers.test.cpp` is `[providers]`: the order with fake providers,
another ABI refused, a throwing create, this product's generated providers into a real `Engine` and server, and a
product listing none. `tests.cmake` adds it, links rpcpp, generates the "without" header and holds the four refused
manifests and the pack's own at every configure. `[n8-adapters]` drives the real provider behind a real engine to
FakeN8 from an RAII holder that reclaims the plans before it stops the provider; `N8Node.test.cpp`'s threads case
becomes "rp.n8.nes declares no threads, so a target with none plans the type".

Create `packages/n8/native/test/FakeJobs.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// A job host of the pack's own tests (graph/rp_jobs.h): the record a job runs into, the request a case builds, and the
// rp.host.jobs/1 a device reports through, over that record. Not the engine's (host/engine/CapabilityJobs.hpp): the
// pack's tests reach nothing of packages/native, and a record that is not the engine's is what the job ABI promises
// works, since every host keeps rp_job incomplete and casts its own record to and from it. N8Host and N8CartLink take
// the job through their DeviceJobSlot and report into it exactly as they would into the engine's.

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "graph/rp_jobs.h"

namespace rp::n8::test {

// What a case asks for, as the control plane would: the strings and bytes rp_job_request borrows.
struct JobRequest {
    std::string               nodeId;
    std::string               capability;
    std::string               op;
    std::string               region;
    std::uint32_t             offset = 0;
    std::uint32_t             length = 0;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;
    std::string               name;
};

// The C request for `r`, borrowing its strings and bytes: valid while `r` is.
inline rp_job_request requestView(const JobRequest& r) {
    return rp_job_request{r.nodeId.c_str(), r.capability.c_str(), r.op.c_str(), r.region.c_str(), r.name.c_str(),
                          r.offset,         r.length,             r.bytes.data(), r.bytes.size()};
}

// One job's record: untouched until the device takes it (Queued), then its progress, and its result or its reason
// before its terminal state, which is stored last with release and read with acquire, as the job model hands it off.
struct Job {
    enum State : std::uint8_t { Queued, Done, Failed };
    enum Failure : std::uint8_t { None, Removed, Device };

    std::atomic<std::uint8_t>  state{Queued};
    std::atomic<std::uint8_t>  failure{None};
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> progress{0};
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> total{0};
    std::vector<std::uint8_t>  result;
    std::string                error;

    bool finished() const {
        const std::uint8_t s = state.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        return s == Done || s == Failed;
    }
};

inline rp_job* handle(Job* job) { return reinterpret_cast<rp_job*>(job); }
inline Job*    record(rp_job* job) { return reinterpret_cast<Job*>(job); }

// rp.host.jobs/1 over the records above.
inline const rp_host_jobs* jobReports() {
    static const rp_host_jobs kReports{
        [](rp_job* h, std::uint32_t done, std::uint32_t total) {
            Job* job = record(h);
            job->total.store(total, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            job->progress.store(done, std::memory_order_release);
        },
        [](rp_job* h, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
            Job* job = record(h);
            job->result.assign(data, data + size);
            job->state.store(Job::Done, std::memory_order_release);
        },
        [](rp_job* h, const char* reason) {
            Job* job = record(h);
            job->error = reason != nullptr ? reason : "";
            job->failure.store(Job::Device, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            job->state.store(Job::Failed, std::memory_order_release);
        },
        [](rp_job* h) {
            Job* job = record(h);
            job->failure.store(Job::Removed, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            job->state.store(Job::Failed, std::memory_order_release);
        }};
    return &kReports;
}

}  // namespace rp::n8::test
````

````cpp
// The N8 pack's provider and facet (n8/desktop/N8Provider.hpp, N8Rpc.hpp; docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section
// 6), over FakeN8: the facet's four link methods read and set an N8Host's state, through the class and through a server
// they are mounted on (rpcpp's JSON codec here; the products mount them over QuickJS's), and a null service mounts
// nothing; the provider installs its cart link under the N8's name and interface, hands the registry hooks that reach
// that link, brings n8.cfg back at restore, and clears the link before it frees it. Run by `pnpm test:n8`.

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "TypedRpcServer.h"
#include "codecs/JsonCodec.h"
#include "transports/QueueTransport.h"

#include "FakeN8.hpp"
#include "n8/CartLink.hpp"
#include "n8/desktop/N8CartLink.hpp"
#include "n8/desktop/N8Host.hpp"
#include "n8/desktop/N8Provider.hpp"
#include "n8/desktop/N8Rpc.hpp"

using retroplug::N8ConfigDto;
using retroplug::N8Host;
using retroplug::N8PortDto;
using retroplug::test::FakeN8;
using retroplug::test::factoryFor;

namespace {

N8Host::PortLister twoPorts() {
    return [] { return std::vector<N8PortDto>{{"/dev/ttyS0", false}, {"/dev/ttyACM0", true}}; };
}

std::filesystem::path cleanDir(const char* name) {
    const auto dir = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / name;
    std::filesystem::create_directories(dir);
    std::filesystem::remove(dir / "n8.cfg");
    return dir;
}

using JsonServer = rpcpp::TypedRpcServer<rpcpp::Empty, rpcpp::JsonCodec>;

std::string ask(JsonServer& server, const std::string& method, const std::string& params = "[]") {
    const auto out =
        server.processMessage(R"({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":")" + method + R"(","params":)" + params + "}");
    return out ? *out : std::string();
}

bool has(const std::string& text, const std::string& part) { return text.find(part) != std::string::npos; }

// A device host recording what the provider installs and clears.
struct Registry {
    void* link = nullptr;
    void (*acquire)(void*) = nullptr;
    void (*release)(void*) = nullptr;
    std::string name, interfaceId;
    std::vector<void*> cleared;
    // What the link read when it was cleared: clear comes before the link is freed, so reading through it here is
    // reading a live object (ASan would catch the provider freeing it first).
    std::vector<bool> connectedAtClear;
    bool refuse = false;
    std::string dir;

    rp_device_host host() {
        rp_device_host h{};
        h.abi_version = RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION;
        h.ctx         = this;
        h.config_dir  = dir.c_str();
        h.install     = [](void* ctx, const char* n, const char* id, void* l, void (*a)(void*), void (*r)(void*)) {
            auto& self = *static_cast<Registry*>(ctx);
            if (self.refuse) return false;
            self.name = n, self.interfaceId = id, self.link = l, self.acquire = a, self.release = r;
            return true;
        };
        h.clear = [](void* ctx, void* l) {
            auto& self = *static_cast<Registry*>(ctx);
            self.cleared.push_back(l);
            self.connectedAtClear.push_back(static_cast<rp::n8::CartLink*>(l)->connected());
        };
        return h;
    }
};

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("the N8 facet's link methods read and set the host's state", "[n8-rpc]") {
    FakeN8          dev;
    const auto      dir = cleanDir("rp-n8-rpc-test");
    N8Host          host(factoryFor(dev), twoPorts(), dir.string());
    rp::n8::N8Rpc   rpc(host);

    N8ConfigDto c = rpc.n8LinkConfig();
    REQUIRE(c.ports.size() == 2);
    CHECK(c.ports[1].port == "/dev/ttyACM0");
    CHECK(c.ports[1].isN8);
    CHECK_FALSE(c.connected);
    CHECK_FALSE(c.enabled);

    CHECK(rpc.n8Connect(true));
    c = rpc.n8LinkConfig();
    CHECK(c.enabled);
    CHECK(c.connected);
    CHECK(c.selectedPort == "/dev/ttyACM0");  // auto-picked: the port flagged as an N8

    CHECK(rpc.n8SetLookahead(25));
    CHECK(rpc.n8LinkConfig().lookaheadMs == 25);
    CHECK(rpc.n8SetPort("/dev/ttyACM1"));
    c = rpc.n8LinkConfig();
    CHECK(c.selectedPort == "/dev/ttyACM1");
    CHECK(c.connected);  // a live link moves to the new port

    CHECK(rpc.n8Connect(false));
    CHECK_FALSE(rpc.n8LinkConfig().connected);
    // Each one is persisted where N8Host keeps it.
    std::ifstream cfg(dir / "n8.cfg");
    std::string   port;
    std::getline(cfg, port);
    CHECK(port == "/dev/ttyACM1");
}

TEST_CASE("registerRpc mounts the four methods on a server, and a null service mounts none", "[n8-rpc]") {
    FakeN8        dev;
    N8Host        host(factoryFor(dev), twoPorts(), cleanDir("rp-n8-rpc-test").string());
    rp::n8::N8Rpc rpc(host);

    rpcpp::QueueTransport<rpcpp::JsonCodec> transport;
    JsonServer                              server(transport);
    rp::n8::registerRpc(server, &rpc);
    std::string reply = ask(server, "n8LinkConfig");
    INFO(reply);
    CHECK(has(reply, R"({"port":"/dev/ttyS0","isN8":false})"));
    CHECK(has(reply, R"("connected":false)"));
    CHECK(has(ask(server, "n8Connect", "[true]"), R"("result":true)"));
    CHECK(has(ask(server, "n8SetLookahead", "[30]"), R"("result":true)"));
    CHECK(has(ask(server, "n8SetPort", R"(["/dev/ttyACM0"])"), R"("result":true)"));
    reply = ask(server, "n8LinkConfig");
    CHECK(has(reply, R"("connected":true)"));
    CHECK(has(reply, R"("lookaheadMs":30)"));
    CHECK(has(reply, R"("selectedPort":"/dev/ttyACM0")"));

    rpcpp::QueueTransport<rpcpp::JsonCodec> otherTransport;
    JsonServer                              other(otherTransport);
    rp::n8::registerRpc(other, nullptr);
    CHECK(has(ask(other, "n8LinkConfig"), "-32601"));  // Method not found
}

TEST_CASE("the N8 provider installs its cart link, restores n8.cfg and clears the link before it frees it",
          "[n8-provider]") {
    FakeN8   dev;
    Registry registry;
    registry.dir = cleanDir("rp-n8-provider-test").string();
    {
        std::ofstream cfg(registry.dir + "/n8.cfg");
        cfg << "/dev/ttyACM0\n0\n1\n";  // the port, a lookahead of 0 ms, streaming left enabled
    }
    const rp_device_host host = registry.host();
    const rp_provider*   provider = rp_n8_provider();
    REQUIRE(std::string(provider->id) == "n8");

    void* self = rp::n8::createProvider(&host, factoryFor(dev), twoPorts());
    REQUIRE(self != nullptr);
    CHECK(registry.name == rp::n8::kDeviceName);
    CHECK(registry.interfaceId == rp::n8::kCartLinkInterface);
    REQUIRE(registry.link != nullptr);
    REQUIRE(registry.acquire != nullptr);
    REQUIRE(registry.release != nullptr);
    auto* cart = static_cast<rp::n8::CartLink*>(registry.link);
    CHECK_FALSE(cart->connected());
    // The hooks reach the cart link's count of the nodes holding it: two nodes binding it (a handover), then both
    // giving it back.
    auto& counted = static_cast<retroplug::N8CartLink&>(*cart);
    CHECK(counted.holders() == 0);
    registry.acquire(registry.link);
    registry.acquire(registry.link);
    CHECK(counted.holders() == 2);
    registry.release(registry.link);
    CHECK(counted.holders() == 1);
    registry.release(registry.link);
    CHECK(counted.holders() == 0);

    // Nothing connects until restore, which reads n8.cfg.
    N8Host& n8 = rp::n8::providerHost(self);
    CHECK_FALSE(n8.getConfig().connected);
    provider->restore(self);
    CHECK(n8.getConfig().connected);
    CHECK(n8.getConfig().lookaheadMs == 0);
    CHECK(cart->connected());

    // The facet's service is the provider's, over the same host.
    auto* rpc = static_cast<rp::n8::N8Rpc*>(provider->rpc_service(self));
    REQUIRE(rpc != nullptr);
    CHECK(rpc->n8LinkConfig().selectedPort == "/dev/ttyACM0");

    void* const installed = registry.link;
    provider->destroy(self);
    CHECK(registry.cleared == std::vector<void*>{installed});
    CHECK(registry.connectedAtClear == std::vector<bool>{true});  // read through the link, still streaming
}

TEST_CASE("the N8 provider refuses another ABI, and one whose link the registry refuses clears nothing",
          "[n8-provider]") {
    FakeN8   dev;
    Registry registry;
    registry.dir        = cleanDir("rp-n8-provider-test").string();
    rp_device_host host = registry.host();
    host.abi_version    = RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION + 1;
    CHECK(rp::n8::createProvider(&host, factoryFor(dev), twoPorts()) == nullptr);
    CHECK(rp::n8::createProvider(nullptr, factoryFor(dev), twoPorts()) == nullptr);

    registry.refuse = true;
    host            = registry.host();
    void* self      = rp::n8::createProvider(&host, factoryFor(dev), twoPorts());
    REQUIRE(self != nullptr);  // it runs, its node on its stub
    CHECK(registry.link == nullptr);
    rp_n8_provider()->destroy(self);
    CHECK(registry.cleared.empty());
}
````

````cpp
// The providers a product starts (graph/rp_provider.h, graph/desktop/Providers.hpp,
// docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 6): created in the order the product's packages list them, restored in
// that order and stopped in the reverse; one that does not start, or is of another ABI version, left out, and one that
// throws stopping those started before it; and what cmake/packages.cmake generates for a product from its packages'
// manifests. This binary is a product listing the N8 pack, so its generated rp_start_providers starts the N8 provider
// into a real engine's registry and its rp_register_package_rpc mounts the pack's facet; a header generated for a
// product listing no provider (tests.cmake, without/rp_product_providers.hpp) starts and mounts nothing. The ports are
// deps/serial's here, so nothing connects: the provider is never restored from an n8.cfg that enables the link, and the
// facet is only read. [n8-adapters] drives the same provider to a fake cart.

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <cstddef>
#include <filesystem>
#include <optional>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "TypedRpcServer.h"
#include "codecs/JsonCodec.h"
#include "transports/QueueTransport.h"

#include "graph/desktop/Providers.hpp"
#include "host/devices/ProviderHost.hpp"
#include "host/engine/Engine.hpp"
#include "n8/CartLink.hpp"

#include "rp_product_providers.hpp"  // this product's (retroplug-engine-graph-test's), generated
// Inside a namespace of its own, so its functions do not collide with this product's. That works only because every
// header it includes was included above already: their guards keep them out of the namespace.
namespace without {
#include "without/rp_product_providers.hpp"  // a product listing core, dsp, graph-runtime and native: no provider
}

namespace {

// A provider that records what is done to it, as "<id>:<call>".
std::vector<std::string> gLog;
struct Fake {
    const char* id;
    int         service = 0;
};
Fake gA{"a"}, gB{"b"};

template <Fake* F>
const rp_provider* fakeProvider() {
    static const rp_provider kProvider{
        RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION, F->id,
        [](const rp_device_host* host) -> void* {
            gLog.push_back(std::string(F->id) + ":create " + host->config_dir);
            return F;
        },
        [](void* self) { gLog.push_back(std::string(static_cast<Fake*>(self)->id) + ":restore"); },
        [](void* self) -> void* { return &static_cast<Fake*>(self)->service; },
        [](void* self) { gLog.push_back(std::string(static_cast<Fake*>(self)->id) + ":destroy"); }};
    return &kProvider;
}
const rp_provider* failingProvider() {
    static const rp_provider kProvider{RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION, "failing",
                                       [](const rp_device_host*) -> void* {
                                           gLog.push_back("failing:create");
                                           return nullptr;
                                       },
                                       [](void*) { gLog.push_back("failing:restore"); }, nullptr,
                                       [](void*) { gLog.push_back("failing:destroy"); }};
    return &kProvider;
}
// Built against another layout of the table: only its version may be read, so nothing of it is ever called.
const rp_provider* otherAbiProvider() {
    static const rp_provider kProvider{RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION + 1, "other",
                                       [](const rp_device_host*) -> void* {
                                           gLog.push_back("other:create");
                                           return &gLog;
                                       },
                                       nullptr, nullptr, [](void*) { gLog.push_back("other:destroy"); }};
    return &kProvider;
}
// A create that throws, which no provider's may: the table is C, but a C++ provider that broke the rule must not leave
// the providers started before it running.
const rp_provider* throwingProvider() {
    static const rp_provider kProvider{RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION, "throwing",
                                       [](const rp_device_host*) -> void* {
                                           gLog.push_back("throwing:create");
                                           throw std::runtime_error("no");
                                       },
                                       nullptr, nullptr, [](void*) { gLog.push_back("throwing:destroy"); }};
    return &kProvider;
}

rp_device_host fakeHost() {
    rp_device_host host{};
    host.abi_version = RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION;
    host.config_dir  = "/cfg";
    return host;
}

using JsonServer = rpcpp::TypedRpcServer<rpcpp::Empty, rpcpp::JsonCodec>;

std::string ask(JsonServer& server, const std::string& method) {
    const auto out = server.processMessage(R"({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":")" + method + R"(","params":[]})");
    return out ? *out : std::string();
}

// Whether `engine`'s registry holds a link under the N8's name and interface: one installed there refuses another.
bool holdsCart(Engine& engine) {
    int probe = 0;
    if (!engine.installDevice(rp::n8::kDeviceName, rp::n8::kCartLinkInterface, &probe)) return true;
    engine.clearDevice(&probe);
    return false;
}

std::string emptyConfigDir() {
    const auto dir = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / "rp-providers-test";
    std::filesystem::create_directories(dir);
    std::filesystem::remove(dir / "n8.cfg");  // never one that would reconnect a real port
    return dir.string();
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("providers start in table order, restore in it and stop in the reverse, and one that fails is left out",
          "[engine-graph][providers]") {
    gLog.clear();
    const rp_device_host host = fakeHost();
    const rp_provider_fn table[] = {&fakeProvider<&gA>, &failingProvider, &fakeProvider<&gB>};
    {
        rp::Providers providers(table, 3, &host);
        CHECK(gLog == std::vector<std::string>{"a:create /cfg", "failing:create", "b:create /cfg"});
        CHECK(providers.size() == 3);
        CHECK(providers.service(0) == &gA.service);
        CHECK(providers.service(1) == nullptr);  // it did not start
        CHECK(providers.service(2) == &gB.service);
        CHECK(providers.service(3) == nullptr);

        gLog.clear();
        providers.restore();
        CHECK(gLog == std::vector<std::string>{"a:restore", "b:restore"});

        // Moved, the providers are stopped once, by their new owner.
        rp::Providers moved = std::move(providers);
        gLog.clear();
        providers.stop();
        CHECK(gLog.empty());
        moved.stop();
        CHECK(gLog == std::vector<std::string>{"b:destroy", "a:destroy"});
        CHECK(moved.service(0) == nullptr);
        gLog.clear();
    }
    CHECK(gLog.empty());  // stopped already: the destructor stops nothing twice

    // And a destructor stops what was not stopped.
    {
        rp::Providers providers(table, 3, &host);
        gLog.clear();
    }
    CHECK(gLog == std::vector<std::string>{"b:destroy", "a:destroy"});
}

TEST_CASE("a provider of another ABI version is refused, and a create that throws stops what started before it",
          "[engine-graph][providers]") {
    const rp_device_host host = fakeHost();
    SECTION("another ABI version") {
        gLog.clear();
        const rp_provider_fn table[] = {&fakeProvider<&gA>, &otherAbiProvider, &fakeProvider<&gB>};
        {
            rp::Providers providers(table, 3, &host);
            CHECK(gLog == std::vector<std::string>{"a:create /cfg", "b:create /cfg"});  // never created
            CHECK(providers.service(1) == nullptr);
            gLog.clear();
            providers.restore();
            CHECK(gLog == std::vector<std::string>{"a:restore", "b:restore"});
            gLog.clear();
        }
        CHECK(gLog == std::vector<std::string>{"b:destroy", "a:destroy"});
    }
    SECTION("a create that throws") {
        gLog.clear();
        const rp_provider_fn table[] = {&fakeProvider<&gA>, &fakeProvider<&gB>, &throwingProvider};
        CHECK_THROWS_AS(rp::Providers(table, 3, &host), std::runtime_error);
        CHECK(gLog == std::vector<std::string>{"a:create /cfg", "b:create /cfg", "throwing:create", "b:destroy",
                                               "a:destroy"});
    }
}

TEST_CASE("this product's generated providers start the N8 provider into its engine and mount the N8 facet",
          "[engine-graph][providers]") {
    Engine                 engine(48000.0);
    rp::host::ProviderHost deviceHost(engine, emptyConfigDir());
    REQUIRE_FALSE(holdsCart(engine));

    rp::Providers providers = rp_start_providers(deviceHost.get());
    REQUIRE(providers.size() == 1);
    CHECK(holdsCart(engine));  // installed as n8 / rp.n8.cart-link/1
    rp_restore_providers(providers);  // no n8.cfg: nothing to bring back, nothing connects
    CHECK(holdsCart(engine));

    rpcpp::QueueTransport<rpcpp::JsonCodec> transport;
    JsonServer                              server(transport);
    rp_register_package_rpc(server, providers);
    const std::string config = ask(server, "n8LinkConfig");
    INFO(config);
    CHECK(config.find(R"("connected":false)") != std::string::npos);
    CHECK(config.find(R"("enabled":false)") != std::string::npos);
    CHECK(config.find(R"("ports":)") != std::string::npos);

    // Stopped after the plans (none here), the provider takes its link back.
    engine.clearGraph();
    rp_stop_providers(providers);
    CHECK_FALSE(holdsCart(engine));
    CHECK(providers.size() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a product listing no provider starts nothing and mounts nothing", "[engine-graph][providers]") {
    Engine                 engine(48000.0);
    rp::host::ProviderHost deviceHost(engine, emptyConfigDir());
    rp::Providers          providers = without::rp_start_providers(deviceHost.get());
    CHECK(providers.size() == 0);
    CHECK_FALSE(holdsCart(engine));

    rpcpp::QueueTransport<rpcpp::JsonCodec> transport;
    JsonServer                              server(transport);
    without::rp_register_package_rpc(server, providers);
    CHECK(ask(server, "n8LinkConfig").find("-32601") != std::string::npos);  // Method not found
    without::rp_restore_providers(providers);
    without::rp_stop_providers(providers);
    CHECK(providers.size() == 0);
}
````
