````diff
+
+# What a manifest may not say, held at every configure: each scratch manifest under test/packages/refused must be
+# refused by the reader retroplug_package() runs (cmake/packages.cmake's _retroplug_read_manifest, run here in script
+# mode by cmake/check-manifest.cmake) with its own reason, so a rule that stopped firing fails the configure rather than
+# going unnoticed; and the N8 pack's manifest, whose desktop entry names a provider and its facet, must read.
+set(_rp_refused_manifests
+    "ProviderOnDevice|entry rp_scratch_package is `device` and names a provider or an rpc"
+    "RpcOnDevice|entry scratch-desktop is `device` and names a provider or an rpc"
+    "RpcWithoutProvider|entry scratch-desktop names an rpc and no provider"
+    "ProviderWithoutDevice|entry scratch-desktop needs \"device\": true or false")
+foreach(_rp_refused IN LISTS _rp_refused_manifests)
+    string(REPLACE "|" ";" _rp_refused "${_rp_refused}")
+    list(GET _rp_refused 0 _rp_manifest)
+    list(GET _rp_refused 1 _rp_reason)
+    execute_process(
+        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -DRP_MANIFEST=${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/test/packages/refused/${_rp_manifest}.json
+                -P ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/check-manifest.cmake
+        RESULT_VARIABLE _rp_result OUTPUT_VARIABLE _rp_output ERROR_VARIABLE _rp_output)
+    if(_rp_result EQUAL 0)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/refused/${_rp_manifest}.json was read; the configure must refuse it")
+    endif()
+    # CMake wraps a message's lines, so the reason is looked for with the output's whitespace folded.
+    string(REGEX REPLACE "[ \t\r\n]+" " " _rp_folded "${_rp_output}")
+    string(FIND "${_rp_folded}" "${_rp_reason}" _rp_at)
+    if(_rp_at EQUAL -1)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/refused/${_rp_manifest}.json was refused, but not with \"${_rp_reason}\":\n"
+                            "${_rp_output}")
+    endif()
+endforeach()
+execute_process(
+    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -DRP_MANIFEST=${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/n8/package.json
+            -P ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/check-manifest.cmake
+    RESULT_VARIABLE _rp_result OUTPUT_VARIABLE _rp_output ERROR_VARIABLE _rp_output)
+if(NOT _rp_result EQUAL 0)
+    message(FATAL_ERROR "packages/n8/package.json did not read in script mode:\n${_rp_output}")
+endif()

+// The provider a case started, stopped as a product stops it: the engine's plans first, while the link is installed,
+// then the provider. A holder, so a REQUIRE that fails mid-case still stops it, in that order, before the FakeN8 whose
+// port its serial thread polls goes out of scope.
+class StartedProvider {
+public:
+    StartedProvider(Engine& engine, void* self) : engine_(engine), self_(self) {}
+    StartedProvider(const StartedProvider&) = delete;
+    StartedProvider& operator=(const StartedProvider&) = delete;
+    ~StartedProvider() { stop(); }
+
+    void* get() const { return self_; }
+    void  stop() {
+        if (!self_) return;
+        engine_.clearGraph();
+        rp_n8_provider()->destroy(std::exchange(self_, nullptr));
+    }
+
+private:
+    Engine& engine_;
+    void*   self_;
+};
+
 }  // namespace

+TEST_CASE("a device's refusal that fills the buffer with no NUL, or ends mid code point, still comes back bounded and "
+          "whole",
+          "[engine-graph][n8-node]") {
+    // A device that copies its reason in rather than through rp_job_error: the engine ends the buffer at its last byte
+    // itself and drops a UTF-8 sequence its end leaves incomplete, so what crosses the RPC is bounded and a string.
+    FakeCart               cart;
+    Engine                 e(kRate);
+    rp::host::test::Roms   roms;
+    std::vector<DocSystem> systems{{1, rp::host::test::kNesType}};
+    withRoms(e, systems, roms);
+    rp::host::test::installCart(e, cart);
+    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(cartDocument(systems)).ok);
+    block(e);
+    static_assert(Engine::kDeviceJobErrorBytes == 256);
+
+    // Every byte of the buffer written, none of them a NUL: the reason is the first 255.
+    cart.rawRefusal = std::string(300, 'q');
+    CHECK(e.submitJob(request(RP_SYSTEM_SRAM_INTERFACE, "dump")).error == std::string(255, 'q'));
+    // A three-byte code point whose last byte is the buffer's 256th: the two that are left are dropped.
+    cart.rawRefusal = std::string(253, 'x') + "\xE2\x82\xAC";
````

- [ ] **Step 9: The UI on the facet**

`n8Devices.ts` calls the facet through `createN8Client(makeCall())`: it probes once, and `hasN8()` is true when
`n8LinkConfig` answers (the headless UI harness mounts no facet, so its submenu stays hidden); `setN8LinkClient()` is
the seam the mock tier uses. `nativeHooks.ts` loses the four hook declarations, `n8-sd-ops.test.ts` installs a fake
link client in place of the globals, and `link-client.test.ts` (3 cases) holds the client's method names and
arguments, its tolerant config read, and a host without the facet throwing from the call. The TS twins' comments name
the moved C++ files' new paths.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/n8/link-client.test.ts`:

````ts
// The N8 pack's client, its streaming-link half (@retroplug/n8, packages/n8/ts/index.ts), over a fake RPC call: each
// method sends the facet's method with its arguments (packages/n8/native/src/n8/desktop/N8Rpc.hpp), the config reply
// is read tolerantly as the UI read the hook object it replaces, and a host that did not mount the facet throws from
// the call, which is what the UI's hasN8 takes for "no N8 seam". The facet itself is held in C++ (retroplug-n8-test's
// [n8-rpc] cases); this is the TS half alone, so it runs in the mock tier, with no native host.
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";
import { createN8Client, type N8Call } from "@retroplug/n8";

function recordingCall(answers: Record<string, unknown>): { call: N8Call; sent: unknown[][] } {
  const sent: unknown[][] = [];
  const call: N8Call = (method, ...params) => {
    sent.push([method, ...params]);
    if (!(method in answers)) throw new Error(`rpc ${method}: [-32601] Method not found`);
    return answers[method];
  };
  return { call, sent };
}

test("the link client sends each facet method with its arguments", () => {
  const { call, sent } = recordingCall({ n8SetPort: true, n8Connect: true, n8SetLookahead: true });
  const link = createN8Client(call).link;
  link.setPort("/dev/ttyACM0");
  link.connect(true);
  link.connect(false);
  link.setLookahead(15.7);
  expect(sent).toEqual([
    ["n8SetPort", "/dev/ttyACM0"],
    ["n8Connect", true],
    ["n8Connect", false],
    ["n8SetLookahead", 15],
  ]);
});

test("the link config reply is read whole, and tolerantly where a field is missing or of another type", () => {
  const full = {
    ports: [{ port: "/dev/ttyACM0", isN8: true }, { port: "/dev/ttyS0", isN8: false }],
    selectedPort: "/dev/ttyACM0",
    connected: true,
    enabled: true,
    lookaheadMs: 10,
    bytes: 1234,
    error: "",
  };
  expect(createN8Client(recordingCall({ n8LinkConfig: full }).call).link.linkConfig()).toEqual(full);

  const sparse = createN8Client(recordingCall({ n8LinkConfig: { ports: [null, { port: 7 }], bytes: 5n, error: 3 } }).call);
  expect(sparse.link.linkConfig()).toEqual({
    ports: [
      { port: "", isN8: false },
      { port: "", isN8: false },
    ],
    selectedPort: "",
    connected: false,
    enabled: false,
    lookaheadMs: 0,
    bytes: 5,
    error: "",
  });
  expect(createN8Client(recordingCall({ n8LinkConfig: null }).call).link.linkConfig().ports).toEqual([]);
});

test("creating a client calls nothing, and a host without the facet throws from the call", () => {
  const { call, sent } = recordingCall({});
  const link = createN8Client(call).link;
  expect(sent).toEqual([]);
  expect(() => link.linkConfig()).toThrow("Method not found");
  expect(() => link.connect(true)).toThrow("Method not found");
});
````

````bash
feat(n8): the N8 pack, its provider and the facet's link half

Everything RetroPlug knows about the Everdrive N8 Pro on the native side moves into one workspace package,
packages/n8 (@retroplug/n8), by git mv, as the template a flash-cart pack follows
(docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md sections 3, 6 and 7). Its manifest has two native entries: the portable
retroplug-n8 (rp_n8_package, device: true: rp.n8.nes, n8/CartLink.hpp and the node's NoCart stub, on node-sdk alone)
and the desktop retroplug-n8-desktop (Edio, N8Link, N8Host, N8Menu, N8CartLink and WjwwoodSerialPort, moved as they
are, plus the provider and the facet). BlipToaster's reliable link moves with N8Link, and util/FixedQueue.hpp into
node-sdk, so the pack reaches nothing of packages/native; the emulated NES FIFO role includes the link from the
pack. retroplug-n8-test, retroplug-serial-test and retroplug-n8-hwtest move with the code and keep their names and
pnpm test:n8. RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES lists n8 after the other carved packages, so the [packages] golden moves rp.n8.nes
after rp.host.audio-out in every row, each product's type ids unchanged.

rp.n8.nes declares no threads: whether a cart link runs a thread is the host's link's business (the desktop's
streams from a serial thread, a box's need not), and the node needs only a push that never blocks, which CartLink
promises. So its entry is device: true, retroplug-n8-device compiles in the default build, n8 joins the device
check's packages, and rp-device-check links rp.n8.nes under the link trap (the check's host offers rp.host.devices
answering null, so the node runs on its stub). A Pico target plans the type, which N8Node.test.cpp holds where it
held the refusal.

A provider (node-sdk's graph/rp_provider.h, desktop-only C) is how a product starts a pack's device service without
naming it. Its table leads with abi_version, which rp::Providers checks, refusing and logging a mismatch; no call of
the table throws (the N8 provider's entry points catch and answer null or log), and rp::Providers destroys the
providers it had started when a create or a push_back throws anyway. A manifest entry's `provider` and `rpc` fields
are read by cmake/packages.cmake, which refuses either on a device entry and an rpc without a provider (held at
every configure over scratch manifests run through the reader in script mode, cmake/check-manifest.cmake), and
generates per product a header-only rp_product_providers.hpp: rp_start_providers(host), rp_restore_providers,
rp_stop_providers (manifest order, stopped in reverse, over node-sdk's rp::Providers) and
rp_register_package_rpc<Server>. The providers' state is an object the product holds per instance, since a DAW holds
several plugin instances, and the header is inline so a binary that never includes it (the render host, most tests)
links nothing of the providers. The engine side of rp_device_host (host/devices/ProviderHost.hpp) forwards to
Engine::installDevice and clearDevice.

The N8 provider owns the serial port factory and lister, the N8Host (n8.cfg's format and path unchanged) and the
N8CartLink, installed as n8 / rp.n8.cart-link/1. The SDL standalone, the plugin and the CLI start, mount and stop it
through their generated functions and name no N8 class; the standalone and the plugin restore it where they restored
the N8Host, and the CLI does not, since restoring the UI's persisted link would claim the port its own N8 sessions
open; the CLI mounts the facet as every product does, and its link half, which persists the n8.cfg the products
share, is the UI's alone. Each reclaims its plans before it stops the providers. The six N8 sources leave the SDL
and plugin targets, and the engine-graph test links the pack instead.

The facet's streaming-link half (n8/desktop/N8Rpc.hpp: n8LinkConfig, n8SetPort, n8Connect, n8SetLookahead) replaces
N8Hooks.cpp and the four __rp_*N8 hooks, so the pack depends on neither QuickJS nor rpcpp. On the TS side
packages/n8/ts/index.ts's createN8Client(call) holds that half, packages/retroplug depends on @retroplug/n8 as
workspace:*, and n8Devices.ts calls the facet, with hasN8() meaning the product mounted it (the headless UI harness
mounts none). The UI reaches it through the control plane's __rpcSend in both the standalone and the plugin, whose
UI shares that context.

The engine ends a device's refusal buffer at its last byte and drops a UTF-8 sequence its end leaves incomplete, so
a device that fills it without rp_job_error still gives a bounded, whole reason; rp_jobs.h says every host keeps
rp_job incomplete.

Tests: [n8-rpc] and [n8-provider] in retroplug-n8-test (the registry's clear reading through the link before it is
freed, the hooks reaching N8CartLink's holder count), [providers] in the engine-graph test (the order, another ABI
refused, a throwing create stopping what started before it, this product's generated providers into a real engine
and server, a product listing none), [n8-adapters] driving the real provider behind a real engine to FakeN8 from an
RAII holder that reclaims the plans before it stops the provider, and the TS client's link half in the mock tier.
The pack's tests run their jobs into a fake job host of their own (test/FakeJobs.hpp, its own record and
rp_host_jobs, through DeviceJobSlot), so retroplug-n8-test and -hwtest read nothing of packages/native.
retroplug-n8-test and the engine-graph tags [n8-node], [n8-adapters] and [providers] run clean under TSan and ASan.
EOF
````

### Task 3: the one Edio, its menu and operations, the facet's sessions and the TS swap

Design sections 4, 6 and 7 and section 10's third commit. The Edio protocol exists once, in the pack's portable target
(`packages/n8/native/src/n8`, namespace `rp::n8`, built for the RP2350 as for the desktop): `Transport.hpp`, the
abstract byte pipe; `Edio`, the commands over it, every call answering a `Status` that `describe()` words as the TS
client threw it; `Menu`, the on-device menu's commands; `Ops`, a file read or written whole and a ROM booted through the
menu with its battery, with one progress callback that cancels between commands. Nothing in it allocates, throws or
uses RTTI, and `rp-device-check` drives it over a scripted cart. `N8Link` and `N8Host` run on it over the desktop's
`SerialTransport` (`WjwwoodSerialPort` renamed); the facet gains its session half; the CLI's raw serial facet
(`SerialRpcService`) and the TypeScript clients (`edio.ts`, `n8Menu.ts`, `transport.ts`, `fakeSerial.ts`) go for
`@retroplug/n8`'s wrapper, and the CLI sessions open the cart through it, their help unchanged. The test host starts the
real provider over `FakeN8`, so a `test:native` session drives `n8-load` through the real facet to a fake cart.

The Edio golden moves into the pack and gains 13 cases recorded from the old TS clients, which the new Edio reproduces
byte for byte; it is placed right after the moves, as the oracle the rest is written to. Nothing builds between the
moves and Step 9.

- [ ] **Step 3: The portable protocol: `Transport`, `Edio`, `Menu`, `Ops`**

`Transport.hpp`: `write` (the bytes taken), `read` (0 on a timeout), `flushInput` and `linkUp()`, with a protected
non-virtual destructor. `Edio`: `Status {code, where, step, device, reply}` with `codeName`, `stepName` and
`describe(status, out, cap, path)`, which formats with its own small writer (newlib's printf family can reach the
heap) and words each failure as the TS client threw it; `Timeouts` per Edio (a reply 2 s, the handshake 300 ms, a file
block 5 s, the menu's install 12 s), overridable per call, with no sticky timeout; one write per frame through a
256-byte scratch, a payload past it in 8 KB writes; a short write fails the command; `listDir` as a visitor over a
256-byte name buffer; and it is not re-entrant. `Menu`: `test`, `install` (the map index out), `start`, `vramDump`
into the caller's arrays and `reset`. `Ops`: `readFile` (a `FileSink`, and a buffer over it), `writeFile`,
`batteryPath` and `bootRom(edio, path, rom, srm, Upload::Always|Never, &mapIndex, progress)`, each status naming its
failed step, the progress answered at stop points between whole commands; an Ops failure leaves the card as it found
it, and only a cancel closes what it opened. The C++ Edio, `N8Menu` and the old serial port's source go; the pack's
CMake builds the new sources into `retroplug-n8` (and so `retroplug-n8-device`) and the new tests into
`retroplug-n8-test`.

Create `packages/n8/native/src/n8/Transport.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The byte pipe the Edio protocol runs over (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 4): the desktop's serial
// port (n8/desktop/SerialTransport.hpp, over deps/serial), the Pico's TinyUSB CDC host, a test's fake cart. Edio knows
// nothing else about where its bytes go: what it takes from a transport is that a write answers how much it took, a
// read how much arrived, and that a link known to be down says so.
//
// Portable, as the protocol over it is: no exceptions (a transport that meets one, as deps/serial's do, catches it and
// answers short, keeping the text for its owner), and a protected non-virtual destructor, since a transport is never
// deleted through this interface and a virtual one makes the deleting destructor reach operator delete. A host that
// owns its transports through a pointer gives them a virtual destructor of its own (the desktop's PortTransport).

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

namespace rp::n8 {

class Transport {
public:
    // Hand the port `size` bytes; the bytes it took. Fewer than `size` is a failure (the port did not take them in its
    // own time, or the link went down), and Edio stops the command there: what follows a part-written command would be
    // parsed by the cart as the rest of it.
    virtual std::size_t write(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) = 0;
    // Up to `size` bytes into `buffer`, waiting up to `timeoutMs` for them (0: only what has already arrived); the
    // bytes that arrived, 0 on a timeout. A short read is not a failure: Edio reads again for the rest, and each read
    // waits its own timeout, so a long reply that keeps arriving never times out.
    virtual std::size_t read(std::uint8_t* buffer, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t timeoutMs) = 0;
    // Drop whatever has arrived and not been read: a late byte would otherwise be taken for the next reply's first.
    virtual void flushInput() = 0;
    // False while the link is known to be down (the Pico's CDC unmount): every wait fails at once rather than running
    // out its timeout against a device that has gone. A port that cannot tell (the desktop's) answers true.
    virtual bool linkUp() const { return true; }

protected:
    ~Transport() = default;
};

}  // namespace rp::n8
````

Create `packages/n8/native/src/n8/Edio.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// krikzz's Edio, the Everdrive N8 Pro's USB protocol (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 4), written once
// for the desktop and the RP2350: the CLI's sessions reach it through the pack's facet (n8/desktop/N8Rpc.hpp), the
// standalone's and the plugin's streaming link and cart jobs run it on their serial thread (n8/desktop/N8Link.hpp,
// N8Host.hpp), and the Pico box runs it over TinyUSB. The N8 speaks it over a CDC serial port, NOT raw passthrough:
// every command is a 4-byte framed header ('+', '+'^0xFF, cmd, cmd^0xFF), arguments are little-endian, and MIDI or a
// save reaches the cart by writing bytes to a device address (CMD_MEM_WR). The flash, RTC and FPGA commands are left
// out. The on-device menu's commands ride on it (n8/Menu.hpp), and the operations of several commands (a file read
// or written whole, a ROM booted) are n8/Ops.hpp's.
//
// It allocates nothing, throws nothing and uses no RTTI: every call answers a Status, values come back through
// out-parameters and caller buffers, and describe() words a failure. Nor is it thread-safe: on the desktop N8Link and
// N8Host serialise every use, and the Pico has one thread. Nor is it re-entrant: the frame being written and the name
// being listed are the object's, so nothing a call runs inside it (a Progress, a listDir visitor, a transport's idle
// hook pumping USB inside a wait) may call the same Edio; a MIDI forward from inside a wait waits for the call. The
// same bytes go out in the same order as the TS and C++ clients it replaced, which edio-golden.json holds
// (packages/n8/native/test).
//
// One write per frame: a command's header, its arguments and as much of its payload as fits a 256-byte scratch in the
// object go out in one Transport::write, and a larger payload follows in further writes. That is the Pico's rule
// (Pico-PIO-USB sends one packet per endpoint per 1 ms frame, so each separate write costs a frame), and on the desktop
// it changes the number of calls and nothing else.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string_view>
#include <type_traits>

#include "n8/Transport.hpp"

namespace rp::n8 {

// What a call came to. Device carries the N8's own status byte (a FatFs error, a menu refusal).
enum class Code : std::uint8_t {
    Ok,
    Timeout,    // a reply did not arrive in its time, or the port did not take a command's bytes
    LinkDown,   // the transport says the link is down (Transport::linkUp)
    BadReply,   // a reply that is not what the protocol answers there
    Device,     // the N8 answered with a non-zero status
    NotFound,   // an operation's file is not on the card (Ops.hpp's readFile)
    Cancelled,  // the progress callback answered false (Ops.hpp)
    TooLarge,   // a string longer than its length prefix, a name longer than asked for, a file larger than its buffer
};

// Where a call failed: what describe() words it by.
enum class Where : std::uint8_t {
    None,
    Write,        // a command's bytes
    Read,         // a reply's bytes
    StatusReply,  // CMD_STATUS's reply, which is <status> A5
    Operation,    // a command's trailing status
    MkDir,        // dirMake's status (8, "exists", is not a failure)
    DirEntry,     // a directory record's own status byte
    FileBlock,    // a file read block's status byte
    WriteAck,     // the ack that releases a file write block
    Name,         // a directory record's name, longer than the 255 bytes the listing asks for
    Length,       // a string longer than the 16-bit length that prefixes it
    Buffer,       // a file larger than the buffer it is read into
    MenuTest,     // the menu's answer to '*t', which is 'k'
    Install,      // the menu's install status
};

// The step of an operation (Ops.hpp) a status comes from; None for a single call.
enum class Step : std::uint8_t { None, Test, Upload, Save, Install, Start, List, Open, Data, Close };

struct Status {
    Code          code   = Code::Ok;
    Where         where  = Where::None;
    Step          step   = Step::None;
    std::uint8_t  device = 0;  // Device: the N8's status byte
    std::uint16_t reply  = 0;  // BadReply: what it answered (the status word, the menu's test byte)

    constexpr bool ok() const { return code == Code::Ok; }
};

// A Status's code as the facet names it ("ok", "timeout", "linkDown", ...), and its step ("test", "upload", ...; ""
// for None).
const char* codeName(Code code);
const char* stepName(Step step);

// The text of a failure, as the TS client this replaced threw it (the CLI prints it, and BlipToaster and the hardware
// lab read it): into `out` (NUL-terminated, cut to `capacity`), its length answered. `path` is the call's path, which
// a few texts name (a mkdir's, an install's, a file not found). "" for Ok.
std::size_t describe(const Status& status, char* out, std::size_t capacity, std::string_view path = {});

// How long each kind of wait lasts, in ms. One table of defaults on every Edio, which a caller may change; a call that
// takes a timeout of its own (0: the table's) overrides it for that call. Each read the transport makes waits this long
// for its bytes, so a long reply that keeps arriving never times out.
struct Timeouts {
    std::uint32_t readMs      = 2000;   // a reply
    std::uint32_t handshakeMs = 300;    // connect's status reply: short, as it is how a port is found to be no N8
    std::uint32_t sdBlockMs   = 5000;   // a file block: a write block's ack, a read block's status and its data
    std::uint32_t installMs   = 12000;  // the menu's install reply, after it loads the ROM and its mapper core off SD
};

// Progress through a transfer, and the one way to cancel it: `step(ctx, done, total)` in bytes, false to cancel. An
// operation takes the answer at its stop points, which are between whole commands (before a file is opened, before
// each block of a file read, before an install); a call made inside a command, as each acknowledged block of a file
// write is, only reports, since the cart takes a command's whole payload once it has asked for it.
struct Progress {
    bool (*step)(void* ctx, std::uint32_t done, std::uint32_t total) = nullptr;
    void* ctx = nullptr;

    bool operator()(std::uint32_t done, std::uint32_t total) const { return !step || step(ctx, done, total); }
};

// A Progress over a callable `f(done, total) -> bool`, which must outlive it.
template <class F>
Progress progressOf(F& f) {
    return Progress{
        [](void* ctx, std::uint32_t done, std::uint32_t total) { return (*static_cast<F*>(ctx))(done, total); },
        const_cast<void*>(static_cast<const void*>(&f))};
}

// One SD-card directory entry, as listDir hands it to its visitor: the name is the Edio's own buffer, valid for the
// call.
struct DirEntry {
    std::string_view name;
    std::uint32_t    size  = 0;
    bool             isDir = false;
};

class Edio {
public:
    // Protocol constants (krikzz Edio).
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_STATUS     = 0x10;  // connect handshake / status poll
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_GET_VDC    = 0x13;  // read board voltages (4x u16: v50, v25, v12, bat)
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_MEM_RD     = 0x19;  // read bytes from a device address
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_SYS_INF    = 0x26;  // read the 64-byte device info (serial, versions, ...)
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_MEM_WR     = 0x1A;  // write bytes to a device address
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_F_DIR_LD   = 0xC5;  // load a directory into the N8 buffer (sorted)
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_F_DIR_SIZE = 0xC6;  // number of records in the loaded directory
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_F_DIR_GET  = 0xC8;  // pull a range of directory records
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_F_FOPN     = 0xC9;  // open a file on the SD card
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_F_FRD      = 0xCA;  // read bytes from the open file
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_F_FWR      = 0xCC;  // write bytes to the open file
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_F_FCLOSE   = 0xCE;  // close the open file
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_F_DIR_MK   = 0xD2;  // make a directory on the SD card
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_F_DEL      = 0xD3;  // delete a file or empty directory
    static constexpr std::uint8_t CMD_F_AVB      = 0xD5;  // free space available on the SD card (u64)
    static constexpr std::int32_t ADDR_PRG      = 0x0000000;  // PRG-ROM PSRAM (8 MB): the same chip the CPU fetches
    static constexpr std::int32_t ADDR_CHR      = 0x0800000;  // CHR-ROM PSRAM (8 MB): the same chip the PPU fetches
    static constexpr std::int32_t ADDR_SRM      = 0x1000000;  // cart battery RAM (SRAM/PRG-NVRAM): a game's .srm
    static constexpr std::int32_t ADDR_MENU_CHR = 0x0FE0000;  // menu CHR (ADDR_CHR 0x800000 + 0x7E0000): screenshot
    static constexpr std::int32_t N8_OS_REGION  = 0x07E0000;  // top of PRG/CHR (0x7E0000..0x800000): the N8 OS's
    static constexpr std::int32_t ADDR_SSR      = 0x1802000;  // save-state sniffer: a running game's live APU/PPU/OAM
    static constexpr std::int32_t ADDR_FIFO     = 0x1810000;  // cart FIFO (NES side reads $40F0/$40F1)
    // The 16-byte FPGA mapper-config block (edn8-pro-pub fpga/base_sv/sys_cfg.sv `scfg`): what the OS told the cart the
    // RUNNING game is - mapper index, PRG/CHR/SRM size masks, mirroring, CHR-RAM-vs-ROM, master volume. Read AND write
    // over USB (HW-verified). Decoded TS-side by @retroplug/n8's mapConfig.ts.
    static constexpr std::int32_t ADDR_CFG     = 0x1800020;
    static constexpr std::size_t  SIZE_CFG     = 16;
    static constexpr std::int32_t ADDR_EXP_VOL = ADDR_CFG + 3;  // expansion-audio master volume (128 = unity)
    // A CHR-RAM cart's RAM is NOT at ADDR_CHR: everdrive.sv forces CHR address bit 22 for a chr_ram game, so the PPU
    // sees the UPPER 4 MB of the CHR chip. That bit is applied only to the console's own fetches (`!dma.req_chr`), so
    // a host read/write over USB has to add this offset itself.
    static constexpr std::int32_t CHR_RAM_OFFSET = 0x400000;
    static constexpr std::size_t  SIZE_CHR_BANK  = 0x2000;   // 8 KB: one CHR bank, the PPU pattern-table window
    static constexpr std::size_t  SIZE_SRM_GAME  = 0x10000;  // 64 KB: the most battery RAM a game uses (risa: 64 KB)
    static constexpr std::size_t  SIZE_SYS_INFO  = 64;
    static constexpr std::size_t  SIZE_VDC       = 8;
    static constexpr int          ACK_BLOCK_SIZE = 1024;  // a file write's ack granularity
    // A file read's block: one CMD_F_FRD per block, as the device's ed_cmd_file_read loops (edn8-pro-pub); at most
    // 512 avoids the cart-FIFO overload the device warns about, which desyncs a multi-block read at 4096.
    static constexpr int          RD_BLOCK_SIZE  = 512;
    // File-open mode flags (FatFs).
    static constexpr std::uint8_t FA_READ          = 0x01;
    static constexpr std::uint8_t FA_WRITE         = 0x02;
    static constexpr std::uint8_t FA_CREATE_ALWAYS = 0x08;
    static constexpr std::uint8_t FS_MAKEPATH      = 0x80;  // create parent dirs if missing
    // The longest name a listing asks for, and the buffer its visitor's name is read into.
    static constexpr std::size_t kNameMax = 255;
    // The frame a command's header, arguments and first payload bytes are written from in one write.
    static constexpr std::size_t kFrameBytes = 256;

    explicit Edio(Transport& transport) : transport_(transport) {}
    Edio(const Edio&)            = delete;
    Edio& operator=(const Edio&) = delete;

    Transport&      transport() { return transport_; }
    Timeouts&       timeouts() { return timeouts_; }
    const Timeouts& timeouts() const { return timeouts_; }

    // The connect handshake: flushInput, then CMD_STATUS, whose reply must be <status> A5 (0 = OK), within
    // `handshakeMs` (0: the table's). The status (which need not be 0) lands in `deviceStatus` when given.
    Status connect(std::uint8_t* deviceStatus = nullptr, std::uint32_t handshakeMs = 0);
    // CMD_STATUS on its own: the reply checked as connect checks it, its status byte into `deviceStatus`.
    Status status(std::uint8_t& deviceStatus, std::uint32_t timeoutMs = 0);

    // The raw 64-byte device-info block (serial, versions, form factor, flash; decoded TS-side by sysInfo.ts), and the
    // 8-byte board-voltage block (four u16: v50, v25, v12, bat). Either works at the menu or in a game.
    Status sysInfo(std::uint8_t (&out)[SIZE_SYS_INFO]);
    Status vdc(std::uint8_t (&out)[SIZE_VDC]);

    // SD file management. freeSpace: bytes free (CMD_F_AVB: two u32, high then low). dirMake: mkdir, an "exists"
    // (status 8) taken as done. fileDelete: remove a file or an empty directory.
    Status freeSpace(std::uint64_t& bytes);
    Status dirMake(std::string_view path);
    Status fileDelete(std::string_view path);

    // Device memory. memWR is fire-and-forget (no status: a failed write is silent, by design); memRD blocks until
    // `size` bytes have arrived. Neither sends anything for a size of 0.
    Status memWR(std::uint32_t addr, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size);
    Status memRD(std::uint32_t addr, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t size);
    // MIDI (or any bytes) to the cart FIFO: memWR to ADDR_FIFO.
    Status fifoWR(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size);
    // A length-prefixed string to the cart FIFO, as two FIFO writes: a 2-byte little-endian length, then the bytes
    // (how the on-device menu receives a path, edlink DeviceIO.FifoTxString).
    Status fifoTxString(std::string_view s);

    // List an SD-card directory, sorted: loaded into the N8's buffer, then every record pulled. `visit(ctx, entry)` is
    // called once an entry, its name in this object's own buffer, so a listing has no capacity of its own; `count`,
    // when given, gets the number of records the N8 said it holds.
    Status listDir(std::string_view path, void (*visit)(void* ctx, const DirEntry& entry), void* ctx,
                   std::uint16_t* count = nullptr);
    template <class F>
    Status listDir(std::string_view path, F&& visit, std::uint16_t* count = nullptr) {
        using V = std::remove_reference_t<F>;
        return listDir(
            path, [](void* ctx, const DirEntry& e) { (*static_cast<V*>(ctx))(e); },
            const_cast<void*>(static_cast<const void*>(&visit)), count);
    }

    // The SD file API. fileOpen(path, FA_WRITE | FA_CREATE_ALWAYS | FS_MAKEPATH), fileWrite, fileClose to write one;
    // fileOpen(path, FA_READ), fileRead, fileClose to read one. fileWrite sends `size` bytes in ACK_BLOCK_SIZE blocks,
    // each released by the cart's 0 ack, then reads the command's status; `progress` reports each block, the command
    // having been asked for (it cannot stop one). fileRead reads `size` bytes as one CMD_F_FRD a RD_BLOCK_SIZE block,
    // each gated by a status byte, with no trailing status; `progress` is asked before each block (false cancels before
    // it: Cancelled, the file still open) and told at the end.
    Status fileOpen(std::string_view path, std::uint8_t mode);
    Status fileWrite(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, Progress progress = {});
    Status fileRead(std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t size, Progress progress = {});
    Status fileClose();

    // Blocking raw reads, with no command sent: a menu's reply (Menu.hpp), which the firmware streams after a FIFO
    // command. `timeoutMs` 0 is the table's readMs.
    Status rx8(std::uint8_t& v, std::uint32_t timeoutMs = 0);
    Status rx16(std::uint16_t& v, std::uint32_t timeoutMs = 0);
    Status rx32(std::uint32_t& v, std::uint32_t timeoutMs = 0);
    Status readData(std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t timeoutMs = 0);

    // Drop any buffered input (reboot garbage before polling the menu, a late ack before a job's reply).
    void flushInput() { transport_.flushInput(); }

private:
    // The frame being built in scratch_: begin() starts a command, the put*s append its arguments, and send() writes it
    // with as much of `payload` as fits, then the rest of `payload` in further writes.
    void   begin(std::uint8_t cmd);
    void   put8(std::uint8_t v);
    void   put16(std::uint16_t v);
    void   put32(std::uint32_t v);
    Status send(const std::uint8_t* payload = nullptr, std::size_t size = 0);
    Status write(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size);
    Status read(std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t timeoutMs);
    // A command that names a path: begin(cmd), the put*s `args` already made, the length, then the path as payload.
    Status sendPath(std::string_view path);
    // CMD_STATUS, and the status a non-zero one is: Device, at `where`.
    Status checkStatus(Where where = Where::Operation);
    std::uint32_t timeout(std::uint32_t ms) const { return ms ? ms : timeouts_.readMs; }

    Transport&   transport_;
    Timeouts     timeouts_;
    std::uint8_t scratch_[kFrameBytes] = {};
    std::size_t  frame_                = 0;
    char         name_[kNameMax + 1]   = {};
};

}  // namespace rp::n8
````

Create `packages/n8/native/src/n8/Edio.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "n8/Edio.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstring>

namespace rp::n8 {

namespace {

// A larger payload than the frame holds goes out in writes of this many bytes, as the clients this replaced chunked it.
constexpr std::size_t kTxBlock = 8192;

constexpr Status fail(Code code, Where where) {
    Status s;
    s.code  = code;
    s.where = where;
    return s;
}

// A value as `digits` lowercase hex digits, as the TS client printed them (toString(16), padStart).
struct Hex {
    unsigned value;
    int      digits;
};

// describe()'s text, built without a formatting library (newlib's printf family can reach the heap): appended into a
// caller's buffer, cut at its capacity and always terminated.
class Text {
public:
    Text(char* out, std::size_t capacity) : out_(out), capacity_(capacity) {
        if (capacity_) out_[0] = '\0';
    }
    Text& operator<<(std::string_view s) {
        for (const char c : s) push(c);
        return *this;
    }
    Text& operator<<(Hex h) {
        static constexpr char kDigits[] = "0123456789abcdef";
        for (int i = h.digits - 1; i >= 0; --i) push(kDigits[(h.value >> (4 * i)) & 0xF]);
        return *this;
    }
    std::size_t size() const { return size_; }

private:
    void push(char c) {
        if (size_ + 1 >= capacity_) return;
        out_[size_++] = c;
        out_[size_]   = '\0';
    }

    char*       out_;
    std::size_t capacity_;
    std::size_t size_ = 0;
};

// How describe() names a step a cancel came before.
std::string_view stepText(Step step) {
    switch (step) {
        case Step::Test: return "the menu test";
        case Step::Upload: return "the upload";
        case Step::Save: return "the save's upload";
        case Step::Install: return "the install";
        case Step::Start: return "the start";
        case Step::List: return "the listing";
        case Step::Open: return "the open";
        case Step::Data: return "the data";
        case Step::Close: return "the close";
        case Step::None: break;
    }
    return {};
}

}  // namespace

const char* codeName(Code code) {
    switch (code) {
        case Code::Ok: return "ok";
        case Code::Timeout: return "timeout";
        case Code::LinkDown: return "linkDown";
        case Code::BadReply: return "badReply";
        case Code::Device: return "device";
        case Code::NotFound: return "notFound";
        case Code::Cancelled: return "cancelled";
        case Code::TooLarge: return "tooLarge";
    }
    return "unknown";
}

const char* stepName(Step step) {
    switch (step) {
        case Step::None: return "";
        case Step::Test: return "test";
        case Step::Upload: return "upload";
        case Step::Save: return "save";
        case Step::Install: return "install";
        case Step::Start: return "start";
        case Step::List: return "list";
        case Step::Open: return "open";
        case Step::Data: return "data";
        case Step::Close: return "close";
    }
    return "";
}

std::size_t describe(const Status& s, char* out, std::size_t capacity, std::string_view path) {
    Text t(out, capacity);
    switch (s.code) {
        case Code::Ok: break;
        case Code::Timeout:
            if (s.where == Where::Write) t << "Edio: serial write timeout (the N8 did not take the command)";
            else t << "Edio: serial read timeout (no N8 response)";
            break;
        case Code::LinkDown: t << "Edio: the N8's USB link is down"; break;
        case Code::BadReply:
            if (s.where == Where::MenuTest)
                t << "N8 menu: unexpected test response 0x" << Hex{s.reply, 2} << " (is the menu running?)";
            else t << "Edio: unexpected status response (" << Hex{s.reply, 4} << ")";
            break;
        case Code::Device:
            switch (s.where) {
                case Where::MkDir: t << "Edio: mkdir error 0x" << Hex{s.device, 2} << " (" << path << ")"; break;
                case Where::DirEntry: t << "Edio: dir read error 0x" << Hex{s.device, 2}; break;
                case Where::FileBlock: t << "Edio: file read error 0x" << Hex{s.device, 2}; break;
                case Where::WriteAck: t << "Edio: tx ack error 0x" << Hex{s.device, 2}; break;
                case Where::Install:
                    // ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: the menu heap is dirty, usually after a prior failed load.
                    if (s.device == 0x44)
                        t << "N8 menu out of memory (0x44) - the menu heap is dirty (e.g. after a prior failed load). "
                             "Power-cycle the console to a fresh menu and retry.";
                    else t << "N8 menu: app install error 0x" << Hex{s.device, 2} << " (path '" << path << "')";
                    break;
                default: t << "Edio: operation error 0x" << Hex{s.device, 2}; break;
            }
            break;
        case Code::NotFound: t << "Edio: file not found on SD: " << path; break;
        case Code::Cancelled:
            t << "Edio: cancelled";
            if (!stepText(s.step).empty()) t << " before " << stepText(s.step);
            break;
        case Code::TooLarge:
            switch (s.where) {
                case Where::Name: t << "Edio: a directory entry's name is longer than the 255 bytes asked for"; break;
                case Where::Buffer: t << "Edio: the file is larger than the buffer it is read into (" << path << ")";
                    break;
                default: t << "Edio: a string longer than 65535 bytes (" << path << ")"; break;
            }
            break;
    }
    return t.size();
}

// --- the frame ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

void Edio::begin(std::uint8_t cmd) {
    scratch_[0] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>('+');
    scratch_[1] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>('+' ^ 0xFF);
    scratch_[2] = cmd;
    scratch_[3] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(cmd ^ 0xFF);
    frame_      = 4;
}

// Every command's arguments fit the frame (the longest, CMD_F_DIR_GET's, is 10 bytes), so these never overflow it.
void Edio::put8(std::uint8_t v) { scratch_[frame_++] = v; }

void Edio::put16(std::uint16_t v) {
    put8(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v));
    put8(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 8));
}

void Edio::put32(std::uint32_t v) {
    put16(static_cast<std::uint16_t>(v));
    put16(static_cast<std::uint16_t>(v >> 16));
}

Status Edio::write(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
    if (!transport_.linkUp()) return fail(Code::LinkDown, Where::Write);
    if (transport_.write(data, size) == size) return {};
    return fail(transport_.linkUp() ? Code::Timeout : Code::LinkDown, Where::Write);
}

Status Edio::send(const std::uint8_t* payload, std::size_t size) {
    const std::size_t first = std::min(size, kFrameBytes - frame_);
    if (first) std::memcpy(scratch_ + frame_, payload, first);
    const std::size_t frame = frame_ + first;
    frame_                  = 0;
    if (Status s = write(scratch_, frame); !s.ok()) return s;
    for (std::size_t off = first; off < size; off += kTxBlock)
        if (Status s = write(payload + off, std::min(kTxBlock, size - off)); !s.ok()) return s;
    return {};
}

Status Edio::sendPath(std::string_view path) {
    if (path.size() > 0xFFFF) {
        frame_ = 0;
        return fail(Code::TooLarge, Where::Length);
    }
    put16(static_cast<std::uint16_t>(path.size()));
    return send(reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(path.data()), path.size());
}

Status Edio::read(std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t timeoutMs) {
    std::size_t got = 0;
    while (got < size) {
        if (!transport_.linkUp()) return fail(Code::LinkDown, Where::Read);
        const std::size_t n = transport_.read(out + got, size - got, timeoutMs);
        if (n == 0) return fail(transport_.linkUp() ? Code::Timeout : Code::LinkDown, Where::Read);
        got += n;
    }
    return {};
}

Status Edio::checkStatus(Where where) {
    std::uint8_t code = 0;
    if (Status s = status(code); !s.ok()) return s;
    if (code == 0) return {};
    Status s = fail(Code::Device, where);
    s.device = code;
    return s;
}

// --- raw reads ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Status Edio::rx8(std::uint8_t& v, std::uint32_t timeoutMs) { return read(&v, 1, timeout(timeoutMs)); }

Status Edio::rx16(std::uint16_t& v, std::uint32_t timeoutMs) {
    std::uint8_t b[2];
    if (Status s = read(b, 2, timeout(timeoutMs)); !s.ok()) return s;
    v = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(b[0] | (b[1] << 8));
    return {};
}

Status Edio::rx32(std::uint32_t& v, std::uint32_t timeoutMs) {
    std::uint8_t b[4];
    if (Status s = read(b, 4, timeout(timeoutMs)); !s.ok()) return s;
    v = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[0]) | (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[1]) << 8) |
        (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[2]) << 16) | (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[3]) << 24);
    return {};
}

Status Edio::readData(std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t timeoutMs) {
    return read(out, size, timeout(timeoutMs));
}

// --- status and device info ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Status Edio::status(std::uint8_t& deviceStatus, std::uint32_t timeoutMs) {
    begin(CMD_STATUS);
    if (Status s = send(); !s.ok()) return s;
    std::uint16_t word = 0;
    if (Status s = rx16(word, timeoutMs); !s.ok()) return s;
    if ((word & 0xFF00) != 0xA500) {
        Status s = fail(Code::BadReply, Where::StatusReply);
        s.reply  = word;
        return s;
    }
    deviceStatus = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word & 0xFF);
    return {};
}

Status Edio::connect(std::uint8_t* deviceStatus, std::uint32_t handshakeMs) {
    transport_.flushInput();
    std::uint8_t code = 0;
    if (Status s = status(code, handshakeMs ? handshakeMs : timeouts_.handshakeMs); !s.ok()) return s;
    if (deviceStatus) *deviceStatus = code;
    return {};
}

Status Edio::sysInfo(std::uint8_t (&out)[SIZE_SYS_INFO]) {
    begin(CMD_SYS_INF);
    if (Status s = send(); !s.ok()) return s;
    return readData(out, sizeof out);
}

Status Edio::vdc(std::uint8_t (&out)[SIZE_VDC]) {
    begin(CMD_GET_VDC);
    if (Status s = send(); !s.ok()) return s;
    return readData(out, sizeof out);
}

Status Edio::freeSpace(std::uint64_t& bytes) {
    begin(CMD_F_AVB);
    if (Status s = send(); !s.ok()) return s;
    std::uint8_t b[8];
    if (Status s = readData(b, sizeof b); !s.ok()) return s;
    const auto u32 = [&](int at) {
        return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[at]) | (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[at + 1]) << 8) |
               (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[at + 2]) << 16) | (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[at + 3]) << 24);
    };
    bytes = (static_cast<std::uint64_t>(u32(0)) << 32) | u32(4);
    return {};
}

Status Edio::dirMake(std::string_view path) {
    begin(CMD_F_DIR_MK);
    if (Status s = sendPath(path); !s.ok()) return s;
    std::uint8_t code = 0;
    if (Status s = status(code); !s.ok()) return s;
    if (code == 0 || code == 8) return {};  // 8: FR_EXIST, the directory is already there
    Status s = fail(Code::Device, Where::MkDir);
    s.device = code;
    return s;
}

Status Edio::fileDelete(std::string_view path) {
    begin(CMD_F_DEL);
    if (Status s = sendPath(path); !s.ok()) return s;
    return checkStatus();
}

// --- device memory -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Status Edio::memWR(std::uint32_t addr, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
    if (size == 0) return {};
    begin(CMD_MEM_WR);
    put32(addr);
    put32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size));
    put8(0);  // exec flag
    return send(data, size);  // fire-and-forget: no status read
}

Status Edio::memRD(std::uint32_t addr, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t size) {
    if (size == 0) return {};
    begin(CMD_MEM_RD);
    put32(addr);
    put32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size));
    put8(0);  // exec flag
    if (Status s = send(); !s.ok()) return s;
    return readData(out, size);
}

Status Edio::fifoWR(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
    return memWR(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(ADDR_FIFO), data, size);
}

Status Edio::fifoTxString(std::string_view str) {
    if (str.size() > 0xFFFF) return fail(Code::TooLarge, Where::Length);
    const std::uint8_t len[2] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(str.size()), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(str.size() >> 8)};
    if (Status s = fifoWR(len, 2); !s.ok()) return s;
    return fifoWR(reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(str.data()), str.size());
}

// --- the SD card -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Status Edio::listDir(std::string_view path, void (*visit)(void* ctx, const DirEntry& entry), void* ctx,
                     std::uint16_t* count) {
    if (count) *count = 0;
    // Load the directory into the N8's buffer (sorted), then pull every record in one range read.
    begin(CMD_F_DIR_LD);
    put8(1);  // sorted
    if (Status s = sendPath(path); !s.ok()) return s;
    if (Status s = checkStatus(); !s.ok()) return s;

    begin(CMD_F_DIR_SIZE);
    if (Status s = send(); !s.ok()) return s;
    std::uint16_t records = 0;
    if (Status s = rx16(records); !s.ok()) return s;
    if (count) *count = records;
    if (records == 0) return {};

    begin(CMD_F_DIR_GET);
    put16(0);  // start index
    put16(records);
    put16(static_cast<std::uint16_t>(kNameMax));  // max name length
    if (Status s = send(); !s.ok()) return s;
    for (std::uint16_t i = 0; i < records; ++i) {
        std::uint8_t resp = 0;
        if (Status s = rx8(resp); !s.ok()) return s;
        if (resp != 0) {
            Status s = fail(Code::Device, Where::DirEntry);
            s.device = resp;
            return s;
        }
        DirEntry      e;
        std::uint16_t date = 0, time = 0, nameLen = 0;
        std::uint8_t  attrib = 0;
        if (Status s = rx32(e.size); !s.ok()) return s;
        if (Status s = rx16(date); !s.ok()) return s;  // unused
        if (Status s = rx16(time); !s.ok()) return s;  // unused
        if (Status s = rx8(attrib); !s.ok()) return s;
        if (Status s = rx16(nameLen); !s.ok()) return s;
        if (nameLen > kNameMax) return fail(Code::TooLarge, Where::Name);
        if (Status s = readData(reinterpret_cast<std::uint8_t*>(name_), nameLen); !s.ok()) return s;
        name_[nameLen] = '\0';
        e.name         = std::string_view(name_, nameLen);
        e.isDir        = (attrib & 0x10) != 0;  // FatFs AM_DIR
        if (visit) visit(ctx, e);
    }
    return {};
}

Status Edio::fileOpen(std::string_view path, std::uint8_t mode) {
    begin(CMD_F_FOPN);
    put8(mode);
    if (Status s = sendPath(path); !s.ok()) return s;
    return checkStatus();
}

Status Edio::fileWrite(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, Progress progress) {
    begin(CMD_F_FWR);
    put32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size));
    if (Status s = send(); !s.ok()) return s;
    const auto total = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size);
    for (std::size_t off = 0; off < size;) {
        std::uint8_t ack = 0;  // the device releases each block with a 0 ack byte
        if (Status s = rx8(ack, timeouts_.sdBlockMs); !s.ok()) return s;
        if (ack != 0) {
            Status s = fail(Code::Device, Where::WriteAck);
            s.device = ack;
            return s;
        }
        const std::size_t block = std::min<std::size_t>(size - off, ACK_BLOCK_SIZE);
        if (Status s = write(data + off, block); !s.ok()) return s;
        off += block;
        progress(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(off), total);  // inside the command: reported, not a stop point
    }
    return checkStatus();
}

Status Edio::fileRead(std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t size, Progress progress) {
    const auto total = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size);
    for (std::size_t off = 0; off < size;) {
        if (!progress(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(off), total)) return fail(Code::Cancelled, Where::FileBlock);
        const std::size_t block = std::min<std::size_t>(RD_BLOCK_SIZE, size - off);
        begin(CMD_F_FRD);
        put32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(block));
        if (Status s = send(); !s.ok()) return s;
        std::uint8_t resp = 0;
        if (Status s = rx8(resp, timeouts_.sdBlockMs); !s.ok()) return s;
        if (resp != 0) {
            Status s = fail(Code::Device, Where::FileBlock);
            s.device = resp;
            return s;
        }
        if (Status s = readData(out + off, block, timeouts_.sdBlockMs); !s.ok()) return s;
        off += block;
    }
    progress(total, total);
    return {};
}

Status Edio::fileClose() {
    begin(CMD_F_FCLOSE);
    if (Status s = send(); !s.ok()) return s;
    return checkStatus();
}

}  // namespace rp::n8
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The on-device Everdrive N8 menu's command channel (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 4). While the N8's
// file-browser menu runs it reads '*'-prefixed commands from the same cart FIFO the MIDI bridge writes to, and replies
// over USB. This drives the menu to install and boot a ROM: the menu firmware itself parses the iNES header, sources
// the standard mapper core from its SD and boots the FPGA; the host does none of that. Only valid while the MENU runs:
// after start() the game runs, and a running game cannot be returned to the menu over USB (the console's reset button
// or a power-cycle does it). Portable, as Edio is: a Status from every call, caller buffers, nothing allocated.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string_view>

#include "n8/Edio.hpp"

namespace rp::n8 {

class Menu {
public:
    static constexpr std::size_t kVramBytes    = 2048;  // 1024 flattened (tileIdx, attr) pairs
    static constexpr std::size_t kPaletteBytes = 16;    // NES master-palette indices

    explicit Menu(Edio& edio) : edio_(edio) {}

    // The handshake: '*t', answered 'k'. Anything else is BadReply (the byte in Status::reply); no answer is a
    // Timeout, which is what a running game gives (it does not read '*' commands).
    Status test();

    // Select a ROM by its SD path: '*n' and the length-prefixed path, answered by a status byte (0 = ok; 0x44 is the
    // menu's out-of-memory, a dirty heap after a failed load) within the install timeout, as the menu loads the ROM and
    // its mapper core off SD first, then the 16-bit map index, into `mapIndex` when given. The index is read at the
    // reply's 2 s, not the install's: the menu sends it straight after the status (the Pico read it so too).
    Status install(std::string_view path, std::uint16_t* mapIndex = nullptr);

    // Boot the installed ROM: '*s'. The menu core drops out and the game runs; nothing answers.
    Status start();

    // The menu's on-screen state: '*v', answered by 2048 VRAM bytes then 16 palette bytes. Pair it with a
    // memRD(ADDR_MENU_CHR, 8192) to rebuild the 256x224 screen (menuImage.ts). Menu-only: test() first for a clean
    // error.
    Status vramDump(std::uint8_t (&vram)[kVramBytes], std::uint8_t (&palette)[kPaletteBytes]);

    // Reboot to the menu: flushInput, '*r', then a best-effort read of its ack (none, or the console already
    // rebooting, is fine: the caller polls test() to learn when the menu is back). Fails only when '*r' could not be
    // written.
    Status reset();

private:
    Status command(char c);

    Edio& edio_;
};

}  // namespace rp::n8
````

````cpp
#include "n8/Menu.hpp"

namespace rp::n8 {

Status Menu::command(char c) {
    const std::uint8_t bytes[2] = {0x2a /* '*' */, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(c)};
    return edio_.fifoWR(bytes, 2);
}

Status Menu::test() {
    if (Status s = command('t'); !s.ok()) return s;
    std::uint8_t resp = 0;
    if (Status s = edio_.rx8(resp); !s.ok()) return s;  // a timeout: the menu is not running (or not listening)
    if (resp == 0x6b /* 'k' */) return {};
    Status s;
    s.code  = Code::BadReply;
    s.where = Where::MenuTest;
    s.reply = resp;
    return s;
}

Status Menu::install(std::string_view path, std::uint16_t* mapIndex) {
    if (Status s = command('n'); !s.ok()) return s;
    if (Status s = edio_.fifoTxString(path); !s.ok()) return s;
    std::uint8_t status = 0;  // the game-select status, once the menu has loaded the ROM and its core off SD
    if (Status s = edio_.rx8(status, edio_.timeouts().installMs); !s.ok()) return s;
    if (status != 0) {
        Status s;
        s.code   = Code::Device;
        s.where  = Where::Install;
        s.device = status;
        return s;
    }
    std::uint16_t index = 0;
    if (Status s = edio_.rx16(index); !s.ok()) return s;
    if (mapIndex) *mapIndex = index;
    return {};
}

Status Menu::start() { return command('s'); }

Status Menu::vramDump(std::uint8_t (&vram)[kVramBytes], std::uint8_t (&palette)[kPaletteBytes]) {
    if (Status s = command('v'); !s.ok()) return s;
    if (Status s = edio_.readData(vram, kVramBytes); !s.ok()) return s;
    return edio_.readData(palette, kPaletteBytes);
}

Status Menu::reset() {
    edio_.flushInput();
    if (Status s = command('r'); !s.ok()) return s;
    std::uint8_t ack = 0;
    (void)edio_.rx8(ack);  // no ack, or already rebooting: fine, readiness is the caller's test() poll
    return {};
}

}  // namespace rp::n8
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The operations of several Edio commands (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 4): a file read or written
// whole and a ROM booted through the menu, shared by the CLI's sessions (through the pack's facet) and the Pico box.
// Each is a fixed sequence of Edio and Menu calls, so its wire is theirs. Each answers a Status whose `step` names the
// step that failed, so a caller keeps its own policy around it: the box skips the upload when its saved CRC matches,
// and re-uploads and retries once when an install fails. One Progress reports the bytes and cancels: its answer is
// taken at the stop points each operation lists, which are between whole commands (Edio.hpp's Progress).
//
// What they leave on a failure is what the failure found: a file a failed call left open stays open (the reply's tail
// may still be on its way, so the caller flushes input and closes it if it goes on), and only a cancel, which comes
// between commands, closes what it opened. Portable, as Edio is.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string_view>

#include "n8/Edio.hpp"

namespace rp::n8 {

// A run of bytes a caller owns, for the length of a call.
struct ByteView {
    const std::uint8_t* data = nullptr;
    std::size_t         size = 0;
};

// Where readFile puts a file once its listing has sized it: `buffer(ctx, size)` answers a buffer of at least `size`
// bytes, or null for none (TooLarge, Where::Buffer, nothing opened). How a caller that can allocate (the facet) reads a
// file it does not know the size of with one listing, as a fixed buffer would need two.
struct FileSink {
    std::uint8_t* (*buffer)(void* ctx, std::size_t size) = nullptr;
    void* ctx = nullptr;
};

// A whole SD file read: its size found by listing its directory (no separate file-info command), the sink asked for a
// buffer that size, then fileOpen(FA_READ), fileRead and fileClose. `size` gets the file's size once the listing has
// found it, so a TooLarge (step List: the listing sized it, nothing opened) says how large a buffer it needs. NotFound
// when the directory holds no file of that name. Stop points: before the open, and before each 512-byte block after
// the first (a cancel there closes the file), each asked once. Steps: List, Open, Data, Close.
Status readFile(Edio& edio, std::string_view path, FileSink sink, std::size_t* size, Progress progress = {});
// The same into `buffer`, `capacity` bytes, as a caller with no heap (the box) reads one.
Status readFile(Edio& edio, std::string_view path, std::uint8_t* buffer, std::size_t capacity, std::size_t* size,
                Progress progress = {});

// A whole file written to an SD path, made with any missing parent directories (FA_WRITE | FA_CREATE_ALWAYS |
// FS_MAKEPATH, which empties a file already there), as one fileWrite. The inverse of readFile. Stop point: before the
// open; each acknowledged block reports. Steps: Open, Data, Close.
Status writeFile(Edio& edio, std::string_view path, ByteView data, Progress progress = {});

// Whether bootRom writes the ROM to the card first, or boots one already there.
enum class Upload : std::uint8_t { Always, Never };

// The SD path the menu loads a game's battery from at its boot (and writes it back to at the next return to the menu):
// EDN8/gamedata/<the ROM's file name>/bram.srm, into `out`. False when it does not fit `capacity` (NUL included).
bool batteryPath(std::string_view romPath, char* out, std::size_t capacity);

// Boot a ROM by driving the menu: test ('*t'), the ROM written to `path` when `upload` is Always, the battery (`srm`,
// when not empty) written to batteryPath(path) so the MENU copies it into cart SRAM at the hand-off (writing the
// cart's SRAM directly over USB corrupts the running menu, which uses that region), install ('*n' and `path`), start
// ('*s'). `mapIndex` gets what the install answered. Progress counts the bytes written, of the ROM and the battery
// together. Stop points: before the test, before each file's open, and before the install. Steps: Test, Upload, Save,
// Install, Start.
Status bootRom(Edio& edio, std::string_view path, ByteView rom, ByteView srm, Upload upload, std::uint16_t* mapIndex,
               Progress progress = {});

}  // namespace rp::n8
````

Create `packages/n8/native/src/n8/Ops.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "n8/Ops.hpp"

#include <cstring>

#include "n8/Menu.hpp"

namespace rp::n8 {

namespace {

Status at(Status s, Step step) {
    s.step = step;
    return s;
}

Status failed(Code code, Where where, Step step) {
    Status s;
    s.code  = code;
    s.where = where;
    s.step  = step;
    return s;
}

// A path's directory and file name, split at its last separator (either kind: the menu takes '/', a Windows caller may
// hand '\\'). Built from the pointer, not substr(), whose range check is a throw a device image may not reference.
std::string_view baseName(std::string_view path) {
    const std::size_t slash = path.find_last_of("/\\");
    return slash == std::string_view::npos ? path : std::string_view(path.data() + slash + 1, path.size() - slash - 1);
}
std::string_view dirName(std::string_view path) {
    const std::size_t slash = path.find_last_of("/\\");
    return slash == std::string_view::npos ? std::string_view{} : std::string_view(path.data(), slash);
}

// One operation's progress inside another's: bootRom's files report their bytes on top of what came before them.
struct Shifted {
    Progress      outer;
    std::uint32_t base  = 0;
    std::uint32_t total = 0;

    Progress progress() {
        return Progress{[](void* ctx, std::uint32_t done, std::uint32_t) {
                            const Shifted& s = *static_cast<const Shifted*>(ctx);
                            return s.outer(s.base + done, s.total);
                        },
                        this};
    }
};

// A Progress that answers its first ask itself (go on) and passes the rest on.
struct SkipFirst {
    Progress outer;
    bool     first = true;

    Progress progress() {
        return Progress{[](void* ctx, std::uint32_t done, std::uint32_t total) {
                            SkipFirst& s = *static_cast<SkipFirst*>(ctx);
                            if (s.first) {
                                s.first = false;
                                return true;
                            }
                            return s.outer(done, total);
                        },
                        this};
    }
};

// The longest battery path batteryPath writes, its NUL included: "EDN8/gamedata/" (14), a FatFs name (at most 255),
// "/bram.srm" (9). bootRom keeps one on its stack, held through the battery's writeFile, whose waits run the Pico's
// idle hook on the SDK's 2 KB stack: exactly this, and no more.
constexpr std::size_t kBatteryPathBytes = 14 + Edio::kNameMax + 9 + 1;

}  // namespace

Status readFile(Edio& edio, std::string_view path, FileSink sink, std::size_t* size, Progress progress) {
    if (size) *size = 0;
    const std::string_view dir   = dirName(path);
    const std::string_view name  = baseName(path);
    bool                   found = false;
    std::uint32_t          bytes = 0;
    const Status listed = edio.listDir(dir, [&](const DirEntry& e) {
        if (!found && !e.isDir && e.name == name) {
            found = true;
            bytes = e.size;
        }
    });
    if (!listed.ok()) return at(listed, Step::List);
    if (!found) return failed(Code::NotFound, Where::None, Step::List);
    if (size) *size = bytes;
    // An empty file needs no buffer (an empty vector's may be null).
    std::uint8_t* const buffer = bytes == 0 ? nullptr : sink.buffer ? sink.buffer(sink.ctx, bytes) : nullptr;
    if (bytes != 0 && !buffer) return failed(Code::TooLarge, Where::Buffer, Step::List);  // sized, nothing opened

    if (!progress(0, bytes)) return failed(Code::Cancelled, Where::None, Step::Open);
    if (Status s = edio.fileOpen(path, Edio::FA_READ); !s.ok()) return at(s, Step::Open);
    // The open's stop point answered for the data's start, so fileRead's own first ask (at 0, before the first block)
    // is not passed on: the caller is asked once at 0, as at every other point.
    SkipFirst skip{progress};
    if (Status s = edio.fileRead(buffer, bytes, skip.progress()); !s.ok()) {
        // A cancel came between two blocks, with nothing owed: the file is closed (best-effort) before it answers.
        if (s.code == Code::Cancelled) (void)edio.fileClose();
        return at(s, Step::Data);
    }
    if (Status s = edio.fileClose(); !s.ok()) return at(s, Step::Close);
    return {};
}

Status readFile(Edio& edio, std::string_view path, std::uint8_t* buffer, std::size_t capacity, std::size_t* size,
                Progress progress) {
    struct Fixed {
        std::uint8_t* buffer;
        std::size_t   capacity;
    } fixed{buffer, capacity};
    const FileSink sink{[](void* ctx, std::size_t bytes) -> std::uint8_t* {
                            const Fixed& f = *static_cast<const Fixed*>(ctx);
                            return bytes <= f.capacity ? f.buffer : nullptr;
                        },
                        &fixed};
    return readFile(edio, path, sink, size, progress);
}

Status writeFile(Edio& edio, std::string_view path, ByteView data, Progress progress) {
    const auto total = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(data.size);
    if (!progress(0, total)) return failed(Code::Cancelled, Where::None, Step::Open);
    const std::uint8_t mode = Edio::FA_WRITE | Edio::FA_CREATE_ALWAYS | Edio::FS_MAKEPATH;
    if (Status s = edio.fileOpen(path, mode); !s.ok()) return at(s, Step::Open);
    if (Status s = edio.fileWrite(data.data, data.size, progress); !s.ok()) return at(s, Step::Data);
    if (Status s = edio.fileClose(); !s.ok()) return at(s, Step::Close);
    return {};
}

bool batteryPath(std::string_view romPath, char* out, std::size_t capacity) {
    constexpr std::string_view kDir  = "EDN8/gamedata/";
    constexpr std::string_view kFile = "/bram.srm";
    const std::string_view     rom   = baseName(romPath);
    const std::size_t          size  = kDir.size() + rom.size() + kFile.size();
    if (size + 1 > capacity) return false;
    std::memcpy(out, kDir.data(), kDir.size());
    std::memcpy(out + kDir.size(), rom.data(), rom.size());
    std::memcpy(out + kDir.size() + rom.size(), kFile.data(), kFile.size());
    out[size] = '\0';
    return true;
}

Status bootRom(Edio& edio, std::string_view path, ByteView rom, ByteView srm, Upload upload, std::uint16_t* mapIndex,
               Progress progress) {
    const std::uint32_t uploaded = upload == Upload::Always ? static_cast<std::uint32_t>(rom.size) : 0;
    const std::uint32_t total    = uploaded + static_cast<std::uint32_t>(srm.size);
    Menu                menu(edio);

    // Confirm the menu is running: a running game does not answer '*t'.
    if (!progress(0, total)) return failed(Code::Cancelled, Where::None, Step::Test);
    if (Status s = menu.test(); !s.ok()) return at(s, Step::Test);

    if (upload == Upload::Always) {
        Shifted shifted{progress, 0, total};
        if (Status s = writeFile(edio, path, rom, shifted.progress()); !s.ok()) return at(s, Step::Upload);
    }
    // The battery goes the native way: into the menu's per-game save slot BEFORE the menu loads the game, so the MENU
    // copies it into cart SRAM at the hand-off.
    if (srm.size != 0) {
        char battery[kBatteryPathBytes];
        if (!batteryPath(path, battery, sizeof battery)) return failed(Code::TooLarge, Where::Length, Step::Save);
        Shifted shifted{progress, uploaded, total};
        if (Status s = writeFile(edio, battery, srm, shifted.progress()); !s.ok()) return at(s, Step::Save);
    }

    if (!progress(total, total)) return failed(Code::Cancelled, Where::None, Step::Install);
    if (Status s = menu.install(path, mapIndex); !s.ok()) return at(s, Step::Install);
    if (Status s = menu.start(); !s.ok()) return at(s, Step::Start);
    return {};
}

}  // namespace rp::n8
````

- [ ] **Step 4: The desktop on the new Edio, and the facet's session half**

`PortTransport.hpp` is the desktop's owned transport (a virtual destructor and the failing call's text,
`failureText()`); `SerialTransport` is the old serial port renamed, its per-read timeout and port listing kept, every
call catching what deps/serial throws and keeping its words, so a failed connect, a job's failure and the link's
`lastError` say what they said. `N8Link` and `N8Host` run on the new Edio, keeping their throw-based control flow
inside and converting statuses at each call; the cart jobs keep their wire exactly (the dump's 512-byte blocks, the
restore's 4 KB commands, the upload's 8 KB commands and its delete on an abort, the job's own words for the menu's
refusals). `N8Rpc.{hpp,cpp}` holds both halves, only `registerRpc` a template: `n8ListPorts`, `n8Open`, the
primitives, the menu's commands and the operations on a handle, and `n8Close`, each answering `{status, deviceStatus,
message, bytes, value, entries, step}`; a call the port itself failed answers `linkDown`; a listing's names reach JS
as TextDecoder decodes them; and the streaming link and a session refuse each other's port, by name or by the device
it resolves to. A device's `fail()` reason is kept to 1024 bytes and cut back to a whole code point
(`CapabilityJobs.hpp`'s `failReason`), and the no-throw rule covers the host's install and clear.

Create `packages/n8/native/src/n8/desktop/PortTransport.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The desktop's transports (n8/Transport.hpp) as its hosts hold them: owned through a pointer (N8Link's port factory,
// the facet's sessions), so with a virtual destructor of their own, and keeping the words of a failure that Edio's
// Status cannot carry. deps/serial reports a failed port by throwing, and a transport answers short instead (Edio
// throws nothing and runs on the device too), so SerialTransport catches the exception and keeps its text here: the
// text N8Link puts in its lastError (Settings > N8 shows it) and a job its failure, as when the throw reached them.

#include <string>
#include <string_view>

#include "n8/Edio.hpp"
#include "n8/Transport.hpp"

namespace retroplug {

class PortTransport : public rp::n8::Transport {
public:
    virtual ~PortTransport() = default;

    // What the port said when its last call failed in the port itself (a deps/serial exception's text), or "" when
    // that call succeeded or only ran out its time. Each call sets it afresh, so after an Edio call that failed it is
    // about the transport call the Edio call stopped at.
    virtual std::string failure() const { return {}; }
};

// The text of a failed Edio call on the desktop: the port's own words when the port failed, else describe()'s.
inline std::string failureText(const rp::n8::Status& status, const PortTransport& port, std::string_view path = {}) {
    if (std::string said = port.failure(); !said.empty()) return said;
    char text[512];
    rp::n8::describe(status, text, sizeof text, path);
    return text;
}

// The same for an Edio a desktop host built, which it always builds over a PortTransport (N8Link's port, a session's).
inline std::string failureText(const rp::n8::Status& status, rp::n8::Edio& edio, std::string_view path = {}) {
    return failureText(status, static_cast<const PortTransport&>(edio.transport()), path);
}

}  // namespace retroplug
````

Create `packages/n8/native/src/n8/desktop/SerialTransport.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "n8/desktop/SerialTransport.hpp"

#include <serial/serial.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cctype>
#include <exception>

namespace retroplug {

namespace {

std::string toLower(std::string s) {
    std::transform(s.begin(), s.end(), s.begin(), [](unsigned char c) { return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(c)); });
    return s;
}

// The N8 Pro presents krikzz's own USB id 38df:0017 - Linux/macOS as "USB VID:PID=38df:0017 ...",
// Windows as "USB\VID_38DF&PID_0017&REV_0200". Match either shape, case-insensitively (a substring
// match, so it works across physical units - the reference did a brittle exact match that baked in one
// unit's serial number).
bool hardwareIdIsN8(const std::string& hwid) {
    const std::string h = toLower(hwid);
    return h.find("38df:0017") != std::string::npos          // Linux / macOS shape
        || h.find("vid_38df&pid_0017") != std::string::npos;  // Windows shape
}

}  // namespace

SerialTransport::SerialTransport(const std::string& portName) : portName_(portName) {
    // 9600 / 8N1, no flow control (all serial::Serial defaults except baud). The initial 2000 ms timeout is a safety
    // net; every read sets its own (read()).
    port_ = std::make_unique<serial::Serial>(portName, 9600, serial::Timeout::simpleTimeout(2000));
}

SerialTransport::~SerialTransport() = default;

bool SerialTransport::isOpen() const { return port_ && port_->isOpen(); }

std::size_t SerialTransport::write(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
    failure_.clear();
    try {
        return port_->write(data, size);
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        failure_ = e.what();
        return 0;
    }
}

std::size_t SerialTransport::read(std::uint8_t* buffer, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t timeoutMs) {
    failure_.clear();
    try {
        // The READ timeout only. serial::Timeout::simpleTimeout(t) sets the write timeout to t as well, and the port
        // has one Timeout for both - so every write inherited the last read's: after a short poll of the back-channel
        // (the reliable link reads with 0 ms) a ~20-byte CMD_MEM_WR timed out part-written, the client then ignored a
        // short write, and the N8's command parser was left mid-command, swallowing everything after it - frames that
        // never landed, then a device that answered nothing (2026-10-22, measured: a 0-1 ms read before a fifoWR, every
        // time).
        serial::Timeout t(serial::Timeout::max(), timeoutMs, 0, kWriteTimeoutMs, 0);
        port_->setTimeout(t);
        return port_->read(buffer, size);
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        failure_ = e.what();
        return 0;
    }
}

void SerialTransport::flushInput() {
    failure_.clear();
    try {
        port_->flushInput();
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        failure_ = e.what();
    }
}

std::vector<N8PortInfo> listSerialPorts() {
    std::vector<N8PortInfo> out;
    try {
        for (const serial::PortInfo& p : serial::list_ports()) {
            N8PortInfo info;
            info.port        = p.port;
            info.description = p.description;
            info.hardwareId  = p.hardware_id;
            info.isN8        = hardwareIdIsN8(p.hardware_id);
            out.push_back(std::move(info));
        }
    } catch (...) {
        // Enumeration failed (no serial subsystem) - return whatever we gathered.
    }
    return out;
}

std::string findN8Port() {
    for (const N8PortInfo& p : listSerialPorts())
        if (p.isN8) return p.port;
    return "";
}

}  // namespace retroplug
````
