Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/n8-session.test.ts`:

````ts
// The CLI's N8 sessions through the real facet, to a fake cart (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 7): this
// host (retroplug-host, packages/native/src/main.cpp) starts the real N8 provider with FakeN8's ports (the model of the
// cart the pack's C++ tests drive, packages/n8/native/test/FakeN8.hpp), so `n8-load` runs here exactly as on the CLI,
// its sessions opened through @retroplug/n8's createN8Client and the protocol run in the host (n8/Edio.hpp): the ports
// it auto-detects, the device info, mkdir, a file put, listed, got back and removed, a ROM booted with its battery
// through the menu, the running cart's config block read back, and the failures the CLI prints in the TS client's
// words. Each run opens and closes its own session, as each CLI process does.
import { test, expect } from "../testing/harness";
import { bootSession } from "../cli/session";
import { n8LoadTool } from "../cli/sessions/n8-load";
import { makeCall } from "../src/rpcClient";
import { createN8Client, N8TimeoutError, ADDR_SSR, decodeSniffer, SNIFFER_REGION_SIZE } from "@retroplug/n8";

const s = bootSession();

// One run of the tool, its console output caught.
function n8Load(...args: string[]): string[] {
  const lines: string[] = [];
  const log = console.log;
  console.log = (...parts: unknown[]) => void lines.push(parts.map(String).join(" "));
  try {
    n8LoadTool.run(s, args);
  } finally {
    console.log = log;
  }
  return lines;
}

const TMP = "/tmp/rp-n8-session-test";
const local = (name: string): string => `${TMP}-${name}`;

test("the facet lists the fake cart's port as an N8, and a session opens on it", () => {
  const client = createN8Client(makeCall());
  expect(client.listPorts()).toEqual([{ port: "fake-n8", isN8: true }]);
  const n8 = client.openN8("fake-n8");
  expect(n8.connect()).toBe(0);
  expect(n8.edio.sysInfo().length).toBe(64);
  expect(n8.edio.vdc().length).toBe(8);
  n8.close();
});

test("n8-load reads the card: info, free space, mkdir, a file put, listed, got back and removed", () => {
  expect(n8Load("--info").some((l) => l.startsWith("serial"))).toBe(true);
  expect(n8Load("--df")).toEqual(["SD free space: 0 (this N8 firmware doesn't report free space via CMD_F_AVB)"]);
  expect(n8Load("--mkdir", "songs")).toEqual(["made directory: songs"]);
  expect(n8Load("--mkdir", "songs")).toEqual(["made directory: songs"]); // an existing directory is done

  const data = new Uint8Array(3000).map((_, i) => (i * 13) & 0xff);
  expect(s.backend.writeFile(local("put.bin"), data)).toBe(true);
  expect(n8Load("--put-file", local("put.bin"), "songs/a.bin")).toEqual([
    `wrote 3000 bytes of ${local("put.bin")} -> songs/a.bin`,
  ]);
  expect(n8Load("--ls", "songs")).toEqual(["songs (1 entry):", "      3000  a.bin"]);
  expect(n8Load("--get-file", "songs/a.bin", local("got.bin"))).toEqual([
    `read 3000 bytes of songs/a.bin -> ${local("got.bin")}`,
  ]);
  expect(Array.from(s.backend.readFile(local("got.bin")) ?? [])).toEqual(Array.from(data));
  expect(n8Load("--rm", "songs/a.bin")).toEqual(["deleted: songs/a.bin"]);
  expect(n8Load("--ls", "songs")).toEqual(["songs (0 entries):"]);
  // What the CLI prints for a file the card does not hold, in the TS client's words.
  expect(() => n8Load("--rm", "songs/a.bin")).toThrow("Edio: operation error 0x04");
  expect(() => n8Load("--get-file", "songs/none.bin", local("none.bin"))).toThrow(
    "Edio: file not found on SD: songs/none.bin",
  );
  s.backend.deleteFile(local("put.bin"));
  s.backend.deleteFile(local("got.bin"));
});

test("n8-load boots a ROM with its battery through the menu, and the running cart answers as a game", () => {
  const rom = new Uint8Array(16 + 32768);
  rom.set([0x4e, 0x45, 0x53, 0x1a, 2, 0, 0x10, 0]); // iNES, mapper 1
  const srm = new Uint8Array(8192).fill(0x5a);
  expect(s.backend.writeFile(local("game.nes"), rom)).toBe(true);
  expect(s.backend.writeFile(local("game.srm"), srm)).toBe(true);
  expect(n8Load(local("game.nes"), "--srm", local("game.srm"))).toEqual([
    `booted 'usb-games/rp-n8-session-test-game.nes' (map index 69) with save ${local("game.srm")}`,
  ]);

  const n8 = createN8Client(makeCall()).openN8("fake-n8");
  try {
    n8.connect();
    // On the card where the menu put them, and the cart's config block names the game's mapper.
    expect(n8.readFile("usb-games/rp-n8-session-test-game.nes").length).toBe(rom.length);
    expect(Array.from(n8.readFile("EDN8/gamedata/rp-n8-session-test-game.nes/bram.srm").subarray(0, 4))).toEqual([
      0x5a, 0x5a, 0x5a, 0x5a,
    ]);
    expect(n8.mapConfig().mapIdx).toBe(69);
    expect(decodeSniffer(n8.edio.memRD(ADDR_SSR, SNIFFER_REGION_SIZE)).magicOk).toBe(false);
    // A running game has no menu: '*t' goes unanswered, which the CLI meets as an N8TimeoutError.
    let thrown: unknown;
    try {
      n8.menu.test();
    } catch (e) {
      thrown = e;
    }
    expect(thrown instanceof N8TimeoutError).toBe(true);
    expect((thrown as Error).message).toBe("Edio: serial read timeout (no N8 response)");
    // The cart's battery written straight and read back, as --sram-only does on a running game.
    expect(n8.writeSramDirect(new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3]))).toBe(3);
    expect(Array.from(n8.dumpSram().subarray(0, 3))).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
  } finally {
    n8.close();
  }
  s.backend.deleteFile(local("game.nes"));
  s.backend.deleteFile(local("game.srm"));
});

test("a session does not open the port the streaming link holds, in the serial client's words", () => {
  const client = createN8Client(makeCall());
  const link = client.link;
  link.connect(true); // auto-picks fake-n8
  try {
    expect(link.linkConfig().connected).toBe(true);
    expect(() => client.openN8("fake-n8")).toThrow("cannot open serial port: fake-n8");
  } finally {
    link.connect(false);
  }
});
````

---

### Task 4: the box on the N8 pack's Edio, a static SOF timer and the link trap on the whole image

Design section 8 and section 10's fourth commit. The Pico box (`pico/n8-host`) becomes C++ and runs the pack's one
Edio: `main.cpp` and `box.cpp` in place of `main.c` and `box.c`, `edio.c` and `edio.h` deleted, and `UsbCdcTransport`,
an `rp::n8::Transport` over TinyUSB's CDC host with what `edio.c` did around its I/O. The boot is the facet's own,
`Ops::bootRom`, which gains `BootOptions` (no handshake of its own, a hook before each step), so the box's wire is
`edio.c`'s byte for byte; `Where::MapIndex` lets it tell a missing map index from a failed install. A remount rebinds
the transport only at the main loop's top level and `BOOT_GONE()` checks the link. The 1 ms SOF timer is the box's
own, and the link wraps `alarm_pool_create_on_timer`, so the whole image links under E1's 87-symbol trap with no heap;
the stack is 4 KB. What the two device projects share moves to `cmake/` (`device-image.cmake`, `reflectcpp-pin.cmake`,
`check-trap.cmake`), and `pnpm device:box` builds both USB variants, in CI beside `device:check`.

Nothing here is flashed or run on the rig: the gate is Task 6's, the controller's. The pack's changes come first and
are proved on the desktop; then the moves, the hoist (proved by `device:check`'s unchanged image), the firmware, its
script and CI step, and the image's own bytes, which must equal the image the gate passed on.

**Files:**

- Create: `cmake/device-image.cmake`, `cmake/reflectcpp-pin.cmake`, `pico/n8-host/SofTimer.cpp`, `pico/n8-host/SofTimer.hpp`, `pico/n8-host/UsbCdcTransport.cpp`, `pico/n8-host/UsbCdcTransport.hpp`, `pico/n8-host/pio_usb_root.c`, `tools/build-box.sh`
- Move (3 files, each by the `git mv` its step prints; 3 of them changed too, `cmake/check-trap.cmake`, `pico/n8-host/box.cpp`, `pico/n8-host/main.cpp`): from `packages/graph-runtime/device-check/`, `pico/n8-host/`
- Modify: `.github/workflows/build.yml`, `.gitignore`, `package.json`, `packages/graph-runtime/device-check/CMakeLists.txt`, `packages/graph-runtime/device-check/N8Protocol.cpp`, `packages/n8/native/src/n8/Edio.hpp`, `packages/n8/native/src/n8/Menu.cpp`, `packages/n8/native/src/n8/Menu.hpp`, `packages/n8/native/src/n8/Ops.cpp`, `packages/n8/native/src/n8/Ops.hpp`, `packages/n8/native/src/n8/desktop/N8Host.hpp`, `packages/n8/native/src/n8/desktop/N8Rpc.cpp`, `packages/n8/native/test/Edio.test.cpp`, `packages/n8/native/test/N8Provider.test.cpp`, `packages/n8/native/test/Ops.test.cpp`, `packages/n8/ts/index.ts`, `packages/n8/ts/test/session-client.test.ts`, `pico/midi-in/midi.h`, `pico/n8-host/CMakeLists.txt`, `pico/n8-host/box.h`, `pico/n8-host/loop.sh`
- Delete: `pico/n8-host/edio.c`, `pico/n8-host/edio.h`

- [ ] **Step 1: The pack's changes for the box**

`Ops::bootRom` takes `BootOptions`, whose defaults are the old behaviour: `handshake` (false leaves out `bootRom`'s
own `*t`, and its stop point) and `before(ctx, step)`, called before each step `bootRom` runs (Test, Upload, Save,
Install, Start), between whole commands with the Edio idle, so unlike a progress callback it may use the Edio; false
stops the boot there as `Cancelled`, with nothing of that step sent. The battery path moves into `writeBattery`, a
never-inlined helper (`__attribute__((noinline))`, `__declspec(noinline)` on MSVC) whose buffer is sized for any FatFs
name (`kBatteryPathBytes`, 14 + 3 x 255 + 9 + 1 = 789), so `bootRom`'s frame drops from 408 bytes to 128 and a boot
without a battery carries no buffer. `Menu::install` reports a missing map index at the new `Where::MapIndex`. From
Task 3's review: `listPorts` answers `[]` for method-not-found alone, a listing's name loses a leading BOM as
TextDecoder drops it, `N8Host`'s port guard says one facet per host, the golden loop checks the map index (`0x45` for
the four boots) and the listings' entries, and a local no longer shadows `::free`. New `Ops.test.cpp` cases hold
`bootRom`'s options (the steps the hook sees, a `box.cfg` written in the Install hook landing between the upload and
`*n`, no `*t`, a stop at Install) and the FatFs bound, and `Edio.test.cpp` tells a missing map index from a failed
install.

````diff
+TEST_CASE("bootRom's options: no handshake, a step hook that may use the Edio, and one that stops the boot",
+          "[n8][ops]") {
+    const Bytes rom = pattern(1500, 6);
+    struct Hook {
+        Edio*             edio = nullptr;
+        std::vector<Step> steps;
+        Step              stopAt = Step::None;
+    };
+    const auto before = [](void* ctx, Step step) {
+        Hook& h = *static_cast<Hook*>(ctx);
+        h.steps.push_back(step);
+        if (step == h.stopAt) return false;
+        // Between whole commands the Edio is idle: a file written here lands between the upload and the install, as
+        // the Pico box's box.cfg does.
+        if (step == Step::Install) {
+            const std::uint8_t cfg[4] = {'N', '8', 'P', 'B'};
+            REQUIRE(rp::n8::writeFile(*h.edio, "usb-games/pico/box.cfg", {cfg, sizeof cfg}).ok());
+        }
+        return true;
+    };
+    {
+        FakeN8     dev;
+        FakeN8Port port(dev);
+        Edio       edio(port);
+        Hook       hook{&edio};
+        REQUIRE(rp::n8::bootRom(edio, "usb-games/b.nes", {rom.data(), rom.size()}, {}, rp::n8::Upload::Always, nullptr,
+                                {}, {false, before, &hook})
+                    .ok());
+        CHECK(hook.steps == std::vector<Step>{Step::Upload, Step::Install, Step::Start});
+        CHECK(dev.booted == "usb-games/b.nes");
+        CHECK(dev.files.count("usb-games/pico/box.cfg") == 1);
+        // No '*t': the install's '*n' is the first FIFO write, after both files.
+        const auto fifo = fifoLog(dev);
+        REQUIRE_FALSE(fifo.empty());
+        CHECK(fifo.front() == "fifo:2A 6E");
+        CHECK(fifo.back() == "fifo:2A 73");
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> l(dev.mu);
+        const auto written = std::count(dev.log.begin(), dev.log.end(), std::string("file-wr"));
+        const auto install = std::find(dev.log.begin(), dev.log.end(), std::string("fifo:2A 6E"));
+        CHECK(written == 2);
+        CHECK(std::count(dev.log.begin(), install, std::string("file-wr")) == 2);
+    }
+    {
+        FakeN8     dev;
+        FakeN8Port port(dev);
+        Edio       edio(port);
+        Hook       hook{&edio, {}, Step::Install};
+        const Status s = rp::n8::bootRom(edio, "usb-games/b.nes", {rom.data(), rom.size()}, {},
+                                         rp::n8::Upload::Always, nullptr, {}, {true, before, &hook});
+        CHECK(s.code == Code::Cancelled);
+        CHECK(s.step == Step::Install);
+        CHECK(hook.steps == std::vector<Step>{Step::Test, Step::Upload, Step::Install});
+        CHECK(dev.files["usb-games/b.nes"] == rom);
+        CHECK(fifoLog(dev) == std::vector<std::string>{"fifo:2A 74"});  // the test alone: no install, no start
+    }
+}
+
````

- [ ] **Step 2: Move the shared trap check and the firmware's two C sources with `git mv`**

`packages/graph-runtime/device-check/check-trap.cmake` moves to the root `cmake/`, beside the hoisted files of the
next step; `pico/n8-host/main.c` and `box.c` become `main.cpp` and `box.cpp`. The device check does not configure
again until Step 3's `CMakeLists.txt` names the moved check, and the firmware not until Step 4.

The moves, as one script (each `git mv` stages its move):

````bash
mkdir -p cmake pico/n8-host
git mv packages/graph-runtime/device-check/check-trap.cmake cmake/check-trap.cmake
git mv pico/n8-host/box.c pico/n8-host/box.cpp
git mv pico/n8-host/main.c pico/n8-host/main.cpp
````

- [ ] **Step 3: What the device projects share, hoisted into `cmake/`**

`cmake/reflectcpp-pin.cmake` holds the reflect-cpp pin (read from rpcpp's `CPMAddPackage` line) and its finder;
`cmake/device-image.cmake` holds `pico_malloc`'s removal from the runtime, the trap list, `rp_device_executable()` and
`rp_device_trap_check()`; `check-trap.cmake` is the post-link check, moved. `rp-device-check`'s `CMakeLists.txt`
includes all three, and its image does not change.

Create `cmake/reflectcpp-pin.cmake`:

````cmake
# reflect-cpp for a device project (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 8): the RP2350 images build
# graph/node.hpp against reflect-cpp's headers (the field reflection graph/fields.hpp compiles against; nothing of it is
# linked), and they are their own CMake projects on the Pico SDK's toolchain, so they find it themselves rather than
# through the desktop's CPM. Included by packages/graph-runtime/device-check and pico/n8-host; sets
# RP_REFLECTCPP_INCLUDE_DIR, which packages/node-sdk's device build puts on its include path.
#
# The version is the desktop's pin, read from where the desktop pins it (rpcpp's CPMAddPackage), so the builds cannot
# drift apart. A checkout the caller names in RP_REFLECTCPP_SOURCE_DIR (the desktop build's, which CI has already
# fetched) must be that version; otherwise a shallow clone of its tag.
get_filename_component(_rp_pin_repo "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/.." ABSOLUTE)
file(READ "${_rp_pin_repo}/deps/dpf.js/deps/rpcpp/CMakeLists.txt" _rp_rpcpp)
string(REGEX MATCH "GITHUB_REPOSITORY[ \t]+getml/reflect-cpp[ \t\r\n]+VERSION[ \t]+([0-9.]+)" _rp_pin "${_rp_rpcpp}")
if(NOT CMAKE_MATCH_1)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "${PROJECT_NAME}: no reflect-cpp pin in deps/dpf.js/deps/rpcpp/CMakeLists.txt")
endif()
set(_rp_reflect_version "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
if(RP_REFLECTCPP_SOURCE_DIR)
    file(READ "${RP_REFLECTCPP_SOURCE_DIR}/CMakeLists.txt" _rp_reflect)
    string(REGEX MATCH "project\\(reflectcpp VERSION ([0-9.]+)" _rp_found "${_rp_reflect}")
    if(NOT CMAKE_MATCH_1 STREQUAL _rp_reflect_version)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "${PROJECT_NAME}: ${RP_REFLECTCPP_SOURCE_DIR} is reflect-cpp ${CMAKE_MATCH_1}, and the "
                            "desktop pins ${_rp_reflect_version}")
    endif()
    set(_rp_reflect_dir "${RP_REFLECTCPP_SOURCE_DIR}")
else()
    include(FetchContent)
    # SOURCE_SUBDIR names a directory the checkout does not have, so the clone is made available without its own
    # CMakeLists being added: the headers are all a device build takes.
    FetchContent_Declare(rp_reflectcpp
        GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/getml/reflect-cpp.git
        GIT_TAG        v${_rp_reflect_version}
        GIT_SHALLOW    TRUE
        SOURCE_SUBDIR  rp-headers-only)
    FetchContent_MakeAvailable(rp_reflectcpp)
    set(_rp_reflect_dir "${rp_reflectcpp_SOURCE_DIR}")
endif()
set(RP_REFLECTCPP_INCLUDE_DIR "${_rp_reflect_dir}/include")
````

Create `cmake/device-image.cmake`:

````cmake
# An RP2350 image under the link trap (docs/modular-graph-phase-e1-design.md section 7, and the E2 design's section 8):
# the runtime with no heap, the trap on the heap, on exceptions and on RTTI, and the post-link check that the trap held.
# Included, after project() and pico_sdk_init(), by both device projects: packages/graph-runtime/device-check
# (rp-device-check) and pico/n8-host (the box's firmware). RP_DEVICE_IMAGE names the including image in what this says.
# Defines rp_device_executable() and rp_device_trap_check().
if(NOT RP_DEVICE_IMAGE)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "device-image.cmake: set RP_DEVICE_IMAGE (the image's name) before including it")
endif()

# --- the runtime: the SDK's pico_stdlib, with pico_malloc taken out of pico_runtime. pico_malloc is the one library
# of the SDK an image cannot have under the trap: it DEFINES the wrapped malloc family (its own --wrap, a heap behind
# it), so with it in the link a call to malloc resolves to its wrapper, the trap fires only further down, at newlib's
# malloc.o, naming that rather than the object that called it, and check-trap.cmake fails the build on the wrapper's
# definition. The rest of what these images link does under the full trap: stdio over the UART and pico_printf among
# them (the SDK wraps puts and printf to its own implementation, which allocates nothing), and stdio over USB too
# (TinyUSB's device CDC, scratch-built against SDK 2.1.1 with its submodules; neither image has it). That holds for
# the SDK's runtime, not for every library: the default alarm pool is static, but alarm_pool_create makes a pool on
# the heap, and a library that calls it (Pico-PIO-USB's host does, at init, unless its config skips the pool, and
# refers to it even then) links only once that reference leads elsewhere (pico/n8-host/CMakeLists.txt).
#
# It is taken out of the SDK's own target, in place, rather than out of a copy of it: every consumer of pico_runtime
# loses it, a library that links pico_stdlib itself (most third-party Pico libraries do) included, and pico_runtime
# keeps everything else it carries, its compile definitions among them. A pico_runtime that no longer links pico_malloc
# stops the configure, as the SDK has moved under it.
if(NOT PICO_SDK_VERSION_STRING STREQUAL "2.1.1")
    message(WARNING "${RP_DEVICE_IMAGE}: built and checked against Pico SDK 2.1.1, and this is "
                    "${PICO_SDK_VERSION_STRING}")
endif()
get_target_property(_rp_runtime_libraries pico_runtime INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES)
if(NOT pico_malloc IN_LIST _rp_runtime_libraries)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "${RP_DEVICE_IMAGE}: pico_runtime no longer links pico_malloc (it links "
                        "${_rp_runtime_libraries}); the Pico SDK's runtime has changed, and what this image removes "
                        "from it must be read again")
endif()
list(REMOVE_ITEM _rp_runtime_libraries pico_malloc)
set_property(TARGET pico_runtime PROPERTY INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES "${_rp_runtime_libraries}")

# --- the link trap. Every symbol through which code reaches the heap or throws is wrapped, and no __wrap_ symbol is
# defined, so a reference to any of them in what the image links is an undefined __wrap_ reference: a link error
# naming the object (and the function) that made it. Every object is compiled with a section per function, so
# --gc-sections (pico_standard_link) means it names what the image keeps, not every function an object happens to
# hold. The C heap is newlib's, and newlib reaches it through its reentrant _r forms as well as the plain ones, so both
# are listed, and sbrk, the break under it; operator new and delete, the C++ runtime's throw path and the
# std::__throw_* helpers the standard headers call are read from the device's own libstdc++ (every variant of each its
# multilib defines), so a variant is never missed for being spelt differently. The function-local static guards
# (__cxa_guard_*) are wrapped too: libsupc++ implements them with a throw, and a device image has no business with
# them (the device product's registration is written to need none).
#
# So is the runtime that exception handling and RTTI reference, so an object compiled with either (a vendored source,
# or one a library adds outside the SDK's -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti) is a link error even where it throws nothing:
# the personality routine and the catch entries a function with a handler or a cleanup references (on ARM a cleanup
# ends in __cxa_end_cleanup; _Unwind_Resume, its form elsewhere, is libgcc's and listed by name), __dynamic_cast, and
# the vtables of the three class type_info kinds a polymorphic class's RTTI points at. __cxa_pure_virtual is not
# trapped: an abstract class compiled without RTTI references it, and a device may have one.
set(_rp_trapped
    malloc calloc realloc free memalign aligned_alloc posix_memalign valloc pvalloc reallocf reallocarray
    malloc_usable_size
    _malloc_r _calloc_r _realloc_r _free_r _memalign_r _valloc_r _pvalloc_r _reallocf_r _malloc_usable_size_r
    sbrk _sbrk _sbrk_r
    __cxa_guard_acquire __cxa_guard_release __cxa_guard_abort
    _Unwind_Resume)
separate_arguments(_rp_cxx_flags UNIX_COMMAND "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS}")
execute_process(COMMAND ${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER} ${_rp_cxx_flags} -print-file-name=libstdc++.a
                OUTPUT_VARIABLE _rp_libstdcxx OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE)
if(NOT IS_ABSOLUTE "${_rp_libstdcxx}" OR NOT EXISTS "${_rp_libstdcxx}")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "${RP_DEVICE_IMAGE}: no libstdc++.a for these flags (${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS}): \"${_rp_libstdcxx}\"")
endif()
# A toolchain upgraded in place re-runs the configure, so the list is read from the library the link uses.
set_property(DIRECTORY APPEND PROPERTY CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS "${_rp_libstdcxx}")
execute_process(COMMAND ${CMAKE_NM} -g --defined-only "${_rp_libstdcxx}" OUTPUT_VARIABLE _rp_nm)
set(_rp_cxx_names
    "_Znw[A-Za-z0-9_]+" "_Zna[A-Za-z0-9_]+"  # operator new and new[]
    "_Zdl[A-Za-z0-9_]+" "_Zda[A-Za-z0-9_]+"  # operator delete and delete[]
    "_ZSt[0-9]+__throw_[A-Za-z0-9_]+"        # std::__throw_*
    "__cxa_(throw|rethrow|allocate_exception|allocate_dependent_exception|free_exception|free_dependent_exception)"
    "__cxa_(init_primary_exception|throw_bad_array_new_length|bad_cast|bad_typeid)"
    # exception handling and RTTI; the type_info vtables are data (R), not code
    "__gxx_personality_v0" "__cxa_(begin_catch|end_catch|end_cleanup)" "__dynamic_cast"
    "_ZTVN10__cxxabiv1[0-9]+__(si_|vmi_)?class_type_infoE")
list(JOIN _rp_cxx_names "|" _rp_cxx_names)
string(REGEX MATCHALL "[ \t][TWR] (${_rp_cxx_names})\n" _rp_cxx "${_rp_nm}")
list(TRANSFORM _rp_cxx REPLACE "^[ \t][TWR] ([^\n]+)\n$" "\\1")
list(REMOVE_DUPLICATES _rp_cxx)
foreach(_rp_required _Znwj _ZdlPv __cxa_throw __cxa_allocate_exception _ZSt17__throw_bad_allocv
                     __gxx_personality_v0 __cxa_begin_catch __cxa_end_catch __cxa_end_cleanup __dynamic_cast
                     _ZTVN10__cxxabiv117__class_type_infoE _ZTVN10__cxxabiv120__si_class_type_infoE
                     _ZTVN10__cxxabiv121__vmi_class_type_infoE)
    if(NOT _rp_required IN_LIST _rp_cxx)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "${RP_DEVICE_IMAGE}: ${_rp_libstdcxx} defines no ${_rp_required}; the trap would miss it")
    endif()
endforeach()
list(APPEND _rp_trapped ${_rp_cxx})
list(LENGTH _rp_trapped _rp_trapped_count)
message(STATUS "${RP_DEVICE_IMAGE}: the link trap wraps ${_rp_trapped_count} symbols")
set(_rp_trap_list "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/trapped-symbols.txt")
list(JOIN _rp_trapped "\n" _rp_trapped_lines)
file(WRITE "${_rp_trap_list}" "${_rp_trapped_lines}\n")
set(_rp_check_trap "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/check-trap.cmake")

# rp_device_executable(<target> <sources>...): an executable as a device builds it: the device-mode flags, the runtime
# and the trap. One --wrap a symbol: -Wl, splits at commas, so a joined list would hand the linker the symbols as input
# files.
function(rp_device_executable target)
    add_executable(${target} ${ARGN})
    set_target_properties(${target} PROPERTIES CXX_STANDARD 20 CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
    target_compile_definitions(${target} PRIVATE RP_DEVICE)
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-fno-exceptions;-fno-rtti>")
    target_link_libraries(${target} PRIVATE pico_stdlib)
    list(TRANSFORM _rp_trapped PREPEND "LINKER:--wrap=" OUTPUT_VARIABLE _wrap)
    target_link_options(${target} PRIVATE ${_wrap})
endfunction()

# rp_device_trap_check(<target>): the trap's second half on <target>'s linked image. None of the wrapped symbols may be
# defined (a library that defined one, as pico_malloc does the malloc family's, would turn the trap into a heap), and
# none may be referred to and left undefined (a link option that tolerates one). Both are checked on the linked image,
# which fails the build when either holds.
function(rp_device_trap_check target)
    add_custom_command(TARGET ${target} POST_BUILD
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -DNM=${CMAKE_NM} -DIMAGE=$<TARGET_FILE:${target}> -DTRAPPED=${_rp_trap_list}
                -P "${_rp_check_trap}"
        VERBATIM)
endfunction()
````

- [ ] **Step 4: The firmware in C++ on the pack**

`UsbCdcTransport` implements `rp::n8::Transport` over TinyUSB's CDC host: each wait pumps `tuh_task` and `box_feed`
(the watchdog and the LED), a best-effort 500 ms drain after a write, a 20 ms quiet input flush, a 2 s write stall,
`linkUp()` from the mount state; one transport and one Edio live in static storage. The probe is `status` and
`sysInfo`; the menu handshake `flushInput` then `Menu::test`; `box.cfg` a plain `fileOpen`, `fileRead(16)` and an
always-sent `fileClose`, its save `Ops::writeFile`; the boot `bootRom(path, rom when uploading, {}, Always or Never,
nullptr, {}, {false, boot_step, &run})`, whose hook prints each line where the old firmware printed it and saves
`box.cfg` before the install; the expansion-volume check, the sniff, the MIDI batches and the health check `memRD`,
`memWR`, `fifoWR` and `status`. The unmount callback unbinds the transport, the mount callback only records the CDC
index, the main loop binds it before the new N8's probe, and `BOOT_GONE()` is `n8_gen != gen || !n8_ready ||
!usb.linkUp()`. `SofTimer` claims hardware alarm 2 of the default timer (`TIMER0_IRQ_2`, priority `0x80`, an absolute
1000 us cadence with catch-up, the first frame armed from a forced IRQ, the handler in RAM), and defines the
`alarm_pool_create_on_timer` wrapper as a `panic()` that never runs. `pio_usb_root.c` is a one-function C shim, since
`pio_usb_ll.h` does not compile as C++; `midi.h` gains `extern "C"` guards and `box.h` takes the `Edio&`. The
`CMakeLists.txt` is `retroplug_product(n8-host DEVICE PACKAGES n8 TARGETS n8_host)` on the hoisted files, with the
wrap, `PICO_STACK_SIZE=0x1000` and `PICO_CORE1_STACK_SIZE=0x800`, its own trap probe, and `main` naming the registered
node types at boot, so `rp.n8.nes` is in the image the trap judges. `loop.sh` hands a fresh build dir the desktop
build's reflect-cpp checkout. Every log string the gate's scripts match is printed where it was.

Create `pico/n8-host/UsbCdcTransport.hpp`:

````cpp
// The N8's Edio link on the Pico (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 8): rp::n8::Transport over TinyUSB's
// CDC host, so the box runs the pack's one Edio (packages/n8/native/src/n8/Edio.hpp) over the N8 in its USB socket.
//
// Each wait pumps the USB host (tuh_task) and the box's idle hook (box_feed: the watchdog and the status LED), never a
// bare sleep, so the long ones (a ROM upload, the menu loading a ROM off the SD for up to 12 s) keep the box alive.
// So it runs from the main loop alone, never from a tuh_* callback, and nothing the hook does may call the Edio over
// it.
//
// The link is up from bind() to unbind(). unbind() is the CDC unmount's (tuh_cdc_umount_cb, which fires inside a
// pump); bind() is the main loop's, before the probe of a new mount, so it never happens inside a wait. From an
// unmount until the box binds the next N8, every wait fails at once (linkUp() false) instead of running out its timeout
// against a device that has gone, and a call that was mid-command when its N8 went can never carry on into the next
// one: the new N8 hears nothing until the box has started over at its probe.
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "n8/Transport.hpp"

class UsbCdcTransport final : public rp::n8::Transport {
public:
    // How long a write may go without the TX FIFO taking a byte, the best-effort wait for a write's bytes to leave,
    // and the silence that ends an input flush: the C Edio's values, which the baseline was measured with.
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kWriteMs      = 2000;
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kDrainMs      = 500;
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kFlushQuietMs = 20;

    // Constant-initialised, so the box's one transport is in static storage with nothing run to make it.
    explicit constexpr UsbCdcTransport(void (*idle)()) : idle_(idle) {}

    // The N8's CDC interface, from its mount: the link is up until unbind().
    void bind(std::uint8_t cdcIndex) {
        idx_ = cdcIndex;
        up_  = true;
    }
    void unbind() { up_ = false; }

    // All of `size` once TinyUSB has taken it, then a wait of up to kDrainMs for the TX FIFO to drain (a short write
    // under a packet does not go out by itself, and a flush is a no-op while the endpoint is busy, so the bytes are
    // flushed until they have left). The drain is best effort: still queued at kDrainMs is a success. Short when the
    // FIFO took nothing for kWriteMs, and 0 when the link went down before the bytes left.
    std::size_t write(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) override;
    // What arrives within `timeoutMs`, counted from the call (0: one pump, and the bytes it found): whatever has come
    // when nothing more is waiting, so Edio reads again for the rest and each wait counts from the last arrival.
    std::size_t read(std::uint8_t* buffer, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t timeoutMs) override;
    // Drops input until kFlushQuietMs pass with nothing arriving.
    void flushInput() override;
    bool linkUp() const override { return up_; }

private:
    void pump() const;

    void (*idle_)();
    std::uint8_t idx_ = 0;
    // Cleared by the unmount callback inside a pump, set by the main loop: both on the one thread, so no fence.
    bool up_ = false;
};
````

Create `pico/n8-host/UsbCdcTransport.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "UsbCdcTransport.hpp"

#include "pico/time.h"
// TinyUSB's osal_none.h applies ++ and -- to a volatile, which C++20 deprecates: its warning, not this file's.
#pragma GCC diagnostic push
#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wvolatile"
#include "tusb.h"
#pragma GCC diagnostic pop

namespace {

std::uint32_t nowMs() { return to_ms_since_boot(get_absolute_time()); }

}  // namespace

// Every wait pumps the USB host and the idle hook, which keeps the watchdog fed and the status LED alive through the
// long ones. The unmount callback runs in here, so each caller looks at the link after it.
void UsbCdcTransport::pump() const {
    tuh_task();
    if (idle_) idle_();
}

std::size_t UsbCdcTransport::write(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
    const std::uint32_t idleFree = tuh_cdc_write_available(idx_);  // the TX FIFO's free space with nothing queued
    std::size_t         sent     = 0;
    std::uint32_t       start    = nowMs();
    while (sent < size) {
        pump();
        if (!up_) return sent;
        const std::uint32_t n = tuh_cdc_write(idx_, data + sent, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size - sent));
        if (n) {
            sent += n;
            tuh_cdc_write_flush(idx_);
            start = nowMs();
        } else if (nowMs() - start > kWriteMs) {
            return sent;
        }
    }
    // The FIFO's free space back at what it was is the transfer done.
    start = nowMs();
    while (nowMs() - start < kDrainMs) {
        pump();
        if (!up_) return 0;
        tuh_cdc_write_flush(idx_);
        if (tuh_cdc_write_available(idx_) >= idleFree) return size;
    }
    return size;
}

std::size_t UsbCdcTransport::read(std::uint8_t* buffer, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t timeoutMs) {
    std::size_t         got   = 0;
    const std::uint32_t start = nowMs();
    for (;;) {
        pump();
        if (!up_) return got;
        const std::uint32_t n = tuh_cdc_read(idx_, buffer + got, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size - got));
        got += n;
        if (got == size || (n == 0 && got != 0)) return got;
        if (n == 0 && (timeoutMs == 0 || nowMs() - start > timeoutMs)) return 0;
    }
}

void UsbCdcTransport::flushInput() {
    std::uint8_t  drop[64];
    std::uint32_t quietSince = nowMs();
    while (nowMs() - quietSince < kFlushQuietMs) {
        pump();
        if (!up_) return;
        if (tuh_cdc_read(idx_, drop, sizeof drop)) quietSince = nowMs();
    }
}
````

````cpp
// Pico-PIO-USB's 1 ms start-of-frame timer, made with nothing allocated (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section
// 8). The host runs every transaction from pio_usb_host_frame(), which something must call once a millisecond: its own
// init makes an alarm pool for that, alarm_pool_create(2, 1), on the heap. The box's image has no heap (the link trap,
// CMakeLists.txt), so its configuration skips the pool (skip_alarm_pool) and the box drives the frame itself, from
// hardware alarm 2 on the default timer, with the IRQ, the priority and the absolute 1000 us cadence the pool's
// repeating timer had (SofTimer.cpp says how each is matched).
#pragma once

// Claims hardware alarm 2 and starts the frames, the first 1000 us from now. Once, after tuh_init() has initialised
// the PIO-USB host (pio_usb_host_frame() reads its state).
void sof_timer_start();
````

Create `pico/n8-host/SofTimer.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "SofTimer.hpp"

#include <cstdint>

#include "hardware/irq.h"
#include "hardware/sync.h"
#include "hardware/timer.h"
#include "pico/platform.h"
#include "pico/time.h"
#include "pio_usb.h"

// What alarm_pool_create(2, 1) and Pico-PIO-USB's alarm_pool_add_repeating_timer_us(pool, -1000, sof_timer, ...) gave
// the frame, read from Pico SDK 2.1.1 (pico_time/time.c and pico_time_adapter's time_adapter.h), and how each is kept:
//   - the alarm and its IRQ: hardware alarm 2 of the default timer (alarm_pool_get_default_timer()), TIMER0_IRQ_2 on
//     the RP2350, claimed, its IRQ an exclusive handler, its bit set in INTE (ta_enable_irq_handler). The same here.
//   - the priority: the pool sets none, so its IRQ keeps the PICO_DEFAULT_IRQ_PRIORITY (0x80) the runtime gives every
//     IRQ at boot. Set here explicitly to that value, above the MIDI UART's PICO_LOWEST_IRQ_PRIORITY, as before.
//   - the cadence: a negative delay repeats "from the last fire time", so each frame's target is the last target plus
//     1000 us, on an absolute schedule that never drifts by the handler's own time; a handler that finds the next
//     target already passed (it ran late) fires again at once, in the same IRQ, until it is ahead (the pool's do-while,
//     which also keeps a past target from being armed: the alarm matches on the timer's low 32 bits, so it would next
//     fire after a wrap). The first frame is 1000 us after the start (make_timeout_time_us(1000)), armed from the IRQ
//     itself, which the pool forces to insert a new alarm. The same here, the force bit cleared on entry as the pool's
//     handler does, and the SEV at its end kept (it wakes a WFE on the other core; the box has none, and it costs
//     nothing).
//   - the code path: the pool's handler ran from flash and called sof_timer and pio_usb_host_frame, both in RAM; this
//     handler is in RAM too, so a frame never waits on a flash fetch.
namespace {

constexpr unsigned     kAlarm   = 2;
constexpr std::int64_t kFrameUs = 1000;

// The next frame's time in microseconds since boot: the pool entry's `target`. Written only by the IRQ once started.
std::int64_t gTarget = 0;

std::int64_t now() { return static_cast<std::int64_t>(timer_time_us_64(timer_hw)); }

void __not_in_flash_func(sofIrq)() {
    hw_clear_bits(&timer_hw->intf, 1u << kAlarm);
    std::int64_t target = 0;
    do {
        timer_hw->intr = 1u << kAlarm;
        if (now() - gTarget >= 0) {
            pio_usb_host_frame();
            gTarget += kFrameUs;
        }
        target                  = gTarget;
        timer_hw->alarm[kAlarm] = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(target);
    } while (target - now() <= 0);
    __sev();
}

}  // namespace

void sof_timer_start() {
    hardware_alarm_claim(kAlarm);  // a second claim panics, as the pool's did
    const unsigned irq = hardware_alarm_get_irq_num(kAlarm);
    timer_hw->armed    = 1u << kAlarm;  // disarmed until the first target is set
    gTarget            = now() + kFrameUs;  // before the IRQ can run, so the force below is all that starts it
    irq_set_exclusive_handler(irq, sofIrq);
    irq_set_priority(irq, PICO_DEFAULT_IRQ_PRIORITY);
    irq_set_enabled(irq, true);
    hw_set_bits(&timer_hw->inte, 1u << kAlarm);
    hw_set_bits(&timer_hw->intf, 1u << kAlarm);  // the IRQ arms the first frame
}

// Pico-PIO-USB's init calls alarm_pool_create(2, 1) unless its config skips the pool, so the call is in the image even
// though the box's config skips it, and the SDK's pool is made with malloc and calloc, which the link trap refuses.
// CMakeLists.txt therefore wraps alarm_pool_create_on_timer (what the inline alarm_pool_create calls) to this, which
// never runs: reaching it means the configuration lost skip_alarm_pool, and the box would have no frames.
extern "C" alarm_pool_t* __wrap_alarm_pool_create_on_timer(alarm_pool_timer_t*, uint, uint) {
    panic("alarm_pool_create: the box's PIO-USB config skips the pool (SofTimer.cpp drives the frames)");
}
````

- [ ] **Step 5: `pnpm device:box`**

`tools/build-box.sh` builds the firmware in both USB variants (PIO-USB, the rig's, and `RP_NATIVE_USB=ON`), each in a
build dir of its own under `build-box/` (now in `.gitignore`), proves each variant's probe fails to link naming its
own object, and prints the image's sizes; it carries no UF2 (`-DPICO_NO_PICOTOOL=1`). Its SDK rule is `loop.sh`'s:
`PICO_SDK_PATH` when it carries TinyUSB, else `/workspaces/pico-sdk`, said aloud.

Create `tools/build-box.sh`:

````bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Builds the Pico box's firmware (pico/n8-host, docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 8), the MIDI-to-N8 bridge
# that runs the N8 pack's Edio, in both of its USB variants, each under the link trap on the heap, on exceptions and on
# RTTI (cmake/device-image.cmake), and prints what each costs in flash and RAM. CI's linux-x64 job runs it beside
# tools/build-device-check.sh; nothing is flashed or run (the hardware gate runs pico/n8-host/loop.sh, stress.sh and
# faults.sh on the rig).
#
#   1. For each variant, PIO-USB (the rig's: the N8 on GP2/GP3) and RP_NATIVE_USB=ON (the chip's own controller):
#      configures the firmware's CMake project on the Pico SDK's toolchain, in a build dir of its own, and builds it.
#      A link error there naming __wrap_<symbol> is the trap: the object it names reached the heap or a throw.
#   2. Builds the variant's trap probe (n8_host_trap_probe: the firmware's libraries and one source that allocates with
#      new and malloc), and stops unless its link FAILS naming its own object for __wrap__Znwj and __wrap_malloc.
#   3. Prints the image's allocated sections (arm-none-eabi-size -A) and its flash, data and bss.
#
# The ELF is the artifact: no UF2 (PICO_NO_PICOTOOL, as the SDK would otherwise fetch and build picotool). loop.sh's
# own build dirs (pico/n8-host/build, build-native, ...) are left alone.
#
# Usage:  tools/build-box.sh                 (pnpm device:box)
#   PICO_SDK_PATH         the Pico SDK (2.1.1) with its lib/tinyusb submodule; when unset, or an SDK without TinyUSB,
#                         /workspaces/pico-sdk (loop.sh's rule). A path that is set and is no SDK stops the run.
#   PICO_PIO_USB_PATH     a Pico-PIO-USB checkout (5a37a66); when unset, /workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB.
#   RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR  a configured desktop build whose reflect-cpp checkout saves a clone (default build/; optional)
#   RP_BOX_BUILD_DIR      the build dirs' parent (default build-box/: pio/ and native/ under it)
#   RP_BOX_BUILD_TYPE     default Release (the SDK's default: -O3, NDEBUG)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
DESKTOP="${RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR:-$REPO_DIR/build}"
OUT="${RP_BOX_BUILD_DIR:-$REPO_DIR/build-box}"
TYPE="${RP_BOX_BUILD_TYPE:-Release}"
JOBS="$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 4)"

die() { echo "build-box: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

# The SDK is loop.sh's: PICO_SDK_PATH when it carries TinyUSB, else /workspaces/pico-sdk (the devcontainer's image
# bakes an SDK without submodules at /opt/pico-sdk and points PICO_SDK_PATH at it), said aloud when it falls back. A
# path that is set and is no SDK at all stops the run, as does a Pico-PIO-USB named that is not one: a wrong path never
# quietly builds against another checkout.
sdk=/workspaces/pico-sdk
if [ -n "${PICO_SDK_PATH:-}" ]; then
    [ -e "$PICO_SDK_PATH/pico_sdk_init.cmake" ] || die "PICO_SDK_PATH ($PICO_SDK_PATH) is not a Pico SDK"
    if [ -e "$PICO_SDK_PATH/lib/tinyusb/src/tusb.h" ]; then
        sdk=$PICO_SDK_PATH
    else
        echo "build-box: PICO_SDK_PATH ($PICO_SDK_PATH) has no TinyUSB submodule; using $sdk, as loop.sh does"
    fi
fi
[ -e "$sdk/pico_sdk_init.cmake" ] || die "no Pico SDK: set PICO_SDK_PATH (the default, $sdk, is not one)"
[ -e "$sdk/lib/tinyusb/src/tusb.h" ] ||
    die "$sdk has no TinyUSB (git -C $sdk submodule update --init lib/tinyusb)"
pio_usb=${PICO_PIO_USB_PATH:-/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB}
[ -e "$pio_usb/src/pio_usb.h" ] || die "PICO_PIO_USB_PATH ($pio_usb) is not a Pico-PIO-USB checkout"
command -v arm-none-eabi-g++ >/dev/null ||
    die "no arm-none-eabi-g++ (apt: gcc-arm-none-eabi libnewlib-arm-none-eabi libstdc++-arm-none-eabi-newlib)"

# reflect-cpp at the desktop's pin: the desktop build's own checkout when there is one (the firmware's CMakeLists checks
# its version against the pin either way, and clones the pinned tag without it).
reflect=
[ -f "$DESKTOP/CMakeCache.txt" ] && reflect="$(sed -n 's/^reflectcpp_SOURCE_DIR:STATIC=//p' "$DESKTOP/CMakeCache.txt")"

for variant in pio native; do
    dir="$OUT/$variant"
    native=OFF
    [ "$variant" = native ] && native=ON
    generator=()
    command -v ninja >/dev/null && [ ! -f "$dir/CMakeCache.txt" ] && generator=(-G Ninja)

    echo "== the firmware, $variant (RP_NATIVE_USB=$native; Pico SDK $sdk, $TYPE)"
    cmake -S "$REPO_DIR/pico/n8-host" -B "$dir" ${generator[@]+"${generator[@]}"} \
        -DPICO_SDK_PATH="$sdk" -DPICO_PIO_USB_PATH="$pio_usb" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE="$TYPE" -DRP_NATIVE_USB="$native" \
        -DPICO_NO_PICOTOOL=1 ${reflect:+-DRP_REFLECTCPP_SOURCE_DIR="$reflect"}
    cmake --build "$dir" -j"$JOBS"

    echo "== the trap's positive control, $variant (n8_host_trap_probe must not link)"
    probe_log="$dir/trap-probe.log"
    if cmake --build "$dir" --target n8_host_trap_probe -j"$JOBS" >"$probe_log" 2>&1; then
        die "n8_host_trap_probe LINKED: the link trap is not reaching the firmware's link ($probe_log)"
    fi
    for symbol in __wrap__Znwj __wrap_malloc; do
        grep -q "trap-probe\.cpp\.o: in function .main.:" "$probe_log" &&
            grep -q "undefined reference to .$symbol'" "$probe_log" ||
            die "n8_host_trap_probe failed, but not with its own object's reference to $symbol ($probe_log)"
    done
    grep -E "trap-probe\.cpp\.o: in function|undefined reference" "$probe_log" | sed 's/^.*ld: //; s/^/  /'

    elf="$dir/n8_host.elf"
    [ -f "$elf" ] || die "no $elf"
    echo
    echo "== $elf: allocated sections"
    arm-none-eabi-size -A "$elf" | awk 'NR <= 2 || ($2 > 0 && $3 > 0)'
    # Flash is code and constants; data is initialised RAM (its image in flash too, RAM-resident code among it); bss
    # is zeroed RAM. The SDK's reserved heap and stack sections are counted in none of them.
    arm-none-eabi-size -A "$elf" | awk -v variant="$variant" '
        $1 == ".text" || $1 == ".rodata" || $1 == ".ARM.exidx" || $1 == ".binary_info" || $1 == ".flash_end" { f += $2 }
        $1 == ".data" || $1 == ".tdata" { d += $2 }
        $1 == ".bss" || $1 == ".tbss" || $1 == ".ram_vector_table" || $1 == ".uninitialized_data" { b += $2 }
        $1 ~ /^\.scratch_/ { b += $2 }
        END { printf "== %s: flash %d, data %d, bss %d bytes\n", variant, f, d, b }'
    echo
done
````

- [ ] **Step 6: Show that the alarm-pool wrap is what keeps the heap out**

`skip_alarm_pool` alone is not enough: `pio_usb_host_init` still contains the call `alarm_pool_create(2, 1)` behind
its `if`, and the SDK makes that pool with `malloc` and `calloc`. Apply this temporary mutation, which drops the wrap,
and the PIO-USB image must fail to link under the trap; then reverse it and build again.

````patch
diff --git a/pico/n8-host/CMakeLists.txt b/pico/n8-host/CMakeLists.txt
--- a/pico/n8-host/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/pico/n8-host/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -85,7 +85,6 @@
         # pio_usb_host_init calls alarm_pool_create unless its config skips the pool, so the call is linked even
         # though the box's config skips it, and the SDK makes that pool with malloc and calloc. The wrap points the
         # call at a stub that never runs (SofTimer.cpp), which leaves the SDK's pool function, and the heap, out.
-        target_link_options(${target} PRIVATE "LINKER:--wrap=alarm_pool_create_on_timer")
     endif()
     # -DN8_TUSB_DEBUG=2 traces TinyUSB's attach / enumeration on the console - the first thing to
     # look at when the N8 never mounts (no attach line at all = nothing electrical on D+/D-).
````

- [ ] **Step 7: The rig's image, built as `loop.sh` builds it, and its bytes**

The gate ran on the prototype's image, and Task 6 runs it again; this step proves the tree builds that very image.
Build in `loop.sh`'s own build dir (`pico/n8-host/build`, PIO-USB, no `-D` overrides) without flashing anything:
configure only if it has no `build.ninja`, with the desktop build's reflect-cpp checkout as `loop.sh` passes it.

Run: `bash -c 'b=pico/n8-host/build; if [ ! -f $b/build.ninja ]; then r=$(sed -n "s/^reflectcpp_SOURCE_DIR:STATIC=//p" build/CMakeCache.txt); PICO_SDK_PATH=/workspaces/pico-sdk cmake -S pico/n8-host -B $b -G Ninja -DRP_NATIVE_USB=OFF ${r:+-DRP_REFLECTCPP_SOURCE_DIR=$r}; fi; cmake --build $b -j$(nproc)'`
Expected: exit 0 (a dir configured before re-runs its configure itself; its warnings are the SDK's).

The image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string (the
gate image holds `Nov 4 2026`). So the check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it
normalised to `Nov 4 2026`, the gate's day; nothing else may differ, and the sizes `device:box` prints do not move
with the date.

Run: `bash -c 'R="(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) [ 0-9][0-9] 20[0-9]{2}"; for e in pico/n8-host/build/n8_host.elf build-box/pio/n8_host.elf; do arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary $e /tmp/e2-box.bin && LC_ALL=C grep -a -c -E "$R" /tmp/e2-box.bin && LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/$R/Nov  4 2026/" /tmp/e2-box.bin | sha256sum; done; rm -f /tmp/e2-box.bin'`
Expected: for each image, `1` (one build-date string) and then `10a6b09edb9931b3652a06d891102277fcef9d24a3e0af20725dfd56b78bf0da  -`: the flashed bytes of the image the gate passed on, but for the day it was built (the report: Its `objcopy -O binary` sha256 is `10a6b09edb9931b3652a06d891102277fcef9d24a3e0af20725dfd56b78bf0da`, the same as the gate image (567c0fab9), and `build-box/pio` gives the same hash., both built on 2026-11-04). A count other than 1, or a different hash, is a finding: stop and report it, since the gate would then not cover this tree.

- [ ] **Step 9: The CI steps, and a dry run of them**

CI's linux job gains two steps after `device:check`: the first initialises the CI's pico-sdk 2.1.1 clone's
`lib/tinyusb` at depth 1 and fetches Pico-PIO-USB at `5a37a66dc5d3fbe0ef3cdbeda923a757440f984f` at depth 1, the second
runs `pnpm device:box` with `PICO_SDK_PATH` and `PICO_PIO_USB_PATH`. Dry-run both device scripts in a clean
environment against fresh shallow clones, as CI has them (this needs GitHub).

````diff
diff --git a/.github/workflows/build.yml b/.github/workflows/build.yml
index ea219c008..4e21fe9f2 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/build.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/build.yml
@@ -136,6 +136,26 @@ jobs:
           PICO_SDK_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/pico-sdk
         run: pnpm device:check
 
+      # The Pico box's firmware (docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 8): pico/n8-host, the MIDI-to-N8 bridge
+      # on the N8 pack's Edio, in both USB variants, each linked under the same trap over the whole image (TinyUSB and
+      # Pico-PIO-USB included), with its own probe that must fail to link. Built, never run (the rig's gate runs it).
+      # It needs what the device check does not: the SDK's TinyUSB submodule (0.18.0, by the 2.1.1 tag's pointer) and
+      # Pico-PIO-USB at the commit the rig's firmware was proven on, which nothing else in the repository uses.
+      - name: Install the box's USB stacks (TinyUSB, Pico-PIO-USB 5a37a66)
+        run: |
+          set -eux
+          git -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/pico-sdk" submodule update --init --depth 1 lib/tinyusb
+          git init -q "$RUNNER_TEMP/Pico-PIO-USB"
+          git -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/Pico-PIO-USB" fetch -q --depth 1 https://github.com/sekigon-gonnoc/Pico-PIO-USB.git \
+            5a37a66dc5d3fbe0ef3cdbeda923a757440f984f
+          git -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/Pico-PIO-USB" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
+
+      - name: Device build (the Pico box's firmware, the link trap)
+        env:
+          PICO_SDK_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/pico-sdk
+          PICO_PIO_USB_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/Pico-PIO-USB
+        run: pnpm device:box
+
       - name: Install plugin-format validators
         run: |
           set -eux
````

````diff
+The desktop's `SerialTransport` wraps `deps/serial` as `WjwwoodSerialPort` did (its per-read timeout reset and its
+port listing included). It is a `PortTransport` (`n8/desktop/PortTransport.hpp`), the desktop's owned interface: the
+transport interface plus a virtual destructor and the text of the call that failed. A transport throws on neither
+target: the desktop's catches deps/serial's exceptions, answers a short count or 0 and keeps the port's own words, which
+`N8Link`, `N8Host` and the facet report in place of Edio's. The Pico's `UsbCdcTransport` (section 8) pumps TinyUSB and
+its idle hook inside its own waits, and `read(..., 0)` returns after one pump with what it found. Edio never knows about
+either.
+
+**`Edio`** is a plain class over a `Transport&`: it allocates nothing, throws nothing, uses no RTTI, and is neither
+thread-safe (on the desktop `N8Link` and `N8Host` already serialise every use; on the Pico there is one thread) nor
+re-entrant: a `Progress`, a `listDir` visitor or a transport's idle hook must not call the same Edio, and a MIDI
+forward from inside a wait waits for the call. Its constructor is not `constexpr` on purpose: a constant-initialised
+static Edio (the box's) would put the whole object, its zeroed buffers included, in `.data`, copied from flash at every
+boot, for no RAM saved.
+
+- **Status, not exceptions.** Every call returns a `Status` struct, `{code, where, step, device, reply}`. The `Code`
+  is `Ok`, `Timeout`, `LinkDown`, `BadReply`, `Device` (`device` is the N8's status byte), `NotFound` (an operation's
+  file is not on the card, which no other code fits), `Cancelled` or `TooLarge`; `Where` names the wire position that
+  failed (a command's bytes, a reply, the status reply, a trailing status, a directory record, a file block, a write's
+  ack, the menu's test answer, its install status, its map index, ...), `Step` the step of an operation (`Test`,
+  `Upload`, `Save`, `Install`, `Start`, `List`, `Open`, `Data`, `Close`), and `reply` what a `BadReply` answered.
+  Values come back through out-parameters and caller buffers. `describe(status, out, capacity, path)` gives the text,
+  with the call's path for the few texts that name one (a mkdir's, an install's, a file not found; `Status` carries no
+  pointer), formatted by its own small writer because newlib's printf family can reach the heap. Where the TS and C++
+  messages differed the TS one is kept, since it is what the CLI prints (section 7), its hex lowercase; four texts
+  have no TS twin (a write timeout, link down, cancelled, too large). A port that fails (a deps/serial exception) is
+  reported by the facet as `linkDown` with the port's words rather than as a timeout: Edio itself says `Timeout`,
+  because a desktop transport cannot tell its link's state, and latching `linkUp` false there would turn a refused
+  config write into a dead stream.
 - **One write per frame.** A command's header, its arguments and as much payload as fits a 256-byte scratch in the
-  object go out in one `write`; a larger payload follows in further writes. That is the Pico's PIO-USB rule (one packet
-  per endpoint per 1 ms frame) and it changes nothing on the desktop but the number of calls. The golden compares byte
-  streams, so it holds the new Edio unchanged; it moves to `packages/n8/native/test/` and stays the protocol's oracle.
+  object go out in one `write`; a larger payload follows in further writes (8 KB at a time). That is the Pico's PIO-USB
+  rule (one packet per endpoint per 1 ms frame) and it changes nothing on the desktop but the number of calls. **A short
+  write fails the command** (`Timeout` at `Where::Write`, `LinkDown` when the link says so): both old clients ignored
+  the write's count, the root of the 2026-10-22 mid-command bug. On the desktop the streaming link stops with `serial
+  write failed (N8 unplugged?): ...` where it used to carry on writing into a cart parser left mid-command, and the
+  expansion-volume write is retried by `OnControl` a second later like any failed config write. The golden compares byte
+  streams, so it holds the new Edio unchanged; it moves to `packages/n8/native/test/` and stays the protocol's oracle,
+  with 13 cases recorded from the old TS clients (a listing, a file read, the menu's commands, ROM boots) added to its
+  original 15 (section 9).
 - **Primitives** (today's C++ coverage, now on the Pico too): `connect` (flush, `CMD_STATUS`, the `A5` check, a short
   handshake timeout) and `status`; `sysInfo` (64 bytes) and `vdc` (8) into caller arrays; `freeSpace`, `dirMake`
   (tolerating "exists"), `fileDelete`; `memRD`, `memWR` (fire and forget), `fifoWR`, `fifoTxString`; `fileOpen`,
   `fileRead` (512-byte response-gated blocks), `fileWrite` (1 KB ack-gated blocks, then a status), `fileClose`;
-  `listDir` as a visitor (one callback per entry, the name in a 256-byte buffer in the object, so no capacity limit);

 ## 8. The Pico
 
-**The firmware** (`pico/n8-host`, in place): `main.c` and `box.c` become `main.cpp` and `box.cpp`; `edio.c` and
-`edio.h` are deleted.
+**The firmware** (`pico/n8-host`, in place): `main.c` and `box.c` become `main.cpp` and `box.cpp` (`git mv`); `edio.c`
+and `edio.h` are deleted. `pio_usb_root.c` is a one-function C shim: `pio_usb_ll.h` does not compile as C++ (an inline
+function stores an int into an enum), and `main` reads `PIO_USB_ROOT_PORT(0)->connected` through it. TinyUSB's
+`osal_none.h` applies `++` and `--` to a volatile, which C++20 deprecates, so a `#pragma GCC diagnostic` around the two
+`#include "tusb.h"` silences it there only.
 
 - `UsbCdcTransport` implements `rp::n8::Transport` over TinyUSB's CDC host: its waits pump `tuh_task` and the idle
   hook (`box_feed`: the watchdog and the LED), `linkUp()` reads the mount state, the drain after a write is best
-  effort, the input flush waits for 20 ms of silence. One `Edio` and one transport live in static storage, and a mount
-  rebinds the transport's CDC index.
-- Every N8 call goes through the pack: the probe (`status`, `sysInfo`, never a cart-memory read), `boot_rom` (`bootRom`
-  inside the box's CRC skip and retry), `box.cfg` (`readFile`, `writeFile`), the expansion-volume check (`memRD`,
-  `memWR` of `ADDR_CFG`), the sniff (`memRD` of `ADDR_SSR + 0x80`), the MIDI batches (`fifoWR`), the health check
-  (`status`).
+  effort, the input flush waits for 20 ms of silence. One `Edio` and one transport live in static storage.
+- **A remount never resumes a call on the new N8.** `tuh_task` drains its event queue and TinyUSB's enumeration delays
+  block inside it, so an unmount and a re-mount can both happen inside one pump. The unmount callback therefore calls
+  `usb.unbind()`; the CDC mount callback only records the index (and bumps `n8_gen`); and **the main loop rebinds**,
+  `usb.bind(n8_cdc_idx)`, at its top level just before the new N8's probe, never inside an Edio call. From the unmount
+  to that bind `linkUp()` is false, so the call in flight fails at once (`LinkDown`), `bootRom` returns and the boot
+  is abandoned, and a MIDI batch flushed in the window fails fast instead of landing in the new N8's menu FIFO. The
+  box's `BOOT_GONE()` is `n8_gen != gen || !n8_ready || !usb.linkUp()`: the link term is what stops a boot whose N8
+  went away during the probe at its first guard, before one futile `*t`. The Edio object starts the next call clean:
+  `send()` zeroes its frame and `begin()` rebuilds it for every command, and `name_` is valid only during a visitor
+  call.
+- **The N8 calls:** the probe is `status` and `sysInfo` (never a cart-memory read); the menu handshake is `flushInput`
+  then `Menu::test`, as `edio_menu_test` flushed first; `box.cfg` is read with the primitives, a plain `fileOpen`,
+  `fileRead(16)` and `fileClose` (a close is always sent once the open succeeded, `edio_file_get`'s wire;
+  `Ops::readFile` would add a directory listing) and saved with `Ops::writeFile`; the expansion-volume check, the
+  sniff, the MIDI batches and the health check are `memRD`, `memWR(ADDR_EXP_VOL)`, `memRD(ADDR_SSR + 0x80)`, `fifoWR`
+  and `status`.
+- **The boot is `bootRom` with its hooks, and its wire is `edio.c`'s.** The box keeps its handshake loop, its CRC skip,
+  its saved choice and its retry, and calls `bootRom(path, rom when uploading, {}, Always or Never, nullptr, {},
+  {handshake false, boot_step, &run})`. Its `boot_step` hook prints each line where the old firmware printed it: before
+  Upload `upload <path> (<n> bytes)...`; before Install `uploaded in <n> ms`, the `box.cfg` save when the choice changed
+  (an interrupted upload never leaves a CRC that claims the ROM is on the card, which is why the save lies between the
+  upload and the install, inside the hook), the pending pick cleared, `BOOT_GONE`, `menu up -> install <path> (*n)...`;
+  before Start `BOOT_GONE` and `installed -> boot (*s)`. The retry (an install refused with a status other than 0x44
+  when the upload was skipped) is `bootRom(Always)` again. An install that answers no map index (`Where::MapIndex`)
+  runs the Start hook and sends `*s` itself, as `edio_menu_install` ignored that read. The commands are the same, in the
+  same order, with no extra `*t`, and every log string the gate's scripts match is unchanged.
 - Unchanged: the box policy and its flags, the LED modes, the watchdog and the recovery with backoff, the ROM table in
   flash at `XIP_BASE + 0x200000`, the UART1 IRQ ring and the 192-byte batches, the SysEx `7D 50` pick, `midi.c` (C,
   behind `extern "C"` guards), the TinyUSB callbacks (`extern "C"`), and `loop.sh`, `stress.sh` and `faults.sh`.
-- **The SOF timer:** the PIO-USB config sets `skip_alarm_pool`; the firmware claims hardware alarm 2 and its callback
-  re-arms itself 1000 us later on an absolute schedule and calls `pio_usb_host_frame()`: the alarm, the IRQ and the
-  cadence `alarm_pool_create(2, 1)` gave, with nothing allocated.

-removed, `check-trap.cmake`'s 87-symbol trap and its probe. Its generated registration includes `rp.n8.nes`, which no

-`RP_NATIVE_USB=ON` variant must build and link under the trap too; the rig is PIO-USB, so only that one runs. The

+- **The SOF timer** (`SofTimer.{hpp,cpp}`): the PIO-USB config sets `skip_alarm_pool`, and the firmware claims
+  hardware alarm 2 of the default timer (`TIMER0_IRQ_2`, exclusive handler, priority `0x80`, the
+  `PICO_DEFAULT_IRQ_PRIORITY` the pool's handler kept) and re-arms it 1000 us after the last target (absolute, no
+  drift; late, the handler fires again in the same IRQ until the target is ahead), calling `pio_usb_host_frame()`: the
+  alarm, the IRQ and the cadence `alarm_pool_create(2, 1)` gave, with nothing allocated. The first frame comes 1000 us
+  after the start, armed from a forced IRQ (`gTarget` is stored before the handler is installed, so the forced IRQ is
+  the only thing that can start it); the handler runs from RAM, where the pool's ran from flash and called into RAM.
+  It differs in starting right after `tuh_init()` returns rather than inside it, microseconds later and before any
+  device can attach. **`skip_alarm_pool` alone is not enough**: `pio_usb_host_init` still contains the call
+  `alarm_pool_create(2, 1)` behind its `if`, so `alarm_pool_create_on_timer`, which mallocs, stays linked (the trap
+  fired at `time.c.o` naming `__wrap_malloc` and `__wrap_calloc`). The firmware links with
+  `--wrap=alarm_pool_create_on_timer` and defines the wrapper in `SofTimer.cpp` as a `panic()` that never runs, and
+  `--gc-sections` drops the SDK's function and the heap with it. The wrapper is not one of the 87 trapped symbols, and
+  Pico-PIO-USB itself is not edited.
+- **The stack is 4 KB.** `n8_host` sets `PICO_STACK_SIZE=0x1000` (all of SCRATCH_Y, which holds nothing else) and
+  `PICO_CORE1_STACK_SIZE=0x800` (core 1's reservation keeps the 2 KB it had; the macro defaults to the main stack's).
+  The linker checks only the reservation: scratch code that would overlap the reserved 4 KB fails the link. The stack's
+  real depth is a hand sum with no limit at run time: the box's deepest wait is `box.cfg`'s save inside the Install
+  hook, about 970 bytes of frames, below it TinyUSB's enumeration and the SDK's printf chain (about 840) and above it
+  the interrupts nested on the same stack (about 500), a pessimistic 2.3 KB against the nominal 2 KB it was and the
+  4 KB it is. If E3 puts anything in scratch or starts core 1, `rp-device-check`'s successor wants the same size.
+
+**The build.** The firmware becomes `retroplug_product(n8-host DEVICE PACKAGES n8 TARGETS n8_host)`, as
+`rp-device-check` is (the target keeps its name, so `loop.sh`'s `n8_host.elf` is unchanged): the pack's portable
+sources compiled with `RP_DEVICE`, `-fno-exceptions` and `-fno-rtti`, E1's runtime with `pico_malloc` removed, the
+87-symbol trap over the whole image (TinyUSB and Pico-PIO-USB included) and `n8_host_trap_probe`, the firmware's own
+probe that must fail to link. What both device projects share is hoisted: `cmake/reflectcpp-pin.cmake` (the
+reflect-cpp pin and finder), `cmake/device-image.cmake` (`pico_malloc`'s removal in place, the trap list,
+`rp_device_executable()` and `rp_device_trap_check()`) and `cmake/check-trap.cmake` (moved from `device-check`). Its
+generated registration includes `rp.n8.nes`, which no plan uses until E3 and which `--gc-sections` would drop, so
+`main` references `rp_register_packages` and prints `[n8-host] node type rp.n8.nes (registered, not planned)` at boot:
+the node linking into the real image is proven by the image naming it. The `RP_NATIVE_USB=ON` variant builds and links
+under the trap too; the rig is PIO-USB, so only that one runs. A scratch build with every `loop.sh` option on at once
+(`-DRP_NATIVE_USB`, `N8_TUSB_DEBUG`, `N8_MENU_TRIES`, `N8_APU_LAT`, `N8_EXP_VOL`, `N8_TEST_HOOKS`, `N8_ROM_PATH`)
+links under the trap. The image carries no UF2 in `device:box` (`-DPICO_NO_PICOTOOL=1`, as E1 decided, or the SDK
+would fetch and build picotool in CI); `loop.sh`'s own build still makes its UF2, and the flashed bytes are identical.
+A fresh `loop.sh` build dir passes the desktop build's `reflectcpp_SOURCE_DIR` from `$repo/build/CMakeCache.txt` when
+there is one, so it needs no network, and falls back to the clone otherwise. `cmake_minimum_required` is 3.20 (the
+packages need 3.19) and the standard C++20.
+
+| Image (Release, flash / data / bss) | Before E2 | After E2 |
+|---|---|---|
+| PIO-USB | 43664 / 16528 / 32192 | 48508 / 15324 / 32360 |
+| `RP_NATIVE_USB` | 41256 / 1412 / 25592 | 48468 / 1560 / 26128 |
+| `rp-device-check` (E1: 65156 / 1844 / 412742) | | 82012 / 2000 / 416402 |
+
+The PIO-USB image before linked a heap (`pico_malloc`'s wrappers, newlib's `malloc`, `calloc`, `free`, `_sbrk` and
+`alarm_pool_create_on_timer`, the only caller); after, it links no heap symbol, and its data shrank because newlib's
+malloc state is gone. The native image already linked none, so its growth is the pack (Edio, Menu, Ops and `rp.n8.nes`)
+with nothing removed to offset it. The box links `writeBattery` and `batteryPath` and never calls them (`--gc-sections`
+cannot drop what a kept function, `bootRom`, refers to without LTO).
+
+**CI.** `pnpm device:box` (`tools/build-box.sh`) builds the firmware in both USB variants, as a step beside
+`device:check` in the linux job: two steps in `build.yml`, the first initialising the CI's pico-sdk 2.1.1 clone's
+`lib/tinyusb` (0.18.0 by the SDK's pointer) at depth 1 and fetching Pico-PIO-USB at `5a37a66`, the second running
+`pnpm device:box` with `PICO_SDK_PATH` and `PICO_PIO_USB_PATH`. The script's SDK rule is `loop.sh`'s, not
+`device:check`'s strict one: `PICO_SDK_PATH` when it carries TinyUSB, else `/workspaces/pico-sdk` (the devcontainer
+bakes an SDK with no TinyUSB at `/opt/pico-sdk` and points the variable at it), said aloud when it falls back; a path
+that is set and is no SDK, or a `PICO_PIO_USB_PATH` that is no checkout, stops the run. `PICO_PIO_USB_PATH` keeps its
+`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB` default for the rig; nothing else in the repository needs Pico-PIO-USB, so it is not
+vendored. An `env -i` dry run against fresh shallow clones passed both.

+E2's reference figures, which a later gate compares per window: `[stats] lat=` is the last window's average and
+maximum, not cumulative; isolated notes 587 us average and 1110 us worst (baseline 625 / 1089); the final line's
+recovery window 10.0 ms (baseline 9.9); the window holding a 40-byte SysEx pair 7.2 ms average and 20.9 ms peak (about
+13 ms of it the SysEx on the wire); sustained-flood windows peak at 3.4 to 7.0 ms. A window may not exceed its
+reference by more than noise.

+## 13. As built

+type ids changed), both consumer suites passed at every commit, and nothing was re-recorded. The desktop's N8
+behaviour is the old clients' wire: identical bytes in identical order, on every path but a short write, for every
+operation the CLI, `N8Host` and `N8Link` perform, in fewer `write` calls. Sections 1 to 11 are corrected in place
+where the build made them false (the Edio's status, the report interface, the providers' per-instance API, what stays
+in `retroplug`, the box on `bootRom`). The final counts: `retroplug-n8-test` ends at 89 cases (1220 assertions; the
+baseline's 57 / 529) and `retroplug-serial-test` at 1 / 7, `retroplug-engine-graph-test` at 330 (313),
+`retroplug-device-mode-test` at 11 cases (10), `pnpm test` at 1781 cases over 174 files (1814), `test:native` at 606
+passed and 2 skipped over 168 files (602 / 167), and `device:check`'s image at 82012 / 2000 / 416402 flash / data /
+bss (65156 / 1844 / 412742).

+### 13.1 The device ABI (commit 1)
+
+- **Headers.** `rp_device.h`, `rp_jobs.h` and `rp_stage.h` in `node-sdk`, as section 5 records them: the fixed 8-entry

+  `rp.host.jobs/1` with no `ctx`, `DeviceJobSlot` under `graph/desktop/`. `Engine::setDeviceLinks`, `HostDevices` and
+  `DeviceLinks.hpp` are gone; `installDevice` / `clearDevice` and `installLink` / `clearLink` replace them, and the
+  three products that installed links (the SDL standalone, the plugin, the test host) call them.
+- **The cart and surface interfaces** are `rp::n8::CartLink` and `rp::launchpad::SurfaceLink`; `rp.n8.nes` was renamed
+  from `N8Nodes` to `N8Node` and `LaunchpadNodes.cpp` includes no engine header either.
+- **Tests.** `DeviceAbi.c` and `DeviceAbi.test.cpp` compile the headers as C, compare C's layout with C++'s and drive
+  a C node through the registry and the report table; `Devices.test.cpp` gains the registry's table, a clear, a
+  release after a clear and a full table; the engine-graph count rose by 11 (313 to 324).

+

+  (`rp_n8_provider`, the `rpc` registration); the N8 tests' targets with their names; `N8ReliableLink.hpp`, which
+  `N8Link` and the emulated NES FIFO role both speak (`retroplug-core` links the pack's include roots for it), and
+  `FixedQueue` to `node-sdk`, so the pack depends on `node-sdk` alone.
+- **The provider mechanism** (`rp_provider.h`, `rp::Providers`, the generated header, `ProviderHost.hpp`, the

+  hold an `rp::Providers` and a `ProviderHost`; `N8Hooks.{hpp,cpp}` and the four `__rp_*N8` hooks are deleted;
+  `RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES` is `core dsp graph-runtime n8 native`. The facet's link half (`N8Rpc.hpp`, header-only at the
+  time) and `n8Devices.ts` on `createN8Client`.
+- **`rp.n8.nes` is `device: true`** (section 13.6): `retroplug-n8-device` compiles in the default build,

+
+- **The firmware** is C++ on the pack (section 8): `main.cpp`, `box.cpp`, `UsbCdcTransport`, `SofTimer`, the C shim, the
````
