````diff
+### 13.5 The prototype questions, answered
+
+1. **A `test:native` session reaches a fake cart through the real facet by the test host calling
+   `rp::n8::createProvider` with `FakeN8`'s factory and a one-port lister** (`"fake-n8"`), `FakeN8.hpp` compiled into
+   that target alone, its `n8.cfg` in a per-process temp directory (a static, since the harness ends the process
+   through txiki's `exit`, which runs static destructors and not `main`'s frame). A test-only port name or an
+   environment hook in the production provider would have shipped fake-cart code and a test switch in every product.
+   The consequence: the test host (which the authoring tools run too) has the N8 facet, and its `rp.n8.nes` binds the
+   disconnected `N8CartLink` instead of its stub; both refuse jobs "not connected", and no suite saw a difference.
+2. **`rp_register_package_rpc<Server>` fits the products' one server type**: the CLI's and SDL's `BackendRpcServer` and
+   the plugin's `PluginRpcServer` are all `TypedRpcServer<Empty, QuickJSCodec>`. It does not instantiate for the JSON
+   codec (`rfl::Bytestring` is unsupported by `rfl::Generic`), so the pack's tests mount on QuickJS. The Node addon's
+   `NodeCodec` was not instantiated: the addon mounts no facet.
+3. **A remount inside an Edio wait** is handled by unbinding in the unmount callback and rebinding at the top of the
+   main loop, with `linkUp()` false in between and `BOOT_GONE` carrying the link term (section 8). The Edio object
+   leaves the next call clean. The first build missed a remount inside the probe, before `boot_rom` read its
+   generation, which cost about 8 s of failed handshakes and a false `no 'k'`; the link term closed it.
+4. **The static SOF timer matches the pool's timing**: the stress latencies, the recovery window and 8 of 8 fault
+   rounds say so (section 13.7). It differs in starting microseconds later, before any device can attach, and in
+   running from RAM.
+5. **`rp.n8.nes` compiles and links in device mode and plans on the Pico**, once it declares no `threads` (section
+   13.6). The first try failed twice: `#include <iterator>` made libstdc++ pull in `<string>`, `<stdexcept>` and
+   `<exception>`, which fired `node.hpp`'s heap-header `#error` (the include is gone; only `std::size` was used and
+   `<string_view>` declares it), and `threads = true` tripped `DeviceTypeCheck`. The device build needs only what
+   `CartLink.hpp`'s `NoCart` has (32-bit atomics); the object's undefined symbols are `__stack_chk_fail`, `lround` and
+   `strlen`, then the soft-double helpers, `memcmp`, `memcpy` and `memset`.
+6. **A 1 MB upload keeps the watchdog fed by the transport's idle hook alone**, by trace: every wait loop pass is
+   `pump()` (`tuh_task(); box_feed();`), thousands of times a second against the 3 s watchdog, and `rom_crc32` feeds it
+   every 64 KB. The longest stretch without a feed is TinyUSB's blocking enumeration delay (about 0.5 s), which predates
+   E2 and cannot happen mid-upload without first failing it. The upload path was also run on the rig (section 13.7).
+7. **The generated provider code costs a product with no providers nothing**: a generated header it never includes, and
+   for a product whose packages name no provider inline stubs (an empty `rp::Providers`, no allocation).
+
+### 13.6 What was found
+
+- **`threads` is the link's business, not the node's.** The first build had `rp.n8.nes` declare `threads`, which kept
+  `Target::Pico` from planning it and `device: true` from holding. The thread belongs to the desktop's link, so the node
+  declares none and relies only on `CartLink::push()` never blocking, never allocating and taking no lock, whoever
+  drains the ring. The flag means what the node itself needs, not its device link; the Launchpad nodes still declare it
+  for theirs (the exception, until their pack). The planner now plans `rp.n8.nes` for a Pico target (`N8Node.test.cpp`
+  holds `"threads":false` and both rigs), E1's portable-types rule counts it, and nothing in TS reads the flag for it.
+- **`rp.host.jobs/1` needed a fourth entry**, `abandon`, and an opaque `rp_job` over the engine's record (an earlier
+  build defined `struct rp_job` as the record itself), and a request with an embedded NUL had to be refused (section 5).
+- **Providers are per instance.** The design's global `rp_start_providers(host)` would have kept provider state in
+  statics, and a DAW holds several instances each with its own engine.
+- **`chrImage.ts` and `risaSyncTranslator.ts` could not move to the pack**: each imports `retroplug` modules, a cycle
+  (section 7).
+- **The golden did not cover the operations.** The review of the Edio found that its 15 cases carried no listing, file
+  read, menu command or boot, so a wrong wire there would have passed. Thirteen cases were recorded from the old TS
+  clients at the pack commit (`3eb5a7928`'s `edio.ts`, `n8Menu.ts` and `n8Load.ts` over their fake port) and appended;
+  every one matched the new Edio byte for byte on the first run, with every queued reply read.
+- **A short write used to be ignored** by both old clients, the root of the 2026-10-22 mid-command bug; it now fails
+  the command (section 4).
+- **`skip_alarm_pool` alone left the heap in the image**: the call to `alarm_pool_create(2, 1)` stays linked behind the
+  config's `if`, so the firmware wraps `alarm_pool_create_on_timer` (section 8).
+- **The first box kept the upload outside `bootRom`**, which sent one extra `*t` before each `*n` and broke the wire
+  equality with `edio.c`; `BootOptions` (no handshake, a before-step hook) lets the box keep `bootRom` and the old wire.
+- **`pnpm install --offline` without `--frozen-lockfile` silently pruned 464 lines of `pnpm-lock.yaml`** (every other
+  platform's esbuild and typescript optional packages). The lockfile was restored and the two entries added by hand;
+  never run the non-frozen offline install here.
+- **The 4 KB stack.** The hand sum for the box's deepest chain is a pessimistic 2.3 KB against the SDK's nominal 2 KB;
+  the old firmware's was about 2.0 KB. Today an overrun would land in unused SCRATCH_Y, but nothing guards it, so the
+  box asks for 4 KB (section 8); `rp-device-check`'s protocol chain is about 1.9 KB against its nominal 2 KB and its
+  types chain (E1's settings decode) about 2.3 KB, and it is never run.
+- **Writing a battery to the SD card is not for the box**: `writeBattery` is linked and never called; its 789-byte
+  path buffer (an 864-byte frame) is on the stack only in the facet's boots (the CLI's) and the device check's.
+
+### 13.7 The gate
+
+Run by the controller on the prototype's image (sha256 `10a6b09edb99...`, BlipToaster, never `n8-midi.nes`), against the
+baseline of section 8. The image is byte-identical to the one the final fix pass produced.
+
+| Leg | Baseline | E2 |
+|---|---|---|
+| `loop.sh --rom .../bliptoaster.nes --until 'booted by the Pico'` | booted 8.4 s after reset (the default ROM, `n8-midi.nes`) | booted by the Pico in 12.2 s with BlipToaster (saved choice, CRC skip), expansion volume 129 (the stage commit's smoke booted the default ROM in 8.0 s) |
+| `stress.sh` | rx=153607 msgs=50775 fwd=50277 fail=0, 0.71 ms average | rx=153277 msgs=50663 fwd=50185 fail=0, overrun, framing and ring loss 0; isolated latency worst 1110 us, average 587 us (baseline 1089 / 625) |
+| audio on the L6's channel 3 | A4 440.30 Hz +1.2 c, C5 522.16 Hz -3.6 c | identical |
+| `faults.sh --rounds 8` | 7 of 8 (the Zigbee late-cut quirk) | 8 of 8; abandoned boots 7, stuck menus 0, recovery reboots 0, uploads 0 |
+| the upload path (added) | | two ROMs staged, SysEx `7D 50` pick and an NES power-cycle: 294928 bytes uploaded in about 4.9 s and booted; the next cycle booted the saved choice by CRC skip (mapper 24 exp vol 139; mapper 69 exp vol 129) |
+
+- **The `lat=` figure in the `[stats]` line is per window, not cumulative.** The 9.9 ms the baseline attributed
+  "maximum latency" to is the final line's recovery window; E2's is 10.0 ms there. Sustained-flood windows peak at 3.4
+  to 7.0 ms, and **the window holding the SysEx pair peaks at 20.9 ms (average 7.2 ms)**: a 40-byte SysEx is about 13
+  ms on the 31250 baud wire, and no baseline window was kept for it. The gate condition, that the maximum not grow,
+  held where it can be compared.
+- **A `loop.sh` reset clears a pending pick**, as `box_start` documents; a pick needs an NES power-cycle only.
+- The desktop leg of the acceptance (`n8-load`, `n8-play`, `retroplug-n8-hwtest`) is the controller's, run after the
+  plan is replayed.
+
+### 13.8 What is left
+
+- **E3.** The box's half of the device ABI: a `rp::n8::CartLink` over the firmware's Edio with no thread, which must
+  keep the promise `CartLink.hpp` makes, that `push()` never blocks, never allocates and takes no lock (a box that
+  forwards from its main loop through the same link its Edio waits on would break it). The stack: `rp-device-check`'s
+  successor wants `PICO_STACK_SIZE=0x1000`, and a `-Wstack-usage` check would replace the hand sum. A host-side fake
+  for `UsbCdcTransport` (the transport's remount, unmount and drain rules are proven on the rig and by reading, and
+  have no host test). The main loop still splits into the generic host and the pack's part then.
+- **The Launchpad's `threads` flag** is the one node still declaring `threads` for its link; it goes with its pack,
+  provider and facet in place of `bindLaunchpadHooks`.
+- **E4**, the rest of the package split and a web transport, as section 11.
````

````diff
+static 400 KiB arena, and then the N8 pack's Edio, menu commands and operations over a scripted cart
+(`N8Protocol.cpp`: a boot, a file read, a cancelled boot, every primitive, held on the desktop by a `[device-check]`
+case), reporting on the UART. It links with `--wrap` on 87 symbols (with arm-none-eabi GCC 13.2.1; the malloc family,
+`sbrk`, `__cxa_guard_*`, every `operator new` / `delete` and `std::__throw_*` the device `libstdc++.a` defines, the
+throw entry points, and the exception-handling and RTTI runtime: the personality routine, the catch and cleanup
+entries, `__dynamic_cast` and the class `type_info` vtables), so any heap use or throw in what it links is a link
+error naming the object, as is an object built with exceptions or RTTI that keeps a handler, a cleanup or a
+polymorphic class's `type_info`; a post-link check also refuses an image that defines a wrapper or refers to one. The
+Pico SDK's `pico_malloc` is taken out of `pico_runtime` in place, the one part of this image's runtime the trap cannot
+have (stdio over the UART links under it); the box's firmware, whose Pico-PIO-USB host makes an alarm pool on the
+heap, needs more (below). The pin, the trap list and the in-place `pico_malloc` removal are shared with the firmware
+through `cmake/reflectcpp-pin.cmake`, `cmake/device-image.cmake` and `cmake/check-trap.cmake`. The script also links a
+probe that allocates and requires it to fail naming `__wrap__Znwj` and `__wrap_malloc`, on every run, so the trap
+cannot silently stop reaching the link. It needs `arm-none-eabi-g++` and a Pico SDK (no submodules); the CI linux-x64
+job installs `gcc-arm-none-eabi libnewlib-arm-none-eabi libstdc++-arm-none-eabi-newlib`, clones SDK 2.1.1 into
+`$RUNNER_TEMP` and runs the script. The image is not run: instance sizes on the device are unmeasured, and the first
+run of the check's successor on hardware is E3 (the box runs the pack's Edio on the rig, but no graph node). Release
+sizes: core, dsp and the executor are about 42 KB of flash and no static RAM; the whole image is 82 KB flash (the
+pack's nodes and Edio about 13 KB of it) and about 418 KB RAM (data and bss), almost all of it the arena.
+
+`pnpm device:box` ([tools/build-box.sh](../tools/build-box.sh)) builds the Pico box's firmware under the same trap. The
+firmware is `retroplug_product(n8-host DEVICE PACKAGES n8 TARGETS n8_host)`: C++ on the N8 pack, the pack compiled
+with `RP_DEVICE`, `-fno-exceptions` and `-fno-rtti`, with no heap anywhere in the image. Pico-PIO-USB's SOF timer was
+an alarm pool made with `malloc`, so the firmware sets `skip_alarm_pool`, runs a static SOF timer of its own on
+hardware alarm 2 (`SofTimer.cpp`) and links with `--wrap=alarm_pool_create_on_timer`, since the config flag alone
+leaves the function (and the heap) linked; the unreachable wrapper panics. The main stack is 4 KB
+(`PICO_STACK_SIZE=0x1000`, core 1's reservation kept at 2 KB), asserted only as a reservation of SCRATCH_Y. Both
+variants, PIO-USB (the rig's; the N8 on GP2/GP3) and `RP_NATIVE_USB=ON`, link under the trap, each with a probe that
+must fail to link; the sizes in flash / data / bss are 48508 / 15324 / 32360 and 48468 / 1560 / 26128. The boot prints
+`[n8-host] node type rp.n8.nes (registered, not planned)`: `main` references the registration, so `--gc-sections` keeps
+the node, and the line is the proof. CI
+installs TinyUSB and clones Pico-PIO-USB at 5a37a66 for it. The hardware gate (`loop.sh`, `stress.sh`, `faults.sh`) is
+run by hand on the rig with BlipToaster; it is not CI.
````

````diff
+## 3b. The Pico box (standalone MIDI to N8, no PC)
+
+`pico/n8-host` is a Pico 2 that boots a ROM through the N8 menu and forwards MIDI to the cart FIFO
+by itself. Its firmware is C++ on the N8 pack (`packages/n8`), so it runs the SAME Edio as
+`retroplug-cli`'s n8-* tools; `pico/n8-host`'s README has the box's behaviour (LED, watchdog, ROM
+staging, the SysEx `7D 50` pick). Notes for running it:
+
+- **The N8's USB belongs to the Pico while a box test runs** (the SD card is reachable only through
+  it), so no CLI session may hold the port at the same time. Drive it only through `pico/n8-host`'s
+  scripts, from that directory (`cd` in a subshell): `./loop.sh --rom
+  /workspaces/bliptoaster/build/bliptoaster.nes --until 'booted by the Pico' --fail "no 'k'|FAILED"`
+  (stages the ROM, builds, flashes over SWD, power-cycles the NES and watches the console),
+  `./stress.sh --rom /workspaces/bliptoaster/build/bliptoaster.nes` (a MIDI flood through the Pico,
+  counters and latency) and `./faults.sh --rounds 8` (random NES power cuts, each round must boot
+  again and play an A4). The Debug Probe and its console (`/dev/ttyDbgProbe`, 115200) are the
+  Pico's; the lab's power rules above apply to the NES.
+- **Box tests boot BlipToaster, never `n8-midi.nes`.** Stage the ROM with `--rom <file.nes>` (it is written into the
+  Pico's flash and copied to `usb-games/pico/<name>.nes`). `n8-midi.nes` is the older MIDI ROM (it drops its first
+  message, hangs on a Launchpad's flood and is broken on ch2); `N8_ROM_PATH` still defaults to it in the firmware, so a
+  bare flash with no `--rom` boots that file if it is on the card.
+- **The boot line to match.** The console prints `[n8-host] USB host up (PIO-USB D+=GP2, D-=GP3)
+  ...`, then `[n8-host] node type rp.n8.nes (registered, not planned)` (the image naming the pack's
+  node; E3 plans it), and a good boot ends `[n8-host] usb-games/pico/bliptoaster.nes booted by the
+  Pico - no PC used.`, about 12 s after the reset from the saved choice with the CRC skip (`[box]
+  already on the SD ... - no upload`), an upload adds about 5 s for a 290 KB ROM. The pass pattern
+  is `booted by the Pico`; fail on `no 'k'` or `FAILED`.
+- **Read `[stats] lat=` per window.** The figure is the last window's average and maximum in us, not
+  cumulative: the final line's 10 ms is the recovery window and the window holding a 40-byte SysEx
+  peaks near 21 ms (the SysEx is about 13 ms on the wire). Isolated notes sit near 0.6 ms average
+  and 1.1 ms worst.
+- **`pnpm device:box` needs no hardware**: it proves the firmware links under the heap/exception/RTTI trap and is CI's
+  check; the scripts above are what prove it behaves.
+

@@ -320,13 +327,45 @@ device (the only trigger seen was the false positive above, now fixed); the menu
 described (this N8 never returned to its menu on RESET); and the error LED's double blink (no boot
 failed or stuck while it was being sampled).
 
+## The firmware's layout, build and link trap
+
+The firmware is C++ on the N8 pack (`packages/n8`), the same `rp::n8::Edio` the desktop runs; nothing of the protocol
+is written here. `main.cpp` is the main loop (USB host, the probe, the boot, the MIDI bridge, the sniff), `box.cpp` the
+standalone box, `UsbCdcTransport.{hpp,cpp}` the `rp::n8::Transport` over TinyUSB's CDC host (its waits pump `tuh_task`
+and `box_feed`, `linkUp()` follows the mount), `SofTimer.{hpp,cpp}` the 1 ms start-of-frame timer, `pio_usb_root.c` a
+one-function C shim (`pio_usb_ll.h` does not compile as C++), and `../midi-in/midi.c` stays C. One `Edio` and one
+transport live in static storage.
+
+`CMakeLists.txt` declares `retroplug_product(n8-host DEVICE PACKAGES n8 TARGETS n8_host)`: the pack's portable sources
+are compiled with `RP_DEVICE`, `-fno-exceptions` and `-fno-rtti`, against `node-sdk` and reflect-cpp's headers, so a
+configure needs a reflect-cpp checkout. `loop.sh` hands a fresh build directory the desktop build's
+(`../../build/CMakeCache.txt`'s `reflectcpp_SOURCE_DIR`) and clones one only when there is none. The whole image links
+under the **link trap** (`cmake/device-image.cmake`, shared with `rp-device-check`): 87 `--wrap`ped symbols on the
+heap, on exceptions and on RTTI, with `pico_malloc` taken out of the runtime and a post-link check. A link error naming
+`__wrap_<symbol>` means an object reached the heap or a throw. The image has no heap at all: Pico-PIO-USB's SOF timer
+was an alarm pool made with `malloc`, so the config sets `skip_alarm_pool`, `SofTimer.cpp` runs a timer of its own on
+hardware alarm 2 (the alarm, the IRQ and the 1000 us absolute cadence the pool had; the handler runs from RAM), and the
+link wraps `alarm_pool_create_on_timer`, which `skip_alarm_pool` alone still leaves linked, to a `panic()` that never
+runs. The main stack is 4 KB (`PICO_STACK_SIZE=0x1000`, core 1's reservation kept at 2 KB): the deepest chain is about
+1 KB of frames, and with TinyUSB's enumeration and the interrupts nested above it the pessimistic sum is 2.3 KB, which
+the SDK's default 2 KB would not have held.
+
+**`pnpm device:box`** ([`../../tools/build-box.sh`](../../tools/build-box.sh)) builds both variants under the trap, in
+`build-box/{pio,native}/`, each with `n8_host_trap_probe` (an allocating program that must fail to link naming
+`__wrap__Znwj` and `__wrap_malloc`), and prints the sizes (flash / data / bss: PIO-USB 48508 / 15324 / 32360,
+`RP_NATIVE_USB` 48468 / 1560 / 26128). It needs the SDK's TinyUSB (`PICO_SDK_PATH` when it carries one, else
+`/workspaces/pico-sdk`) and Pico-PIO-USB at `5a37a66`; it builds an ELF only (`PICO_NO_PICOTOOL`) and runs in CI beside
+`device:check`. It proves the image links and traps; the rig's gate (`loop.sh`, `stress.sh`, `faults.sh`, with
+BlipToaster) proves it works.
+
 ## Build + flash + verify
 
 `loop.sh` does all of this; by hand:
 
 ```sh
 export PICO_SDK_PATH=/workspaces/pico-sdk         # NOT the image's /opt/pico-sdk: it has no TinyUSB
-cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja && cmake --build build
+cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -Dreflectcpp_SOURCE_DIR=<a reflect-cpp checkout, e.g. ../../build/_deps/reflectcpp-src> \
+  && cmake --build build     # without it the configure clones reflect-cpp
 sudo openocd -f interface/cmsis-dap.cfg -f target/rp2350.cfg \
      -c "program build/n8_host.elf verify reset exit"      # button-free SWD
 sudo stty -F /dev/ttyDbgProbe 115200 raw -echo && cat /dev/ttyDbgProbe
@@ -341,12 +380,17 @@ A good boot from a fresh N8 menu:
 [n8-host] SYS_INF: serial=00035AAD.00002C4D  device_id=0x17 (N8 PRO)  sw=0103 hw=0001
 [n8-host] --- probe done ---
 [n8-host] menu handshake (*t)...
-[n8-host] menu up -> install usb-games/n8-midi.nes (*n)...
-[n8-host] installed -> boot (*s); BlipToaster starting...
-[n8-host] BlipToaster booted by the Pico - no PC used.
+[box] ROM 0 of 1: usb-games/pico/bliptoaster.nes (crc f39a6773) - saved choice
+[box] already on the SD (its CRC was saved at the last upload) - no upload
+[n8-host] menu up -> install usb-games/pico/bliptoaster.nes (*n)...
+[n8-host] installed -> boot (*s); the ROM is starting...
+[n8-host] usb-games/pico/bliptoaster.nes booted by the Pico - no PC used.
 ```
 
-If a game is already running, the menu isn't there to answer `*t`, so `boot_bliptoaster()` gives
+(The boot starts with `[n8-host] USB host up (PIO-USB D+=GP2, D-=GP3). ...` and `[n8-host] node type rp.n8.nes
+(registered, not planned)`, the image naming the pack's node so the linker keeps it; E3 plans it.)
+
+If a game is already running, the menu isn't there to answer `*t`, so `boot_rom()` gives
 up after `N8_MENU_TRIES` (~48 s by default) and the bridge forwards MIDI to whatever runs.
 `midi_to_fifo()` forwards only channel-voice messages (`0x80-0xEF`), dropping clock / sensing /
 transport / aftertouch so they can't flood the FIFO; `sniff_report()` is read-only.
````

- [ ] **Step 12: Not runnable here: the Windows, macOS and arm64 runs that are owed**

E2's code has never met MSVC: the pack's targets and the device ABI's C test are ours, so they build under `/W4 /WX`,
and a Windows problem breaks `build.bat`'s plain build. On a Windows machine with this tree (the user's Windows
agent), run `build.bat` and then `test.bat` (all four suites), and report both. The risks: `DeviceAbi.c` compiled as C
by MSVC, with `rp_job_error`'s `static __inline` under MSVC's C; `__declspec(noinline)` on `writeBattery`;
`rfl::Bytestring` in the facet under the QuickJS codec; the local names MSVC's `/W4` refuses to let shadow (the stage
named `restored` and `uploaded` for that); `std::filesystem::canonical` in the port guard on a COM port name; the
serial lister and `SerialTransport` on Windows' serial API; and the test host's per-process scratch directory for its
n8.cfg. macOS (AppleClang with libc++) has not built E2 either: CI's macOS job builds `all`, so it compiles the pack's
portable and desktop targets and `retroplug-n8-device` with Apple clang and libc++ and links the serial library with
IOKit and CoreFoundation; the prototype's compilers were GCC 13 and the devcontainer's `arm-none-eabi-g++`. CI's arm64
Linux job (the same GCC 13) has not built it either, and the linux job's two new steps (the TinyUSB init with the
Pico-PIO-USB fetch at `5a37a66`, and `pnpm device:box`) have run only as Step 5's local `env -i` dry run, never on a
GitHub runner. `build.yml` runs on `workflow_dispatch`, on pull requests and on pushes to `main` only, so pushing
`feature/modularize` runs none of it: the CI runs are owed to a dispatched run or a PR, which the user (or their
Windows agent) starts. The acceptance records all of these as owed rather than passed: report them as such.
